sentences.zh: 志第二十三職官二

translations.literal: Treatise 23: Offices and Ranks 2
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 23, Offices and Ranks, Part 2

sentences.zh: =三師=

translations.literal: = The Three Preceptors =
translations.idiomatic: The Three Preceptors

sentences.zh: 太師、太傅、太保各一員。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector — one post each.
translations.idiomatic: There was one post each for the Grand Preceptor, the Grand Tutor, and the Grand Protector.

sentences.zh: 謂之三師，並正一品。

translations.literal: They are called the Three Preceptors, all of the senior first rank.
translations.idiomatic: These were called the Three Preceptors, all of the senior first rank.

sentences.zh: 後漢初，太傅置府僚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Later Han, the Grand Tutor was provided with staff for his office.
translations.idiomatic: In early Later Han, the Grand Tutor was assigned a staff for his office.

sentences.zh: 至周、隋，三師不置府僚，初拜於尚書省上。

translations.literal: By Zhou and Sui, the Three Preceptors had no office staff; at initial appointment they were invested at the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou and Sui, the Three Preceptors had no office staff; new appointees received their investiture at the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝廢三師之官。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui abolished the posts of the Three Preceptors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang of Sui abolished the offices of the Three Preceptors.

sentences.zh: 武德復置，一如隋制。

translations.literal: In Wude they were restored, exactly as under the Sui system.
translations.idiomatic: They were restored in the Wude era, following the Sui arrangement.

sentences.zh: 三師，訓導之官，天子所師法，大抵無所統職，然非道德崇重，則不居其位。

translations.literal: The Three Preceptors are officers of instruction and guidance whom the Son of Heaven takes as his models; for the most part they have no administrative duties, yet unless one's virtue and standing are exceptionally high, one does not hold these posts.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Preceptors were mentors whom the emperor was to emulate; they generally held no executive authority, and only those of exceptional moral stature were appointed.

sentences.zh: 無其人，則闕之。

translations.literal: When there is no suitable person, the posts remain vacant.
translations.idiomatic: When no one qualified, the posts were left unfilled.

sentences.zh: =三公=

translations.literal: = The Three Dukes =
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dukes

sentences.zh: 太尉、司徒、司空各一員。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works — one post each.
translations.idiomatic: There was one post each for the Grand Commandant, the Minister of Education, and the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 謂之三公，並正一品。

translations.literal: They are called the Three Dukes, all of the senior first rank.
translations.idiomatic: These were called the Three Dukes, all of the senior first rank.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉至北齊，三公置府僚。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin through Northern Qi, the Three Dukes had office staff.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wei and Jin through Northern Qi, each of the Three Dukes maintained an office staff.

sentences.zh: 隋初亦置府僚，尋省府僚，初拜於尚書省上，唐因之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui they also had office staff; soon the staff was cut, and at initial appointment they were invested at the Department of State Affairs — Tang followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Early Sui likewise provided office staff, but the staff was soon abolished; new appointees were invested at the Department of State Affairs, and the Tang continued the practice.

sentences.zh: 武德初，太宗為之，其後親王拜三公，皆不視事，祭祀則攝者行也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, the Prince of Qin held the post; thereafter when imperial princes received the Three Dukes, none actually administered affairs — at sacrifices a deputy performed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In early Wude, Prince Qin (the future Emperor Taizong) held one of these offices; thereafter when imperial princes were named to the Three Dukes they did not manage affairs, and at sacrifices a stand-in performed the ritual duties.

sentences.zh: 三公，論道之官也。

translations.literal: The Three Dukes are officers who discuss the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dukes were counsellors charged with deliberating on state policy.

sentences.zh: 蓋以佐天子理陰陽，平邦國，無所不統，故不以一職名其官。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking they assist the Son of Heaven in harmonizing yin and yang and settling the realm; there is nothing they do not oversee, hence their offices are not named for a single function.
translations.idiomatic: They were to assist the emperor in harmonizing cosmic order and governing the state; their charge was so broad that no single functional title could name the office.

sentences.zh: 大祭祀，則太尉亞獻，司徒奉俎，司空掃除。

translations.literal: At great sacrifices the Grand Commandant serves as secondary offerer, the Minister of Education presents the sacrificial tray, and the Minister of Works sweeps and cleans.
translations.idiomatic: At major sacrifices the Grand Commandant served as secondary offerer, the Minister of Education presented the meat tray, and the Minister of Works performed the sweeping and purification.

sentences.zh: =尚書省=

translations.literal: = Department of State Affairs =
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs

sentences.zh: 尚書都省龍朔二年，改為中台，光宅元年，改為文昌台，神龍初復。

translations.literal: The central office of the Department of State Affairs: in the second year of Longshuo it was renamed the Central Terrace; in the first year of Guangzhai, the Wenchang Terrace; at the beginning of Shenlong it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The central secretariat of the Department of State Affairs was renamed the Central Terrace in 662, the Wenchang Terrace in 689, and restored to its former name at the beginning of the Shenlong restoration (705).

sentences.zh: 尚書省領二十四司。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs oversees twenty-four bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs oversaw twenty-four bureaus.

sentences.zh: 六尚書，各分領四司。

translations.literal: The six ministers each oversee four bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: The six ministers each directed four bureaus.

sentences.zh: 尚書令尚書令一員。

translations.literal: Director of the Department — one post.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Department of State Affairs: one post.

sentences.zh: 正二品。

translations.literal: Senior second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Senior second rank.

sentences.zh: 武德中，太宗為之，自是闕而不置。

translations.literal: During Wude the Prince of Qin held it; from then on the post has remained vacant and unset.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude era Prince Qin held the post; thereafter it was left permanently vacant.

sentences.zh: 令總領百官，儀刑端揆。

translations.literal: The Director overall leads the hundred officials, setting the model and standard for the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Director was to oversee all officials and set the court's moral standard.

sentences.zh: 其屬有六尚書：一曰吏部，二曰戶部，三曰禮部，四曰兵部，五曰刑部，六曰工部。

translations.literal: His subordinates are the six ministers: first Personnel, second Revenue, third Rites, fourth War, fifth Justice, sixth Works.
translations.idiomatic: Under him were six ministers: Personnel, Revenue, Rites, War, Justice, and Works.

sentences.zh: 凡庶務，皆會而決之。

translations.literal: All routine affairs are convened and decided together.
translations.idiomatic: All routine business was brought together for collective decision.

sentences.zh: 尚書左右僕射左右僕射各一員，從二品。

translations.literal: Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department — one each, junior second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department: one post each, junior second rank.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改為左右匡，光宅元年，改為文昌左右相，開元元年，改為左右丞相，天寶元年，復為左右僕射。

translations.literal: Second year of Longshuo, renamed Left and Right Rectifiers; first year of Guangzhai, Wenchang Left and Right Chancellors; first year of Kaiyuan, Left and Right Chief Ministers; first year of Tianbao, restored as Left and Right Vice Directors.
translations.idiomatic: In 662 they became the Left and Right Rectifiers; in 689 the Wenchang Left and Right Chancellors; in 713 the Left and Right Chief Ministers; in 742 the titles reverted to Left and Right Vice Directors.

sentences.zh: 掌統理六官，綱紀庶務，以貳令之職。

translations.literal: They oversee and govern the six ministers, maintain the regulations for routine affairs, and serve as deputies to the Director.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised the six ministers, maintained administrative discipline, and served as the Director's deputies.

sentences.zh: 自不置令，僕射總判省事。

translations.literal: Since the Director post is not filled, the Vice Directors in chief judge the affairs of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: With no Director appointed, the Vice Directors in practice presided over the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 御史糾劾不當，兼得彈之。

translations.literal: When censors impeach improper conduct, they may also be subject to impeachment themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When the censors found impropriety they could also impeach the Vice Directors.

sentences.zh: 尚書左右丞左右丞各一員。

translations.literal: Left and Right Assistant Directors of the Department — one each.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Assistant Directors: one post each.

sentences.zh: 左丞，正四品上。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director, senior fourth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Assistant Director held senior fourth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 右丞，正四品下。

translations.literal: Right Assistant Director, senior fourth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Assistant Director held senior fourth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為左右肅機，咸亨復，永昌元年，升為從三品也，如意元年，復四品也。

translations.literal: Longshuo renamed them Left and Right Overseers of Protocol; Xianheng restored the old titles; first year of Yongchang promoted to junior third rank; first year of Ruyi restored to fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Longshuo reform they became the Left and Right Overseers of Protocol; the original titles returned in 670; in 689 they were raised to junior third rank; in 692 they reverted to fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 左丞掌管轄諸司，糾正省內，勾吏部、戶部、禮部十二司，通判都省事。

translations.literal: The Left Assistant Director supervises and governs the various bureaus, corrects matters within the secretariat, audits the twelve bureaus under Personnel, Revenue, and Rites, and jointly adjudicates central secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Assistant Director oversaw the various bureaus, supervised internal discipline, audited the twelve bureaus of Personnel, Revenue, and Rites, and shared adjudication of central secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 若右丞闕，則並行之。

translations.literal: If the Right Assistant Director's post is vacant, he handles both sides.
translations.idiomatic: If the Right Assistant Director's post was vacant, he handled both portfolios.

sentences.zh: 右丞管兵部、刑部、工部十二司。

translations.literal: The Right Assistant Director oversees the twelve bureaus of War, Justice, and Works.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Assistant Director oversaw the twelve bureaus under War, Justice, and Works.

sentences.zh: 若左闕，右丞兼知其事。

translations.literal: If the left post is vacant, the Right Assistant Director also manages those affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If the Left Assistant Director's post was vacant, the Right Assistant Director handled both sides.

sentences.zh: 御史有糾劾不當，兼得彈之。

translations.literal: When censors impeach improper conduct, they may also be subject to impeachment themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When the censors found impropriety they could also impeach the Assistant Directors.

sentences.zh: 左右司郎中左右司郎中各一員。

translations.literal: Left and Right Bureau Directors — one each.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Bureau Directors: one post each.

sentences.zh: 並從五品上。

translations.literal: Both junior fifth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Both held junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 隋置，武德初省。

translations.literal: Established under Sui; cut in early Wude.
translations.idiomatic: Established under the Sui; abolished in early Wude.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，復置。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, restored.
translations.idiomatic: Restored at the beginning of the Zhenguan era (627).

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改為左右丞務，咸亨復也。

translations.literal: Second year of Longshuo renamed Left and Right Assistant Duties; Xianheng restored the former title.
translations.idiomatic: In 662 they were renamed Left and Right Assistant Duties; the original title returned in 670.

sentences.zh: 左司郎中，副左丞所管諸司事，省署鈔目，勘稽失，知省內宿直之事。

translations.literal: The Left Bureau Director assists the Left Assistant Director in the affairs of the bureaus under his charge, compiles the secretariat's document registers, investigates errors and omissions, and attends to overnight duty in the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Bureau Director assisted the Left Assistant Director, maintained the secretariat document registers, investigated discrepancies, and managed overnight duty rotations.

sentences.zh: 若右司郎中闕，則並行之。

translations.literal: If the Right Bureau Director's post is vacant, he handles both.
translations.idiomatic: If the Right Bureau Director's post was vacant, he handled both sides.

sentences.zh: 左右司員外郎各一員。

translations.literal: Left and Right Bureau Assistant Directors — one each.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Bureau Assistant Directors: one post each.

sentences.zh: 天后永昌元年，置左右司員外郎各一人。

translations.literal: First year of Yongchang under the Empress, established one Left and one Right Bureau Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: In 689 the Empress established one Left and one Right Bureau Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 神龍初省，後復置。

translations.literal: Cut at the beginning of Shenlong; later restored.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished at the beginning of the Shenlong restoration; later reinstated.

sentences.zh: 左右司郎中、員外郎各掌副十有二司之事，以舉正稽違，省署符目焉。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Bureau Directors and Assistant Directors each assist in the affairs of the twelve bureaus, to promote correctness and audit violations, and maintain the secretariat's document tallies.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau Directors and Assistant Directors each assisted the twelve bureaus, enforced compliance, audited violations, and maintained the secretariat's document tallies.

sentences.zh: 凡都省掌舉諸司之綱紀與百僚之程式，以正邦理，以宣邦教。

translations.literal: Broadly, the central secretariat oversees the regulations of all bureaus and the protocols of all officials, to rectify state governance and disseminate state instruction.
translations.idiomatic: In general the central secretariat upheld the regulations governing all bureaus and the protocols for officials, to maintain sound governance and disseminate state policy.

sentences.zh: 凡上之所以迨下，其制有六，曰制、敕、冊、令、教、符。

translations.literal: For communications from above reaching below, there are six forms: ordinance, edict, investiture document, order, instruction, and dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Communications from superior to subordinate took six forms: ordinances, edicts, investiture documents, orders, instructions, and dispatches.

sentences.zh: 天子曰制，曰敕，曰冊。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven issues ordinances, edicts, and investiture documents.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued ordinances, edicts, and investiture documents.

sentences.zh: 皇太子曰令。

translations.literal: The heir apparent issues orders.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince issued orders.

sentences.zh: 親王、公主曰教。

translations.literal: Imperial princes and princesses issue instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes and princesses issued instructions.

sentences.zh: 尚書省下於州，州下縣，縣下鄉，皆曰符也。

translations.literal: From the Department down to the prefecture, prefecture to county, county to township — all are called dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: Communications from the Department to prefectures, prefectures to counties, and counties to townships were all called dispatches.

sentences.zh: 凡下之所以達上，其制亦有六，曰表、狀、箋、啟、辭、牒。

translations.literal: For communications from below reaching above, there are also six forms: memorial, report, letter of petition, report to superior, commoner's petition, and official document.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate communications upward also took six forms: memorials, reports, formal letters, personal communications, commoners' petitions, and official documents.

sentences.zh: 表上于天子。

translations.literal: Memorials are submitted to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials were addressed to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 其近臣亦為狀。

translations.literal: His close ministers also use reports.
translations.idiomatic: Close ministers could also submit reports.

sentences.zh: 箋、啟上皇太子，然于其長亦為之，非公文所施。

translations.literal: Letters of petition and personal reports are addressed to the heir apparent; yet one may also use them toward one's elders — they are not forms for official documents.
translations.idiomatic: Formal letters and personal communications were directed to the crown prince, though they could also be used toward one's seniors; they were not standard administrative forms.

sentences.zh: 有品已上公文，皆曰牒。

translations.literal: Official documents of all those with rank and above are called documents.
translations.idiomatic: Official paperwork by all ranked officials was called a dispatch document.

sentences.zh: 庶人言曰辭也。

translations.literal: Commoners' communications are called petitions.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners submitted petitions.

sentences.zh: 諸司自相質問，其義有三：關、刺、移。

translations.literal: When bureaus question one another, there are three forms: notification, impeachment report, and transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Inter-bureau inquiries took three forms: notifications, impeachment reports, and transfers.

sentences.zh: 關，謂關通其事；

translations.literal: Notification — meaning to notify and communicate the matter;
translations.idiomatic: A notification meant communicating a matter for coordination;

sentences.zh: 刺，謂刺舉之；

translations.literal: Impeachment report — meaning to impeach and expose;
translations.idiomatic: an impeachment report meant exposing misconduct;

sentences.zh: 移，謂移其事于他司。

translations.literal: Transfer — meaning to transfer the matter to another bureau.
translations.idiomatic: and a transfer meant shifting a matter to another bureau.

sentences.zh: 移則通判之官皆連署也。

translations.literal: For transfers, all officials with joint jurisdiction must co-sign.
translations.idiomatic: Transfers required co-signature by all officials with joint jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 凡內外百司所受之事，皆印其發日，為之程限。

translations.literal: All matters received by bureaus inside and outside the capital are stamped with the date of issue and given deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: Every matter received by capital and provincial bureaus was date-stamped at issuance and assigned a deadline.

sentences.zh: 凡尚書省施行制敕，案成則給程以鈔之。

translations.literal: All ordinances and edicts implemented by the Department — when the case is completed, a deadline is given and recorded in the register.
translations.idiomatic: When the Department implemented imperial ordinances and edicts, a processing deadline was set and recorded once the dossier was complete.

sentences.zh: 若急速者，不出其日。

translations.literal: If urgent, it is not held beyond that day.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent matters had to be completed the same day.

sentences.zh: 若諸州計奏達于京師，量事之大小與多少，以為之節。

translations.literal: For statistical reports from the prefectures reaching the capital, deadlines are set according to the size and volume of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Deadlines for prefectural statistical reports reaching the capital varied with the scope and volume of the business.

sentences.zh: 凡京師諸司，有符、移、關、牒下諸州者，必由於都省以遣之。

translations.literal: Whenever capital bureaus issue dispatches, transfers, notifications, or documents down to the prefectures, they must pass through the central secretariat for transmission.
translations.idiomatic: When capital bureaus sent dispatches, transfers, notifications, or documents to the prefectures, transmission had to go through the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 凡文案既成，勾司行硃施訖，皆書其上端，記年月日，納諸庫。

translations.literal: When documents are completed, the auditing office applies the vermilion seal; all are inscribed at the top with the year, month, and day, then filed in the archive.
translations.idiomatic: Completed documents were sealed in vermilion by the auditing office, inscribed at the top with the date, and filed in the archive.

sentences.zh: 凡施行公文應印者，監印之官考其事目無差，然後印之，必書於曆。

translations.literal: For all implementing documents requiring seals, the seal-monitoring officer verifies that the subject matter is without discrepancy, then applies the seal; this must be recorded in the ledger.
translations.idiomatic: For documents requiring official seals, the seal officer verified that the contents matched before sealing, and every use was logged.

sentences.zh: 每月終納諸庫。

translations.literal: At each month's end they are submitted to the archive.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end the records were deposited in the archive.

sentences.zh: 凡尚書省官，每日一人宿直。

translations.literal: Among Department officials, one person each day holds overnight duty.
translations.idiomatic: One Department official each day held overnight duty.

sentences.zh: 都司報廢直簿，轉以為次。

translations.literal: The central office reports to retire the duty roster and rotates the turn.
translations.idiomatic: The central office updated the duty roster and rotated assignments.

sentences.zh: 凡內外百僚，日出而視事，既午而退，有事則直官省之。

translations.literal: All officials inside and outside, at sunrise they attend to affairs, after noon they withdraw; if there is business the duty officer handles it in the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Officials throughout the empire reported at dawn and withdrew at noon; after hours the duty officer handled affairs.

sentences.zh: 其務繁，不在此例。

translations.literal: Where duties are heavy, this rule does not apply.
translations.idiomatic: Offices with heavy workloads were exempt from this rule.

sentences.zh: 凡天下制敕計奏之數。

translations.literal: Broadly, the number of ordinances, edicts, and statistical reports throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The volume of imperial ordinances, edicts, and statistical reports nationwide.

sentences.zh: 省符宣告之節，率以歲終為斷。

translations.literal: The deadlines for secretariat dispatches and proclamations — as a rule the year-end is the cutoff.
translations.idiomatic: Deadlines for secretariat dispatches and proclamations typically ran to year-end.

sentences.zh: 京師諸司，皆以四月一日納於都省。

translations.literal: Capital bureaus all submit on the first day of the fourth month to the central secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Capital bureaus submitted their returns to the central secretariat on the first day of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 其天下諸州，則本司推校，以授勾官。

translations.literal: For prefectures throughout the realm, their home bureau verifies and forwards to the auditing officer.
translations.idiomatic: For prefectures, the supervising bureau verified the figures and forwarded them to the auditing officer.

sentences.zh: 勾官審之。

translations.literal: The auditing officer reviews them.
translations.idiomatic: The auditing officer reviewed them.

sentences.zh: 連署封印，附計帳，使納於都省。

translations.literal: Co-signed and sealed, attached to the statistical account, and sent for submission to the central secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After joint signature and sealing, they were attached to the statistical ledger and forwarded to the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 常以六月一日，都事集諸司令史對覆。

translations.literal: Regularly on the first day of the sixth month the central registrar convenes the clerks of all bureaus for cross-checking.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month the central registrar convened all bureau clerks for cross-verification.

sentences.zh: 若有隱漏不同，皆附於考課焉。

translations.literal: If there is concealment, omission, or discrepancy, all are attached to the merit evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Concealment, omission, or discrepancy was recorded in merit evaluations.

sentences.zh: 主事主事六人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Chief clerks — six persons, junior ninth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks: six posts, junior ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史十八人，書令史三十六人，亭長六人，掌固十四人。

translations.literal: Document clerks eighteen, writing clerks thirty-six, ward captains six, custodians fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: There were eighteen document clerks, thirty-six writing clerks, six ward captains, and fourteen custodians.

sentences.zh: 凡令史掌案文簿，亭長、掌固檢校省門戶倉庫廳事陳設之事也。

translations.literal: Document clerks manage case documents and registers; ward captains and custodians inspect the secretariat gates, storehouses, reception halls, and furnishings.
translations.idiomatic: Document clerks maintained dossiers and registers; ward captains and custodians inspected the gates, storehouses, halls, and furnishings.

sentences.zh: 吏部吏部尚書吏部尚書一員，正三品。

translations.literal: Ministry of Personnel — Minister of Personnel — one post, senior third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Personnel. Minister of Personnel: one post, senior third rank.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改為司列太常伯，光宅元年，改為天官尚書，神龍復為吏部尚書也。

translations.literal: Second year of Longshuo renamed Director of Appointments and Grand Master of Splendor; first year of Guangzhai, Heavenly Offices Minister; Shenlong restored as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 662 the title became Director of Appointments and Grand Master of Splendor; in 689 Heavenly Offices Minister; after the Shenlong restoration (705) it reverted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 侍郎二員。

translations.literal: Vice ministers — two posts.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Ministers: two posts.

sentences.zh: 正四品上。

translations.literal: Senior fourth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Senior fourth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝大業三年，尚書六曹，各置侍郎一人，以貳尚書之職，並正四品。

translations.literal: Third year of Daye under Emperor Yang of Sui, for the six sections of the Department each established one Vice Minister to assist the Minister, all senior fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 607 Emperor Yang assigned one Vice Minister to each of the six ministries to assist the minister, all at senior fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 國家定令，諸曹侍郎降為正四品下，唯吏部侍郎為正四品上。

translations.literal: When the state fixed its code, Vice Ministers of all sections were lowered to senior fourth rank lower grade; only the Vice Minister of Personnel remained senior fourth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang code, Vice Ministers of all ministries were set at senior fourth rank, lower grade, except the Vice Minister of Personnel, who remained at senior fourth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為司列少常伯，咸亨復。

translations.literal: Longshuo renamed Junior Director of Appointments and Vice Grand Master of Splendor; Xianheng restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Longshuo reform the title became Junior Director of Appointments and Vice Grand Master of Splendor; it was restored in 670.

sentences.zh: 總章元年，吏部、兵部各增置侍郎一員也。

translations.literal: First year of Zongzhang, Personnel and War each added one Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In 668 one additional Vice Minister was added to both Personnel and War.

sentences.zh: 尚書、侍郎之職，掌天下官吏選授、勳封、考課之政令。

translations.literal: The duties of the Minister and Vice Ministers are to administer the policies for selecting, appointing, enfeoffing, and evaluating officials throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister and Vice Ministers administered policies for appointing officials, granting enfeoffments, and conducting merit evaluations empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 其屬有四：一曰吏部，二曰司封，三曰司勳，四曰考功。

translations.literal: Their subordinates are four: first Personnel, second Enfeoffments, third Meritorious Service, fourth Merit Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised four bureaus: Personnel, Enfeoffments, Meritorious Service, and Merit Evaluation.

sentences.zh: 總其職務，而行其制命。

translations.literal: They gather their respective duties and carry out the issued regulations.
translations.idiomatic: They coordinated bureau duties and implemented issued regulations.

sentences.zh: 凡中外百司之事，由於所屬，皆質正焉。

translations.literal: All matters of the hundred bureaus inside and outside pass through their jurisdiction and are verified for correctness.
translations.idiomatic: All capital and provincial bureau business under their jurisdiction was verified for correctness.

sentences.zh: 凡選授之制，每歲集于孟冬。

translations.literal: The system for selection and appointment gathers each year in the first month of winter.
translations.idiomatic: The annual selection and appointment cycle convened in the first month of winter.

sentences.zh: 去王城五百里之內以上旬，千里之內以中旬，千里之外以下旬。

translations.literal: Within five hundred li of the capital, the first ten-day period; within a thousand li, the middle ten-day period; beyond a thousand li, the last ten-day period.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates within five hundred li reported in the first ten-day period; within a thousand li, the middle period; beyond a thousand li, the last period.

sentences.zh: 尚書、侍郎，分為三銓。

translations.literal: The Minister and Vice Ministers divide into three selection boards.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister and Vice Ministers divided selection into three boards.

sentences.zh: 尚書為尚書銓，侍郎二人分為中銓、東銓也。

translations.literal: The Minister heads the Minister's Board; the two Vice Ministers divide into the Central Board and Eastern Board.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister chaired the Minister's Board; the two Vice Ministers headed the Central Board and Eastern Board.

sentences.zh: 凡擇人以四才，校功以三實。

translations.literal: In selecting men, use the four talents; in evaluating merit, use the three realities.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates were assessed by four talents and three measures of actual achievement.

sentences.zh: 四才，謂身、言、書、判。

translations.literal: The four talents are physique, speech, calligraphy, and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The four talents were physique, speech, calligraphy, and judgment.

sentences.zh: 其優長者，有可取焉。

translations.literal: Whoever excels in these has something to be drawn upon.
translations.idiomatic: Those who excelled in any of these had merit to draw upon.

sentences.zh: 三實，謂德行、才用、勞效，德均以才，才均以勞，勞必考其實而進退之。

translations.literal: The three realities are virtue and conduct, talent and employment, and labor and effect; virtue is balanced against talent, talent against labor, and labor must be examined for its reality before advancement or demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The three realities were virtue and conduct, talent and employment, and labor and effect; virtue was weighed against talent, talent against labor, and labor had to be verified before promotion or demotion.

sentences.zh: 較之優劣，而定其留放，所以正權衡，明與奪，抑貪冒，進賢能，然後據其官資，量其注擬。

translations.literal: Comparing superiority and inferiority, deciding retention or dismissal — thereby to set the balance, clarify grant and denial, suppress greed and usurpation, and advance the worthy and able; then according to their official qualifications, measure their proposed appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing candidates' merits determined retention or dismissal, set the balance of appointments, curbed corruption, advanced the capable, and then matched qualifications to proposed posts.

sentences.zh: 五品已上，以名上中書門下，聽制授其官。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above — submit names to the Chancellery and Secretariat, and await imperial appointment to office.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above: names went to the Chancellery and Secretariat for imperial appointment.

sentences.zh: 六品已下，量資任定。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below — measure qualifications and duties to fix appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank and below: appointments were fixed by qualifications and duties.

sentences.zh: 其才職頗高，可擢為拾遣、補闕、監察御史者，亦以名送中書門下，聽敕授。

translations.literal: Those whose talent and office are quite high and may be promoted to Remonstrator, Supplementation Censor, or Investigating Censor — also submit names to the Chancellery and Secretariat and await edict appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Those of notable talent eligible for remonstrator, supplementation censor, or investigating censor also had names sent to the Chancellery and Secretariat for edict appointment.

sentences.zh: 其有曆職清要，考第頗深者，得隔品授之，不然即否。

translations.literal: Those who have held clear and important posts with deep evaluation grades may receive appointment across rank levels; otherwise not.
translations.idiomatic: Those with distinguished service records and high evaluation grades could receive cross-rank appointments; otherwise not.

sentences.zh: 凡出身非清流者，不注清資官。

translations.literal: All those whose origins are not from the pure stream may not be assigned to pure-stream posts.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates not of pure-stream origin could not be assigned to pure-stream offices.

sentences.zh: 凡注官，若官資未相當，及以為非便者，聽至三注。

translations.literal: For all appointment assignments, if qualifications do not match the post or it is deemed unsuitable, up to three assignments are permitted.
translations.idiomatic: If qualifications did not match a post or the assignment was unsuitable, up to three alternative assignments were permitted.

sentences.zh: 凡伎術之官，皆本司定，送吏部附甲。

translations.literal: All technical-skill officials are fixed by their home bureau and sent to Personnel to attach to the roster.
translations.idiomatic: Technical officials were designated by their home bureau and registered with Personnel.

sentences.zh: 凡同司聯事勾檢之官，皆不得注大功已上親。

translations.literal: All officials in the same bureau who jointly audit matters may not be assigned relatives within the greater mourning circle.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in the same bureau who jointly audited matters could not be assigned relatives within the greater mourning circle.

sentences.zh: 凡皇親諸親及軍功，兼注員外郎。

translations.literal: All imperial kin, related kin, and military merit holders may concurrently be assigned as bureau assistant directors.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kin, related kin, and military merit holders could also be assigned as bureau assistant directors.

sentences.zh: 凡注擬，必先具官階團甲，送門下以聞。

translations.literal: For all proposed appointments, rank registers and selection rosters must first be prepared and sent to the Secretariat for report.
translations.idiomatic: Proposed appointments required rank registers and selection rosters sent to the Secretariat first.

sentences.zh: 注官，階高擬卑曰「行」，階卑擬高曰「守」。

translations.literal: For appointment assignment, when rank is high and proposed post low it is called 'acting'; when rank is low and proposed post high it is called 'holding'.
translations.idiomatic: When rank exceeded the proposed post the assignment was marked 'acting'; when rank fell short it was marked 'holding'.

sentences.zh: 三銓注擬訖，皆當銓團甲，過左右僕射。

translations.literal: When the three boards finish proposed appointments, each board's roster passes the Left and Right Vice Directors.
translations.idiomatic: When the three boards finished, each board's roster passed the Left and Right Vice Directors.

sentences.zh: 若中銓、東銓，則過尚書訖，乃上門下省。

translations.literal: For the Central and Eastern Boards, after passing the Minister they go up to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Central and Eastern Board rosters passed the Minister before going to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 給事中讀，黃門侍郎省，侍中審，然後進甲以聞，聽旨授而施行焉。

translations.literal: The Supervising Secretary reads, the Vice Chamberlain of the Yellow Gate reviews, the Attendant-in-Chief examines, then the roster is submitted for report; upon receiving the decree, appointment is carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary read, the vice chamberlain reviewed, the attendant-in-chief examined, then the roster was submitted; upon imperial approval appointments were issued.

sentences.zh: 若左右僕射門下批官不當者，別改注，亦有重執而上者也。

translations.literal: If the Left and Right Vice Directors or Secretariat reject an appointment as improper, it is reassigned; there are also cases of resubmission after rejection.
translations.idiomatic: If the Vice Directors or Secretariat rejected an appointment, it was reassigned; some cases were resubmitted after rejection.

sentences.zh: 凡大選，終於季春之月，若選人有身在軍旅，則軍中試書判，封送吏部。

translations.literal: The great selection ends in the last month of spring; if a candidate is in military service, the army tests calligraphy and judgment and seals the results to send to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The great selection ended in late spring; candidates in military service took calligraphy and judgment tests in the army, sealed and sent to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 亦有春中下解而後集，謂之春選。

translations.literal: There are also those who submit credentials in spring and assemble later — called the spring selection.
translations.idiomatic: Some submitted credentials in spring and assembled later, called the spring selection.

sentences.zh: 若優勞人，有敕則有處分及即與官者，並聽非時選，一百日內注擬之。

translations.literal: For those of outstanding merit with an edict granting disposition or immediate office, non-scheduled selection is permitted — appointment within one hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Those of outstanding merit with edicts for immediate appointment could be selected off-cycle within one hundred days.

sentences.zh: 所以定九流之品格，補萬方之闕政，官人之道備焉。

translations.literal: Thus to fix the grades of the nine streams and remedy the realm's administrative gaps — the way of managing officials is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the nine streams of rank were fixed and administrative gaps remedied — the system for managing officials was complete.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎中郎中二員，並從五品上。

translations.literal: Personnel Bureau Director — two posts, junior fifth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel Bureau Directors: two posts, junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司列大夫，咸亨、光宅並隋曹改也。

translations.literal: Longshuo as Director of Appointments Grandee; Xianheng and Guangzhai both followed the Sui bureau title.
translations.idiomatic: Under Longshuo, Director of Appointments Grandee; Xianheng and Guangzhai followed Sui titles.

sentences.zh: 員外郎二員。

translations.literal: Bureau Assistant Directors — two posts.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Assistant Directors: two posts.

sentences.zh: 並從六品上。

translations.literal: Both junior sixth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Both junior sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史三十人，書令史六十人，亭長八人，掌固十二人。

translations.literal: Document clerks thirty, writing clerks sixty, ward captains eight, custodians twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty document clerks, sixty writing clerks, eight ward captains, and twelve custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中一人，掌考天下文吏之班秩階品。

translations.literal: One Director oversees evaluating the ranks and grades of all civil officials in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: One Director managed the ranks and grades of all civil officials empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 凡敘階二十有九，品在都序，自一品至九品，品有上下，凡散官四品已下，九品已上，並於吏部當番上下。

translations.literal: For rank sequence there are twenty-nine grades; ranks are ordered in sequence from senior first to ninth, each with upper and lower; all honorary officials from fourth rank down and ninth rank up rotate duty at Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Rank sequence comprised twenty-nine grades from senior first through ninth, each with upper and lower subdivisions; honorary officials from fourth rank down and ninth rank up rotated duty at Personnel.

sentences.zh: 其應當番四十五日。

translations.literal: Those on rotation serve forty-five days.
translations.idiomatic: Rotation duty lasted forty-five days.

sentences.zh: 若都省須人送符，諸司須人者，並兵部、吏部散官上。

translations.literal: If the central secretariat needs messengers or bureaus need personnel, War and Personnel honorary officials are assigned.
translations.idiomatic: When the central secretariat or bureaus needed personnel, honorary officials from War and Personnel were assigned.

sentences.zh: 經兩番已上，聽簡入選。

translations.literal: After two rotations or more, they may be selected for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After two or more rotations they could enter selection.

sentences.zh: 不第者，依番名不過五六也。

translations.literal: Those who fail are listed by rotation name, not exceeding five or six times.
translations.idiomatic: Failures were listed by rotation, not exceeding five or six cycles.

sentences.zh: 凡敘階之法，有以封爵，有以親戚，有以勳庸，有以資廕，有以秀孝，有以勞考，有除免而復敘者，皆循法以申之，無或枉冒。

translations.literal: The method for rank sequence: by enfeoffment, by imperial kin, by meritorious service, by inherited privilege, by filial piety and integrity, by labor and evaluation, or restoration after dismissal — all follow the law to apply; none may falsely usurp.
translations.idiomatic: Rank sequence could derive from enfeoffment, imperial kinship, merit, inherited privilege, filial piety recommendations, labor evaluations, or restoration after dismissal — all per statute, with no false claims.

sentences.zh: 凡應入三品五品者，皆待別制而進之，不然則否。

translations.literal: All who should enter third or fifth rank await special edict for advancement; otherwise not.
translations.idiomatic: Advancement to third or fifth rank required special edict; otherwise not.

sentences.zh: 凡文武百僚之班序，官同者先爵，爵同者先齒。

translations.literal: For the sequence of all civil and military officials, when office is equal precedence goes to enfeoffment; when enfeoffment is equal, to age.
translations.idiomatic: When office was equal, enfeoffment took precedence; when enfeoffment was equal, age did.

sentences.zh: 凡京司有常參官、謂五品以上職事官、八品已上供奉官、員外郎、監察御史、太常博士。

translations.literal: For capital bureaus there are regular attendees: meaning fifth rank and above functional officials, eighth rank and above attendance officials, bureau assistant directors, investigating censors, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Capital regular attendees included fifth-rank functional officials and above, eighth-rank attendance officials and above, bureau assistant directors, investigating censors, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians.

sentences.zh: 供奉官、兩省自侍中、中書令已下，盡名供奉官。

translations.literal: Attendance officials — from the two departments, from Attendant-in-Chief and Secretariat Director down, all are called attendance officials.
translations.idiomatic: Attendance officials: from the two departments, from Attendant-in-Chief and Secretariat Director downward, all were attendance officials.

sentences.zh: 諸司長官、清望官、四品已下八品已上清官。

translations.literal: Bureau chiefs, clear-expectation officials, and clear officials from fourth rank down to eighth rank up.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau chiefs, clear-expectation officials, and clear officials from fourth rank down through eighth rank up.

sentences.zh: 每日以六品已上清官兩人，待制於衙。

translations.literal: Daily two clear officials of sixth rank and above wait on duty at the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Daily, two sixth-rank clear officials waited on duty at court.

sentences.zh: 供奉官、宿衛官不在此例。

translations.literal: Attendance officials and guard officials are not in this category.
translations.idiomatic: Attendance and guard officials were exempt.

sentences.zh: 凡授四品已下清望官，才職相當，不應進讓。

translations.literal: For all appointments to clear-expectation offices of fourth rank and below, talent and office must match; advancement without demurral is not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-expectation appointments of fourth rank and below required matching talent and office; improper advancement was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 凡職事官應覲省及移疾，不得過程。

translations.literal: Functional officials attending court and reporting illness may not exceed the permitted period.
translations.idiomatic: Functional officials on court attendance or sick leave could not exceed permitted periods.

sentences.zh: 年七十已上應致仕，若齒力未衰，亦聽厘務。

translations.literal: At age seventy and above one should retire; if vigor has not declined, one may still hear limited matters.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy officials should retire; if still vigorous they could handle limited duties.

sentences.zh: 凡官人身及同居大功已上親，自執工商，家專其業，及風疾、使酒，皆不得入仕。

translations.literal: Any official whose person or co-resident relatives within the greater mourning circle practice crafts or commerce as their household profession, or who have wind illness or abuse wine, may not enter office.
translations.idiomatic: Officials or co-resident relatives within the greater mourning circle engaged in crafts or commerce, or those with chronic illness or alcohol abuse, could not enter office.

sentences.zh: 凡內外官有清白著聞，應以名薦，則中書門下改授，五品已上，量加升進，六品已下，有付吏部即量等第遷轉。

translations.literal: All inside and outside officials of clear repute recommended by name — the Chancellery and Secretariat reassign; fifth rank and above receive measured promotion; sixth rank and below Personnel immediately measures grade for transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of clear repute were recommended by name; fifth rank and above received measured promotion through the Chancellery; sixth rank and below Personnel graded for transfer.

sentences.zh: 若第二第三等人，五品已上，改日稍優之。

translations.literal: For second and third grade persons, fifth rank and above receive slightly preferential dates.
translations.idiomatic: Second- and third-grade recommendees of fifth rank and above received slightly preferential appointment dates.

sentences.zh: 六品已下，秩滿聽選，不在放限。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below, when term expires may enter selection, not subject to dismissal limits.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank and below could enter selection when terms expired, without dismissal limits.

sentences.zh: 其嶺南、黔中，三年一置選補使，號為南選。

translations.literal: For Lingnan and Qianzhong, every three years a selection supplement commissioner is established, called the southern selection.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan and Qianzhong held a southern selection every three years via a supplement commissioner.

sentences.zh: 凡天下官吏，各有常員。

translations.literal: All officials throughout the realm each have fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: All officials empire-wide had fixed establishment quotas.

sentences.zh: 凡諸司置直，皆有定數。

translations.literal: All bureaus establishing rotation duty have fixed numbers.
translations.idiomatic: All bureaus had fixed rotation duty numbers.

sentences.zh: 諸司諸色有品直官。

translations.literal: All bureaus and categories have ranked rotation officials.
translations.idiomatic: All bureaus had ranked rotation officials.

sentences.zh: 內外官吏，則有假寧之節，行李之命。

translations.literal: Inside and outside officials have leave regulations and travel orders.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside officials had leave regulations and travel orders.

sentences.zh: 簿書景跡，功賞殿最，具員皆與員外郎分掌之。

translations.literal: Registers, records, merit rewards, and evaluation grades — full quotas are all divided among the bureau assistant directors.
translations.idiomatic: Registers, records, merit rewards, and evaluation grades were divided among bureau assistant directors.

sentences.zh: 郎中一人掌小銓，亦分為九品，通謂之行署。

translations.literal: One Director manages the minor selection, also divided into nine grades, collectively called the acting office.
translations.idiomatic: One Director managed minor selection, also nine grades, called the acting office.

sentences.zh: 以其在九流之外，故謂之流外銓，亦謂之小選。

translations.literal: Because they are outside the nine streams, they are called the outside-stream selection, also called the minor selection.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the nine streams, this was the outside-stream selection, also called minor selection.

sentences.zh: 其校試銓注，與流內銓略同。

translations.literal: Their examination, selection, and appointment are broadly the same as the inside-stream selection.
translations.idiomatic: Examination and appointment procedures broadly matched inside-stream selection.

sentences.zh: 其吏部、兵部、禮部、考功、都省、御史台、中書、門下，謂之前八司，其餘則曰後行。

translations.literal: Personnel, War, Rites, Merit Evaluation, central secretariat, Censorate, Secretariat, and Chancellery are called the front eight bureaus; the rest are called the rear acting offices.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel, War, Rites, Merit Evaluation, central secretariat, Censorate, Secretariat, and Chancellery were the front eight bureaus; the rest were rear acting offices.

sentences.zh: 凡擇流外，取工書、計，兼頗曉時務。

translations.literal: In selecting outside-stream candidates, require skill in writing and calculation, and some familiarity with current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Outside-stream candidates required writing and calculation skills plus familiarity with current affairs.

sentences.zh: 三事中，有一優長，則在敘限。

translations.literal: If one of the three matters is outstanding, they are within the promotion period.
translations.idiomatic: Excellence in one of three areas placed them within the promotion period.

sentences.zh: 每經三考轉選，量其才能而進之，不則從舊任。

translations.literal: Every three evaluations lead to transfer selection; measure ability to advance; otherwise retain former post.
translations.idiomatic: Every three evaluations triggered transfer selection by ability; otherwise the former post was retained.

sentences.zh: 小銓，舊委郎中專知。

translations.literal: Minor selection was formerly entrusted solely to the Director.
translations.idiomatic: Minor selection was formerly managed solely by the Director.

sentences.zh: 開元二十五年，又敕銓試訖留放，皆尚書侍郎定之也。

translations.literal: Twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan, an edict also ordered that after examination and retention or dismissal, the Minister and Vice Ministers would decide.
translations.idiomatic: In 737 an edict ordered that after examination, retention and dismissal were decided by the Minister and Vice Ministers.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一人掌判南曹。

translations.literal: One Bureau Assistant Director adjudicates the Southern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: One Bureau Assistant Director adjudicated the Southern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 曹在選曹之南，故謂之南曹。

translations.literal: The bureau lies south of the selection bureau, hence called the Southern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau lay south of the selection bureau, hence the Southern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 每歲選人，有解狀、簿書、資歷、考課，必由之以核其實，乃上三銓。

translations.literal: Each year's candidates have credentials, registers, qualifications, and evaluations — all must pass through it to verify reality before going to the three boards.
translations.idiomatic: Annual candidates' credentials, registers, qualifications, and evaluations passed through it for verification before the three boards.

sentences.zh: 其三銓進甲則署焉。

translations.literal: When the three boards submit rosters, they are signed there.
translations.idiomatic: The three boards' rosters were signed there.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一人裳判曹務。

translations.literal: One Bureau Assistant Director handles bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Bureau Assistant Director handled bureau affairs.

sentences.zh: 凡預太廟齋郎帖試，如貢舉之制。

translations.literal: All who participate in the Imperial Temple Acolyte credential test follow the metropolitan examination system.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Temple Acolyte credential tests followed the metropolitan examination system.

sentences.zh: 司封郎中司封郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Enfeoffments Bureau Director — one post, junior fifth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffments Bureau Director: one post, junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 隋曰主爵郎，武德因之。

translations.literal: Under Sui called Master of Enfeoffments Director; Wude followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, Master of Enfeoffments Director; Wude followed.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年改為司封大夫，光宅改司封郎中也。

translations.literal: Second year of Longshuo renamed Enfeoffments Grandee; Guangzhai changed to Enfeoffments Director.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed it Enfeoffments Grandee; Guangzhai changed to Enfeoffments Director.

sentences.zh: 司封員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Enfeoffments Bureau Assistant Director — one post, junior sixth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffments Bureau Assistant Director: one post, junior sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Chief clerks two, junior ninth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks: two, junior ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史四人，書令史九人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Document clerks four, writing clerks nine, custodians four.
translations.idiomatic: Four document clerks, nine writing clerks, four custodians.

sentences.zh: 司封郎中、員外郎之職，掌國之封爵，凡有九等。

translations.literal: The Enfeoffments Director and Assistant Director administer the state's enfeoffments; there are nine grades.
translations.idiomatic: The Enfeoffments Director and Assistant Director administered state enfeoffments, of which there were nine grades.

sentences.zh: 一曰王，正一品，食邑一萬戶。

translations.literal: First, King, senior first rank, fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: First, King: senior first rank, fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 二曰郡王，從一品，食邑五千戶。

translations.literal: Second, Commandery Prince, junior first rank, fief of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Second, Commandery Prince: junior first rank, fief of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 三曰國公，從一品，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: Third, State Duke, junior first rank, fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Third, State Duke: junior first rank, fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 四曰郡公，正二品，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: Fourth, Commandery Duke, senior second rank, fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, Commandery Duke: senior second rank, fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 五曰縣公，從二品，食邑一千五百戶。

translations.literal: Fifth, County Duke, junior second rank, fief of fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, County Duke: junior second rank, fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 六曰縣侯，從三品，食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Sixth, County Marquis, junior third rank, fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, County Marquis: junior third rank, fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 七曰縣伯，正四品，食邑七進戶。

translations.literal: Seventh, County Earl, senior fourth rank, fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, County Earl: senior fourth rank, fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 八曰縣子，正五品，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Eighth, County Viscount, senior fifth rank, fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, County Viscount: senior fifth rank, fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 九曰縣男，從五品，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Ninth, County Baron, junior fifth rank, fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, County Baron: junior fifth rank, fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 凡名山大川，及畿內諸縣，皆不以封。

translations.literal: All famous mountains, great rivers, and counties within the capital region may not be enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Famous mountains, great rivers, and capital-region counties could not be enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 至郡公有餘爵，聽回授子孫。

translations.literal: For commandery dukes with surplus enfeoffments, they may be transferred back to descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery dukes with surplus enfeoffments could transfer them to descendants.

sentences.zh: 其國公皆特封。

translations.literal: All state dukes are specially enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: All state dukes received special enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 凡天下觀有定數。

translations.literal: Broadly, all shrines throughout the realm have fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: All Daoist shrines empire-wide had fixed establishment quotas.

sentences.zh: 每觀立三綱，以道德高者充。

translations.literal: Each shrine establishes three directors, filled by those of high moral virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Each shrine appointed three directors, filled by those of highest moral virtue.

sentences.zh: 凡三元諸齋日，修金錄、明真等齋。

translations.literal: On all three-principle yuan festival fast days, Golden Register, Bright Truth, and similar fasts are performed.
translations.idiomatic: On three-principle yuan fast days, Golden Register, Bright Truth, and similar rites were performed.

sentences.zh: 凡道士、女道士簿籍，三年一造。

translations.literal: Registers of Daoist priests and priestesses are compiled every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist priest and priestess registers were compiled every three years.

sentences.zh: 凡外命婦之制，皇之姑，封大長公主，皇姊妹，封長公主，皇女，封公主，皆視正一品。

translations.literal: For external titled ladies: the emperor's paternal aunts are enfeoffed Grand Senior Princesses, paternal sisters Senior Princesses, daughters Princesses — all treated as senior first rank.
translations.idiomatic: External titled ladies: the emperor's paternal aunts as Grand Senior Princesses, sisters as Senior Princesses, daughters as Princesses — all senior first rank.

sentences.zh: 皇太子之女，封郡主，視從一品。

translations.literal: The crown prince's daughters are enfeoffed Commandery Princesses, treated as junior first rank.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's daughters were Commandery Princesses, junior first rank.

sentences.zh: 王之女，封縣主，視正二品。

translations.literal: Kings' daughters are enfeoffed County Princesses, treated as senior second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Kings' daughters were County Princesses, senior second rank.

sentences.zh: 王母妻，為妃。

translations.literal: A king's consort is styled Consort.
translations.idiomatic: A king's consort was styled Consort.

sentences.zh: 一品及國公母妻，為國夫人。

translations.literal: Senior first rank and state dukes' mothers and wives are styled Ladies of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Senior first rank and state dukes' mothers and wives were Ladies of the State.

sentences.zh: 三品已上母妻，為郡夫人。

translations.literal: Third rank and above mothers and wives are styled Ladies of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above mothers and wives were Ladies of the Commandery.

sentences.zh: 四品母妻，為郡君。

translations.literal: Fourth rank mothers and wives are styled Commandery Ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank mothers and wives were Commandery Ladies.

sentences.zh: 五品若勳官，三品有封，母妻為縣君。

translations.literal: Fifth rank or merit officials, third rank with enfeoffment — mothers and wives are styled County Ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank or merit officials with third-rank enfeoffment — mothers and wives were County Ladies.

sentences.zh: 散官並同職事。

translations.literal: Honorary officials follow functional officials.
translations.idiomatic: Honorary officials followed functional officials.

sentences.zh: 勳官四品有封，母妻為鄉君。

translations.literal: Fourth-rank merit officials with enfeoffment — mothers and wives are styled Township Ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth-rank merit officials with enfeoffment — mothers and wives were Township Ladies.

sentences.zh: 其母邑號，皆加「太」字，各視其夫、子之品。

translations.literal: Mothers' fief titles all add the character 'Grand'; each follows husband or son's rank.
translations.idiomatic: Mothers' fief titles added 'Grand'; each followed husband or son's rank.

sentences.zh: 若兩有官爵者，從其高。

translations.literal: If holding both office and enfeoffment, follow the higher.
translations.idiomatic: If holding both office and enfeoffment, the higher rank applied.

sentences.zh: 若內命婦，一品之母，為正四品郡君；

translations.literal: For internal titled ladies, a senior first rank's mother is a senior fourth rank Commandery Lady;
translations.idiomatic: Internal titled ladies: a senior first rank's mother was a senior fourth rank Commandery Lady;

sentences.zh: 二品之母，為從四品郡君；

translations.literal: a senior second rank's mother is a junior fourth rank Commandery Lady;
translations.idiomatic: a senior second rank's mother was a junior fourth rank Commandery Lady;

sentences.zh: 三品四品之母，並為正五品縣君。

translations.literal: senior third and fourth rank mothers are all senior fifth rank County Ladies.
translations.idiomatic: senior third and fourth rank mothers were senior fifth rank County Ladies.

sentences.zh: 凡婦人，不因夫及子而別加邑號，夫人雲某品夫人，郡君為某品郡君，縣君、鄉君亦然。

translations.literal: Broadly, women do not receive separate fief titles apart from husband or son; Lady means a lady of such rank, Commandery Lady, County Lady, and Township Lady likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Women did not receive separate fief titles apart from husband or son; titles followed the same pattern for Lady, Commandery Lady, County Lady, and Township Lady.

sentences.zh: 凡庶子，有五品已上官，皆封嫡母。

translations.literal: For all secondary sons, if holding fifth rank or above office, the primary mother is enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Secondary sons holding fifth rank or above enfeoffed the primary mother.

sentences.zh: 無嫡母，封所生母。

translations.literal: Without a primary mother, the birth mother is enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Without a primary mother, the birth mother was enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 凡二王后夫人，職事五品已上，散官三品已上，王及國公母妻，朝參各視其夫及子之禮。

translations.literal: For consorts of the two former kings, functional officials fifth rank and above, honorary third rank and above, kings and state dukes' mothers and wives — court attendance each follows husband and son's ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts of former dynasties, fifth-rank functional officials and above, third-rank honorary officials and above, and kings' and state dukes' mothers and wives attended court per husband and son's ritual.

sentences.zh: 凡親王，孺人二人，視正五品，媵十人，視正六品。

translations.literal: For imperial princes: two Consorts, treated as senior fifth rank; ten Subsidiary Consorts, treated as senior sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes: two Consorts at senior fifth rank; ten Subsidiary Consorts at senior sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 嗣王、郡王及一品，媵十人，視從六品。

translations.literal: Heir princes, commandery princes, and senior first rank — ten Subsidiary Consorts, treated as junior sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Heir princes, commandery princes, and senior first rank: ten Subsidiary Consorts at junior sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 二品，媵八人，視正七品。

translations.literal: Senior second rank — eight Subsidiary Consorts, treated as senior seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Senior second rank: eight Subsidiary Consorts at senior seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 三品及國公，媵六人，視從七品。

translations.literal: Senior third rank and state dukes — six Subsidiary Consorts, treated as junior seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Senior third rank and state dukes: six Subsidiary Consorts at junior seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 四品，媵四人，視正八品。

translations.literal: Fourth rank — four Subsidiary Consorts, treated as senior eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank: four Subsidiary Consorts at senior eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 五品，媵三人，視從八品。

translations.literal: Fifth rank — three Subsidiary Consorts, treated as junior eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: three Subsidiary Consorts at junior eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 降此外皆為妾。

translations.literal: Below this all are concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Below this rank all were concubines.

sentences.zh: 凡皇家五等親，及諸親三等，存亡升降，皆立簿書籍，每三年一造。

translations.literal: For the imperial clan's five degrees of kin and all three degrees of related kin, survival, death, promotion, and demotion — all have registers compiled every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial five degrees of kin and three degrees of related kin — survival, death, promotion, and demotion — had registers compiled every three years.

sentences.zh: 除附之制，並載于宗正寺。

translations.literal: The system for removal and attachment is all recorded in the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Removal and attachment regulations were recorded in the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 司勳郎中司勳郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Meritorious Service Bureau Director — one post, junior fifth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious Service Bureau Director: one post, junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 隋曰司勳郎，武德初乃加「中」字。

translations.literal: Under Sui called Meritorious Service Director; at the beginning of Wude the character 'central' was added.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, Meritorious Service Director; early Wude added 'central'.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為司勳大夫，咸亨復也。

translations.literal: Longshuo renamed Meritorious Service Grandee; Xianheng restored.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed it Meritorious Service Grandee; restored in 670.

sentences.zh: 司勳員外郎二員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Meritorious Service Bureau Assistant Directors — two posts, junior sixth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious Service Bureau Assistant Directors: two posts, junior sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事四人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Chief clerks four, junior ninth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks: four, junior ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史三十三人，書令史六十人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Document clerks thirty-three, writing clerks sixty, custodians four.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-three document clerks, sixty writing clerks, four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌邦國官人之勳級。

translations.literal: The Director and Assistant Directors administer merit grades for state officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Director and Assistant Directors administered merit grades for state officials.

sentences.zh: 凡勳，十有二轉為上柱國，比正二品。

translations.literal: For merit, twelve rotations reach Senior Pillar of the State, equivalent to senior second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve merit rotations reached Senior Pillar of the State, equivalent to senior second rank.

sentences.zh: 十一轉為柱國，比從二品。

translations.literal: Eleven rotations — Pillar of the State, equivalent to junior second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven rotations: Pillar of the State, junior second rank.

sentences.zh: 十轉為上護軍，比正三品。

translations.literal: Ten rotations — Senior Protector General, equivalent to senior third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ten rotations: Senior Protector General, senior third rank.

sentences.zh: 九轉為護軍，比從三品。

translations.literal: Nine rotations — Protector General, equivalent to junior third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Nine rotations: Protector General, junior third rank.

sentences.zh: 八轉為上輕車都尉，比正四品。

translations.literal: Eight rotations — Senior Light Chariot Commandant, equivalent to senior fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Eight rotations: Senior Light Chariot Commandant, senior fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 七轉為輕車都尉，比從四品。

translations.literal: Seven rotations — Light Chariot Commandant, equivalent to junior fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Seven rotations: Light Chariot Commandant, junior fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 六轉為上騎都尉，比正五品。

translations.literal: Six rotations — Senior Cavalry Commandant, equivalent to senior fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Six rotations: Senior Cavalry Commandant, senior fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 五轉為騎都尉，比從五品。

translations.literal: Five rotations — Cavalry Commandant, equivalent to junior fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Five rotations: Cavalry Commandant, junior fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 四轉為驍騎尉，比正六品。

translations.literal: Four rotations — Valiant Cavalry Commandant, equivalent to senior sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Four rotations: Valiant Cavalry Commandant, senior sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 三轉為飛騎尉，比從六品。

translations.literal: Three rotations — Flying Cavalry Commandant, equivalent to junior sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Three rotations: Flying Cavalry Commandant, junior sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 二轉為雲騎尉，比正七品。

translations.literal: Two rotations — Cloud Cavalry Commandant, equivalent to senior seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two rotations: Cloud Cavalry Commandant, senior seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 一轉為武騎尉，比從七品。

translations.literal: One rotation — Martial Cavalry Commandant, equivalent to junior seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: One rotation: Martial Cavalry Commandant, junior seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 凡有功效之人，合授勳官者，皆委之覆定，然後奏擬。

translations.literal: All persons with achievements who should receive merit offices are entrusted for review and confirmation, then memorialized for proposed appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Those with achievements eligible for merit offices were reviewed and confirmed, then memorialized for appointment.

sentences.zh: 考功郎中考功郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Merit Evaluation Bureau Director — one post, junior fifth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Merit Evaluation Bureau Director: one post, junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年改為司績大夫，咸亨初乃復。

translations.literal: Second year of Longshuo renamed Director of Records Grandee; at the beginning of Xianheng restored.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed it Director of Records Grandee; restored at the beginning of 670.

sentences.zh: 考功員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Merit Evaluation Bureau Assistant Director — one post, junior sixth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Merit Evaluation Bureau Assistant Director: one post, junior sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為司績員外郎，咸亨復。

translations.literal: Longshuo renamed Records Bureau Assistant Director; Xianheng restored.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed it Records Bureau Assistant Director; restored in 670.

sentences.zh: 主事三人，從八品上。

translations.literal: Chief clerks three, junior eighth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks: three, junior eighth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史十三人，書令史二十五人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Document clerks thirteen, writing clerks twenty-five, custodians four.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen document clerks, twenty-five writing clerks, four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌內外文武官吏之考課。

translations.literal: The Director and Assistant Directors administer merit evaluation for civil and military officials inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: The Director and Assistant Directors administered merit evaluation for all civil and military officials.

sentences.zh: 凡應考之官家，具錄當年功過行能，本司及本州長官對眾讀，議其優劣，定為九等考第，各于所由司准額校定，然後送省。

translations.literal: All officials subject to evaluation at home compile that year's achievements, faults, conduct, and ability; the home bureau and prefectural chief read before the assembly, discuss superiority and inferiority, fix nine-grade evaluation, each bureau verifies by quota, then sends to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Evaluated officials compiled annual achievements, faults, conduct, and ability; home bureau and prefectural chiefs read before assembly, fixed nine-grade evaluations, bureaus verified by quota, then sent to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 內外文武官，量遠近以程之有差，附朝集使送簿至省。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials inside and outside — measuring distance, deadlines differ; attached to capital assembly envoys they send registers to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials sent registers via capital assembly envoys, with deadlines varying by distance.

sentences.zh: 每年別敕定京官位望高者二人，其一人校京官考，一人校外官考。

translations.literal: Each year a separate edict fixes two capital officials of high standing; one evaluates capital officials, one evaluates outside officials.
translations.idiomatic: Annual edict appointed two high-standing capital officials: one evaluated capital officials, one outside officials.

sentences.zh: 又定給事中、中書舍人各一人，其一人監京官考，一人監外官考。

translations.literal: Also fixing one Supervising Secretary and one Secretariat Drafter each; one supervises capital evaluation, one supervises outside evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: One supervising secretary and one secretariat drafter supervised capital and outside evaluations respectively.

sentences.zh: 郎中判京官考，員外判外官考。

translations.literal: The Director adjudicates capital evaluation; the Assistant Director adjudicates outside evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: The Director adjudicated capital evaluation; the Assistant Director outside evaluation.

sentences.zh: 其檢覆同者，皆以功過上使。

translations.literal: When inspection and review agree, all are reported to the emperor with achievements and faults.
translations.idiomatic: When inspection confirmed, achievements and faults were reported to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 京官則集應考之人對讀註定，外官對朝集使註定。

translations.literal: Capital officials gather candidates for public reading and annotation; outside officials annotate with capital assembly envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials gathered for public reading and annotation; outside officials annotated via assembly envoys.

sentences.zh: 凡考課之法，有四善：一曰德義有聞，二曰清慎明著，三曰公平可稱，四曰恪勤匪懈。

translations.literal: The evaluation method has four excellences: first, virtue and righteousness widely known; second, purity and prudence clearly manifest; third, fairness can be praised; fourth, diligence without slackness.
translations.idiomatic: Evaluation used four excellences: widely known virtue, manifest purity and prudence, praiseworthy fairness, and diligent industry.

sentences.zh: 善狀之外，有二十七最：其一曰獻可替否，拾遺補闕，為近侍之最。

translations.literal: Beyond excellence records, there are twenty-seven 'bests': first, presenting what is acceptable and replacing what is not, remedying omissions and filling gaps — the best for close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond excellences, twenty-seven 'bests': first, remedying omissions and filling gaps — best for close attendants.

sentences.zh: 其二曰銓衡人物，擢盡才良，為選司之最。

translations.literal: Second, weighing persons and elevating all talent — the best for selection bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Second, weighing talent and elevating the capable — best for selection bureaus.

sentences.zh: 其三曰揚清激濁，褒貶必當，為考校之最。

translations.literal: Third, promoting the pure and repelling the turbid, praise and censure always appropriate — the best for evaluation officers.
translations.idiomatic: Third, promoting the worthy and repelling the corrupt with appropriate praise and censure — best for evaluators.

sentences.zh: 其四曰禮制儀式，動合經典，為禮官之最。

translations.literal: Fourth, ritual forms and ceremonies moving in accord with classics — the best for rites officers.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, ritual forms conforming to classics — best for rites officers.

sentences.zh: 其五曰音律克諧，不失節奏，為樂官之最。

translations.literal: Fifth, musical tones harmonious, never missing rhythm — the best for music officers.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, harmonious music without missed rhythm — best for music officers.

sentences.zh: 其六曰決斷不滯，與奪合理，為判事之最。

translations.literal: Sixth, decisions without delay, grant and denial reasonable — the best for adjudicators.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, prompt decisions with reasonable grant and denial — best for adjudicators.

sentences.zh: 其七曰都統有方，警守無失，為宿衛之最。

translations.literal: Seventh, overall command effective, alert guard without lapse — the best for palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, effective command with alert guard — best for palace guards.

sentences.zh: 其八曰兵士調習，戎裝充備，為督領之最。

translations.literal: Eighth, soldiers drilled, military equipment complete — the best for supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, drilled soldiers with complete equipment — best for supervisors.

sentences.zh: 其九曰推鞫得情，處斷平允，為法官之最。

translations.literal: Ninth, investigation obtaining the facts, judgment and sentence fair — the best for judges.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, investigation finding facts with fair judgment — best for judges.

sentences.zh: 其十曰讎校精審，明為刊定，為校正之最。

translations.literal: Tenth, proofreading precise and careful, clearly edited and fixed — the best for correctors.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, precise proofreading and clear editing — best for correctors.

sentences.zh: 其十一曰承旨敷奏，吐納明敏，為宣納之最。

translations.literal: Eleventh, receiving orders and memorializing, expression clear and keen — the best for announcement officers.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh, clear and keen memorializing — best for announcement officers.

sentences.zh: 其十二曰訓導有方，生徒充業，為學官之最。

translations.literal: Twelfth, instruction effective, students completing studies — the best for academy officers.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth, effective instruction with students completing studies — best for academy officers.

sentences.zh: 其十三曰賞罰嚴明，攻戰必勝，為將帥之最。

translations.literal: Thirteenth, rewards and punishments strict and clear, attacking in battle always victorious — the best for generals.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteenth, strict rewards and punishments with battle victory — best for generals.

sentences.zh: 其十四曰禮義興行，肅清所部，為政教之最。

translations.literal: Fourteenth, rites and righteousness flourishing, the governed area purified — the best for civil administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteenth, flourishing rites with purified jurisdiction — best for civil administrators.

sentences.zh: 其十五曰詳錄典正，辭理兼舉，為文史之最。

translations.literal: Fifteenth, detailed records canonical and correct, rhetoric and principle both raised — the best for literary historians.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteenth, detailed canonical records with rhetoric and principle — best for literary historians.

sentences.zh: 其十六曰訪察精審，彈舉必當，為糾正之最。

translations.literal: Sixteenth, investigation precise and careful, impeachment always appropriate — the best for censors.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteenth, precise investigation with appropriate impeachment — best for censors.

sentences.zh: 其十七曰明於勘覆，稽失無隱，為勾檢之最。

translations.literal: Seventeenth, clear in audit and review, errors and omissions not concealed — the best for auditors.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeenth, clear audit with no concealed errors — best for auditors.

sentences.zh: 其十八曰職事修理，供承強濟，為監掌之最。

translations.literal: Eighteenth, duties maintained and repaired, supply and service strong and sufficient — the best for supervisors of supply.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteenth, maintained duties with sufficient supply — best for supply supervisors.

sentences.zh: 其十九曰功課皆充，丁匠無怨，為役使之最。

translations.literal: Nineteenth, labor service all fulfilled, craftsmen without complaint — the best for corvée officers.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteenth, fulfilled labor with no craftsman complaints — best for corvée officers.

sentences.zh: 其二十曰耕耨以時，收穫成課，為屯官之最。

translations.literal: Twentieth, plowing and hoeing on schedule, harvest completing quota — the best for garrison officers.
translations.idiomatic: Twentieth, timely farming with completed harvest — best for garrison officers.

sentences.zh: 其二十一曰謹于蓋藏，明于出納，為倉庫之最。

translations.literal: Twenty-first, careful in storage, clear in disbursement — the best for storehouse officers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-first, careful storage and clear disbursement — best for storehouse officers.

sentences.zh: 其二十二曰推步盈虛，究理精密，為曆官之最。

translations.literal: Twenty-second, calendrical calculation of fullness and emptiness, principles investigated with precision — the best for calendar officers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-second, precise calendrical calculation — best for calendar officers.

sentences.zh: 其二十三曰占候醫卜，效驗居多，為方術之最。

translations.literal: Twenty-third, observation, medicine, and divination with mostly verified results — the best for technical specialists.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-third, observation, medicine, and divination with verified results — best for technical specialists.

sentences.zh: 其二十四曰譏察有方，行旅無壅，為關津之最。

translations.literal: Twenty-fourth, inspection effective, travelers unimpeded — the best for pass officers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-fourth, effective inspection with unimpeded travel — best for pass officers.

sentences.zh: 其二十五曰市廛不擾，奸濫不作，為市司之最。
