translations.literal: Twenty-fifth, markets undisturbed, fraud and usury not arising — the best for market officers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-fifth, undisturbed markets without fraud — best for market officers.

sentences.zh: 其二十六曰牧養肥碩，蕃息孳多，為牧官之最。

translations.literal: Twenty-sixth, herds fat and thriving, breeding prolific — the best for pasture officers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-sixth, fat herds with prolific breeding — best for pasture officers.

sentences.zh: 其二十七曰邊境肅清，城隍修理，為鎮防之最。

translations.literal: Twenty-seventh, borders quiet and clear, walls and moats repaired — the best for frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seventh, quiet borders with repaired defenses — best for frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 一最以上，有四善，為上上。

translations.literal: One 'best' or more with four excellences — highest upper.
translations.idiomatic: One or more 'bests' with four excellences: highest upper grade.

sentences.zh: 一最以上，有三善，或無最而有四善，為上中。

translations.literal: One 'best' or more with three excellences, or no 'best' but four excellences — upper middle.
translations.idiomatic: One or more 'bests' with three excellences, or four excellences without a 'best': upper middle.

sentences.zh: 一最以上，有二善，或無最而有三善，為上下。

translations.literal: One 'best' or more with two excellences, or no 'best' but three excellences — upper lower.
translations.idiomatic: One or more 'bests' with two excellences, or three excellences without a 'best': upper lower.

sentences.zh: 一最以上，而有一善，或無最而有二善，為中上。

translations.literal: One 'best' or more with one excellence, or no 'best' but two excellences — middle upper.
translations.idiomatic: One or more 'bests' with one excellence, or two excellences without a 'best': middle upper.

sentences.zh: 一最以上，或無最而有一善，為中中。

translations.literal: One 'best' or more, or no 'best' but one excellence — middle middle.
translations.idiomatic: One or more 'bests', or one excellence without a 'best': middle middle.

sentences.zh: 職事粗理，善最不聞，為中下。

translations.literal: Duties roughly managed, excellence and 'best' not heard of — middle lower.
translations.idiomatic: Duties roughly managed, no excellence or 'best' noted: middle lower.

sentences.zh: 愛憎任情，處斷乖理，為下上。

translations.literal: Love and hate follow feeling, judgment and sentence contrary to reason — lower upper.
translations.idiomatic: Following personal bias with unreasonable judgment: lower upper.

sentences.zh: 背公向私，職務廢闕，為下中。

translations.literal: Turning from public to private, duties abandoned and lacking — lower middle.
translations.idiomatic: Neglecting public duty for private gain: lower middle.

sentences.zh: 居官諂詐，貪濁有狀，為下下。

translations.literal: In office flattering and deceitful, greed and corruption with evidence — lower lower.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery, deceit, and proven corruption in office: lower lower.

sentences.zh: 若於善最之外，別可加尚，及罪雖成殿，情狀可矜，雖不成殿，而情狀可責者，省校之日，皆聽考官臨時量定。

translations.literal: If beyond excellences and 'bests' there is special merit to be commended, or guilt though forming demerit record yet circumstances pitiable, or though not forming demerit yet circumstances blameworthy — on the day of provincial review, evaluators may provisionally decide at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond standard grades, special merit, pitiable guilt, or blameworthy conduct without formal demerit — evaluators could decide provisionally at review.

sentences.zh: 內外官從見任改為別官者，其年考從日申校，百司量其閑劇，諸州據其上下。

translations.literal: Inside and outside officials transferred from current post to another — that year's evaluation follows from the day of transfer; bureaus measure leisure or urgency, prefectures follow upper or lower.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred officials' annual evaluation dated from transfer; bureaus weighed workload, prefectures upper or lower status.

sentences.zh: 進考之人，皆有定限，苟無其功，不要充數。

translations.literal: Those advancing in evaluation all have fixed limits; if without achievement, do not fill the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Evaluation advancement had fixed limits; without achievement, quotas were not filled.

sentences.zh: 功過於限，亦聽量進。

translations.literal: If achievement exceeds the limit, measured advancement is also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Achievement exceeding limits permitted measured advancement.

sentences.zh: 其流外官，本司量其行能功過，立四等考第而勉進之。

translations.literal: For outside-stream officials, the home bureau measures conduct, ability, achievement, and fault, establishes four-grade evaluation, and urges advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Outside-stream officials received four-grade evaluations by home bureau measuring conduct and achievement.

sentences.zh: 凡親勳翊衛，皆有考第。

translations.literal: All imperial kin, merit guards, and assist guards have evaluation grades.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kin, merit guards, and assist guards all received evaluation grades.

sentences.zh: 考第之中，略有三等。

translations.literal: Among evaluation grades, broadly there are three levels.
translations.idiomatic: Evaluation grades broadly had three levels.

sentences.zh: 衛主帥，如三衛之考。

translations.literal: Guard commanders, like the three guards' evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Guard commanders followed three-guards evaluation.

sentences.zh: 其監門、校尉、直長，如主帥之考。

translations.literal: Gatekeepers, commandants, and duty chiefs, like commanders' evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Gatekeepers, commandants, and duty chiefs followed commanders' evaluation.

sentences.zh: 凡諡議之法，古之通典，皆審其事，以為旌別。

translations.literal: The method for posthumous titles is an ancient universal statute; all examine the matter to make distinction and praise.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title deliberation was an ancient universal statute examining conduct for distinction.

sentences.zh: 戶部戶部尚書戶部尚書一員，正三品。

translations.literal: Revenue Ministry Minister — one post, senior third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue: one post, senior third rank.

sentences.zh: 隋為民部尚書，貞觀二十三年改為戶部。

translations.literal: Under Sui called Minister of the People; twenty-third year of Zhenguan changed to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, Minister of the People; renamed Revenue in 649.

sentences.zh: 明慶元年改為度支，龍朔二年改為司元太常伯，光宅元年改為地官尚書，神龍復為戶部。

translations.literal: First year of Mingqing changed to Expenditure; second year of Longshuo to Director of Origins Grand Master of Splendor; first year of Guangzhai to Earthly Offices Minister; Shenlong restored as Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Renamed Expenditure in 656, Director of Origins in 662, Earthly Offices Minister in 689; restored as Revenue after Shenlong.

sentences.zh: 侍郎二員。

translations.literal: Vice Ministers — two posts.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Ministers: two posts.

sentences.zh: 正四品下。

translations.literal: Senior fourth rank lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Senior fourth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 因隋已來改易名位，皆隋尚書也。

translations.literal: Because from Sui onward names and ranks changed, all follow Sui ministry titles.
translations.idiomatic: Name changes from Sui onward followed Sui ministry titles.

sentences.zh: 尚書、侍郎之職，掌天下田戶、均輸、錢谷之政令，其屬有四：一曰戶部，二曰度支，三曰金部，四曰倉部。

translations.literal: Minister and Vice Ministers administer policies for fields, households, equal transport, and money and grain throughout the realm; subordinates are four: Revenue, Expenditure, Metals, and Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister and Vice Ministers administered land, household, transport, and fiscal policy via four bureaus: Revenue, Expenditure, Metals, and Granaries.

sentences.zh: 總其職務，而行其制命。

translations.literal: Gather respective duties and carry out issued regulations.
translations.idiomatic: They coordinated bureau duties and implemented regulations.

sentences.zh: 凡中外百司之事，由於所屬，皆質正焉。

translations.literal: All inside and outside bureau matters through their jurisdiction are verified.
translations.idiomatic: All bureau business under their jurisdiction was verified.

sentences.zh: 戶部郎中郎中二員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Revenue Bureau Director — two posts, junior fifth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Bureau Directors: two posts, junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 員外郎二員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Bureau Assistant Directors — two posts, junior sixth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Assistant Directors: two posts, junior sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外，自隋已來，隨曹改易。

translations.literal: Director and Assistant Director, from Sui onward, change with the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Director and Assistant Director titles changed with the bureau from Sui onward.

sentences.zh: 主事四人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Chief clerks four, junior ninth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks: four, junior ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史十五人，書令史三十四人，亭長六人，掌固十人。

translations.literal: Document clerks fifteen, writing clerks thirty-four, ward captains six, custodians ten.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen document clerks, thirty-four writing clerks, six ward captains, ten custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌分理戶口、井田之事。

translations.literal: Director and Assistant Director administer household registers and well-field matters.
translations.idiomatic: The Director and Assistant Director administered household registers and land allocation.

sentences.zh: 凡天下十道，任土所出，為貢賦之差。

translations.literal: Broadly, the ten circuits of the realm — each land produces its tribute and tax differences.
translations.idiomatic: The ten circuits' tribute and tax varied by local production.

sentences.zh: 凡天下之州府，三百一十有五，而羈縻之州，迨八百焉。

translations.literal: All prefectures and districts in the realm number three hundred fifteen; tributary prefectures reach eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The realm had 315 prefectures; tributary prefectures reached 800.

sentences.zh: 四萬戶已上為上州，二萬戶以上為中州，不滿為下州。

translations.literal: Forty thousand households and above are upper prefectures, twenty thousand and above middle prefectures, below are lower prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Forty thousand households or more: upper prefecture; twenty thousand or more: middle; below: lower.

sentences.zh: 凡三都之縣，在內曰京縣，城外曰畿，又望縣有八十五焉。

translations.literal: All counties of the three capitals — within the walls are capital counties, outside the walls capital outskirts; also eighty-five 'prominent' counties.
translations.idiomatic: Three capitals' counties: capital counties within walls, outskirts counties outside; plus 85 prominent counties.

sentences.zh: 其餘則六千戶以上為上縣，二千戶已上為中縣，一千戶已上為中下縣，不滿一千戶皆為下縣。

translations.literal: The rest: six thousand households and above upper county, two thousand and above middle county, one thousand and above lower-middle county, below one thousand all lower counties.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand or more: upper county; two thousand or more: middle; one thousand or more: lower-middle; below one thousand: lower.

sentences.zh: 凡天下之戶，八百一萬八千七百一十，口四千六百二十八萬五千一百六十一。

translations.literal: All households in the realm: eight million one hundred eighty-seven thousand one hundred ten; population forty-six million two hundred eighty-five thousand one hundred sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Households: 8,187,710; population: 46,285,161.

sentences.zh: 百戶為裏，五里為鄉。

translations.literal: One hundred households make a li, five li make a township.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred households formed a li; five li formed a township.

sentences.zh: 兩京及州縣之郭內，分為坊，郊外為村。

translations.literal: Within the two capitals and prefectural and county cities, divided into wards; outside the walls are villages.
translations.idiomatic: Capitals and cities divided into wards; outskirts into villages.

sentences.zh: 裏及坊村皆有正，以司督察。

translations.literal: Each li, ward, and village has a head to supervise and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Each li, ward, and village had a head for supervision.

sentences.zh: 四家為鄰，五鄰為保。

translations.literal: Four households make a neighbor group, five neighbor groups make a mutual-security unit.
translations.idiomatic: Four households formed a neighbor group; five groups formed a mutual-security unit.

sentences.zh: 保有長，以相禁約。

translations.literal: Mutual-security units have chiefs to mutually restrain.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual-security chiefs enforced mutual restraint.

sentences.zh: 凡男女，始生為黃，四歲為小，十六為中，二十有一為丁，六十為老。

translations.literal: All men and women: at birth yellow, at four small, at sixteen middle, at twenty-one ding, at sixty old.
translations.idiomatic: Life stages: yellow at birth, small at four, middle at sixteen, ding at twenty-one, old at sixty.

sentences.zh: 每一歲一造計帳。

translations.literal: Each year compile statistical accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Statistical accounts compiled annually.

sentences.zh: 三年一造戶籍。

translations.literal: Every three years compile household registers.
translations.idiomatic: Household registers compiled every three years.

sentences.zh: 縣以籍成於州，州成於省，戶部總而領焉。

translations.literal: Counties complete registers for prefectures, prefectures for the ministry, Revenue ministry totals and oversees.
translations.idiomatic: Counties reported to prefectures, prefectures to the ministry; Revenue oversaw totals.

sentences.zh: 凡天下之戶，量其資定為九等，每定戶以仲年，造籍以季年。

translations.literal: All households measured by assets into nine grades; household fixing in mid-year, register compilation in last quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Households graded into nine asset classes; fixing in mid-year, registers in last quarter.

sentences.zh: 州縣之籍，恆留五比，省籍留九比。

translations.literal: Prefectural registers permanently keep five cycles; ministry registers nine cycles.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures kept five register cycles; the ministry nine.

sentences.zh: 凡戶之兩貫者，先從邊州為定，次從關內，次從軍府州。

translations.literal: For households with two registrations, first fix from border prefectures, next from interior, next from military prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Dual-registration households: border prefectures first, then interior, then military prefectures.

sentences.zh: 若俱者，各從其先貫焉。

translations.literal: If equal, each follows whichever was registered first.
translations.idiomatic: If equal, whichever registered first applied.

sentences.zh: 樂住之制：居狹鄉者，聽其從寬；

translations.literal: Residence-fixing system: those in cramped districts may move to spacious;
translations.idiomatic: Residence rules: cramped districts could move to spacious ones;

sentences.zh: 居遠者，聽其從近；

translations.literal: those in distant places may move to near;
translations.idiomatic: distant places to nearer ones;

sentences.zh: 居輕役之地者，聽其從重。

translations.literal: those in light-corvée districts may move to heavy.
translations.idiomatic: light-corvée districts to heavier ones.

sentences.zh: 辨天下之四人，使各專其業。

translations.literal: Distinguish the four classes of the realm, each specializing in their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Four classes specialized in their occupations.

sentences.zh: 凡習學文武者為士，肆力耕桑者為農，巧作器用者為工，屠沽興販者為商。

translations.literal: Those studying civil and military arts are scholars, exerting strength in farming and sericulture are farmers, skillfully making implements are artisans, butchering and trading are merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars studied civil and military arts; farmers farmed; artisans made implements; merchants traded.

sentences.zh: 工商之家，不得預於士。

translations.literal: Artisan and merchant families may not participate among scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Artisan and merchant families could not enter scholar ranks.

sentences.zh: 食祿之人，不得奪下人之利。

translations.literal: Salary recipients may not seize profit from those below.
translations.idiomatic: Salary recipients could not seize subordinates' profit.

sentences.zh: 凡天下之田，五尺為步，步二百有四十為畝，畝百為頃。

translations.literal: All fields in the realm: five chi make a bu, 240 bu make a mu, 100 mu make a qing.
translations.idiomatic: Fields: five chi per bu, 240 bu per mu, 100 mu per qing.

sentences.zh: 度其肥瘠寬狹，以居其人。

translations.literal: Measure fertility, barrenness, width, and narrowness to settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: Land was allocated by fertility and size to settle the people.

sentences.zh: 凡給田之制有差，園宅之地亦如之。

translations.literal: All land-grant systems have differences; garden and residential land likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Land grants and residential plots followed graded rules.

sentences.zh: 凡給口分田，皆從便近。

translations.literal: All per-capita land grants follow convenience of proximity.
translations.idiomatic: Per-capita grants followed proximity.

sentences.zh: 居城之人，本縣無田者，則隔縣給授。

translations.literal: City dwellers without land in their home county receive grants from a neighboring county.
translations.idiomatic: City dwellers without home-county land received grants from neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 凡應收授之田，皆起十月，畢十二月。

translations.literal: All land to be received or returned — begin in the tenth month, finish by the twelfth.
translations.idiomatic: Land receipt and return ran from the tenth through twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 凡授田，先課後不課，先貧後富，先多後少。

translations.literal: For land grants: first taxed then untaxed, first poor then rich, first many then few.
translations.idiomatic: Grants prioritized taxed before untaxed, poor before rich, many before few.

sentences.zh: 凡州縣界內所部，受田悉足者，為寬鄉，不足者為狹鄉。

translations.literal: Where all land within a prefecture's borders is fully allocated — spacious district; where insufficient — cramped district.
translations.idiomatic: Fully allocated districts were spacious; insufficient ones cramped.

sentences.zh: 凡官人及勳，授永業田。

translations.literal: All officials and merit holders receive permanent estate land.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and merit holders received permanent estate land.

sentences.zh: 凡天下諸州有公廨田，凡諸州及都護府官人有職分田。

translations.literal: All prefectures have public office land; all prefectures and protectorate officials have duty land.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures had public office land; officials had duty land.

sentences.zh: 凡賦役之制有四：一曰租，二曰調，三曰役，四曰雜徭。

translations.literal: The tax and corvée system has four: first rent, second allocation, third labor, fourth miscellaneous corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Tax and corvée had four types: rent, allocation, labor, and miscellaneous corvée.

sentences.zh: 課戶每丁租粟二石。

translations.literal: Tax households: each ding two shi of grain rent.
translations.idiomatic: Each ding paid two shi grain rent.

sentences.zh: 其調，隨鄉土所產綾絹絁各二丈，布加五分之一。

translations.literal: Allocation: according to local products, silk gauze two zhang each, cloth adds one-fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Allocation: local silk or cloth two zhang; cloth added one-fifth.

sentences.zh: 輸綾絹絁者，綿三兩。

translations.literal: Those submitting silk gauze — three liang cotton.
translations.idiomatic: Silk submitters added three liang cotton.

sentences.zh: 輸布者，麻三斤。

translations.literal: Those submitting cloth — three jin hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Cloth submitters added three jin hemp.

sentences.zh: 皆書印焉。

translations.literal: All are stamped with seal.
translations.idiomatic: All were officially stamped.

sentences.zh: 凡丁，歲役二旬，無事則收其庸，每日三尺。

translations.literal: Each ding, two ten-day periods labor yearly; if no labor, collect substitution at three chi per day.
translations.idiomatic: Each ding: two ten-day labor periods yearly; otherwise three chi cloth per day substitution.

sentences.zh: 有事而加役者，旬有五日免調，三旬則租調俱免。

translations.literal: If labor added for affairs, fifteen days exempts allocation; thirty days exempts rent and allocation.
translations.idiomatic: Added labor: fifteen days exempted allocation; thirty days exempted rent and allocation.

sentences.zh: 凡庸調之物，仲秋斂之，季秋發於州。

translations.literal: All substitution and allocation goods collected mid-autumn, sent to prefectures last autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Substitution and allocation collected mid-autumn, sent to prefectures last autumn.

sentences.zh: 租則准州土收穫早晚，量事而斂之。

translations.literal: Rent follows each prefecture's harvest timing, measuring affairs to collect.
translations.idiomatic: Rent collection followed local harvest timing.

sentences.zh: 仲冬起輸，孟春而納畢。

translations.literal: Collection begins mid-winter, completed by first month of spring.
translations.idiomatic: Collection mid-winter through first month of spring.

sentences.zh: 本州納者，季冬而畢。

translations.literal: Those delivered to home prefecture complete by last month of winter.
translations.idiomatic: Home prefecture delivery completed by last winter month.

sentences.zh: 凡諸國蕃胡內附者，亦定為九等。

translations.literal: All submitted foreign and inner tribes also fixed in nine grades.
translations.idiomatic: Submitted foreign and inner tribes also graded in nine classes.

sentences.zh: 凡嶺南諸州稅米，及天下諸州稅錢，各有准常。

translations.literal: Lingnan prefectures' grain tax and all prefectures' money tax each have fixed rates.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan grain tax and prefectural money tax had fixed rates.

sentences.zh: 凡丁戶皆有優復蠲免之制。

translations.literal: All ding households have preferential exemption systems.
translations.idiomatic: Ding households had preferential exemptions.

sentences.zh: 若孝子順孫、義夫節婦志行聞於鄉閭者，州縣申省奏聞，而表其門閭，同籍悉免課役。

translations.literal: Filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, chaste wives whose conduct is known in village and hamlet — prefecture and county report to ministry for memorial, tablet their gate, same register all exempt from tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and chaste conduct reported to ministry brought gate tablets and household tax exemption.

sentences.zh: 有精誠致應者，則加優賞焉。

translations.literal: Those with sincere devotion and responsive efficacy receive added preferential reward.
translations.idiomatic: Sincere devotion with responsive efficacy received added rewards.

sentences.zh: 凡京司文武職事官，皆有防閣。

translations.literal: All capital functional civil and military officials have guard attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Capital civil and military officials had guard attendants.

sentences.zh: 凡州縣官僚，皆有白直。

translations.literal: All prefectural and county officials have white-attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county officials had white-attendants.

sentences.zh: 凡州縣官及在外監官，皆有執衣。

translations.literal: All prefectural officials and outside supervisors have uniform-bearers.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural officials and outside supervisors had uniform-bearers.

sentences.zh: 凡諸親王府屬，並給士力，具品數如白直。

translations.literal: All imperial prince household staff receive laborers, quotas like white-attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial prince households received laborers per white-attendant quotas.

sentences.zh: 凡有功之臣，賜實封者，皆以課戶充。

translations.literal: All meritorious subjects granted substantive enfeoffment — all filled with tax households.
translations.idiomatic: Substantive enfeoffment used tax households.

sentences.zh: 凡食封，皆傳於子孫。

translations.literal: All food-enfeoffment passes to descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Food-enfeoffment passed to descendants.

sentences.zh: 凡庶人年八十及篤疾，給侍丁一人，九十，給二人，百歲，三人。

translations.literal: Commoners age eighty and seriously ill receive one attendant ding; ninety, two; one hundred, three.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners: one attendant at eighty, two at ninety, three at one hundred.

sentences.zh: 凡天下朝集使，皆以十月二十五日至京師，十一月一日戶部引見訖，於尚書省與群官禮見，然後集於考堂，應考績之事。

translations.literal: All capital assembly envoys arrive twenty-fifth day of tenth month, first day of eleventh month Revenue presents them, at the ministry ritual meeting with officials, then gather at evaluation hall for merit matters.
translations.idiomatic: Assembly envoys arrived 25th of tenth month; Revenue presented them 1st of eleventh; merit evaluation followed.

sentences.zh: 元日，陳其貢篚於殿廷。

translations.literal: New Year's Day, present tribute at hall court.
translations.idiomatic: New Year's Day tribute presented at court.

sentences.zh: 凡京都諸縣令，每季一朝。

translations.literal: All capital county magistrates attend court each season.
translations.idiomatic: Capital county magistrates attended court quarterly.

sentences.zh: 度支郎中度支郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Expenditure Bureau Director — one post, junior fifth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Expenditure Bureau Director: one post, junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為司度大夫，咸亨復。

translations.literal: Longshuo renamed Director of Measures Grandee; Xianheng restored.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed Director of Measures Grandee; restored in 670.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Bureau Assistant Director — one post, junior sixth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Assistant Director: one post, junior sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Chief clerks two, junior ninth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks: two, junior ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史十六人，書令史三十三人，計史一人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Document clerks sixteen, writing clerks thirty-three, accounting clerks one, custodians four.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen document clerks, thirty-three writing clerks, one accounting clerk, four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌判天下租賦多少之數，物產豐約之宜，水陸道途之利。

translations.literal: Director and Assistant Director adjudicate rent and tax amounts, product abundance or scarcity, water and land route profit.
translations.idiomatic: They adjudicated rent, tax, production, and transport routes.

sentences.zh: 每歲計其所出而度其所用，轉運征斂送納，皆准程而節其遲速。

translations.literal: Each year calculate output and measure use; transport, collection, and delivery all by schedule regulating speed.
translations.idiomatic: Annual output and expenditure calculated; transport and delivery followed schedules.

sentences.zh: 凡和糴和市，皆量其貴賤，均天下之貨，以利於人。

translations.literal: All harmonized purchase and market purchase measure value, balance realm's goods for people's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonized and market purchases balanced goods for public benefit.

sentences.zh: 凡金銀寶貨綾羅之屬，皆折庸調以造。

translations.literal: All gold, silver, treasures, silk — all made from substitution and allocation.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, silver, treasures, and silk were procured via substitution and allocation.

sentences.zh: 凡天下舟車水陸載運，皆具為腳直，輕重貴賤、平易險澀而為之制。

translations.literal: Generally, for all transport by boat, cart, water, and land throughout the realm, porter fees are fully provided for, and regulations are established according to weight, value, and ease or difficulty of the route.
translations.idiomatic: For all freight moved by land and water across the empire, porter charges were set in full, with rules tailored to load, value, and route conditions.

sentences.zh: 凡天下邊軍，有支度使，以計軍資糧仗之用。

translations.literal: Generally, for all frontier armies throughout the realm, there are supply commissioners to calculate the use of military provisions, grain, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Every frontier army had a supply commissioner who calculated needs for provisions, grain, and arms.

sentences.zh: 每歲所費，皆申度支會計，以長行旨為准。

translations.literal: Each year's expenditures are all reported to the Expenditure Bureau for accounting, taking the standing directive as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Annual costs were reported to the Expenditure Bureau for audit according to standing orders.

sentences.zh: 金部郎中金部郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Metals Bureau Director — one post, junior fifth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Metals Bureau Director: one post, junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司珍大夫，咸亨復。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo styled Grand Master of Treasures; restored under Xianheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 662 the title became Grand Master of Treasures; restored in 670.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: One Bureau Assistant Director, junior sixth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: One Bureau Assistant Director, junior sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事三人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Three chief clerks, junior ninth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Three chief clerks, junior ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史八人，書令史二十一人，計史一人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Eight document clerks, twenty-one writing clerks, one accounting clerk, four custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Eight document clerks, twenty-one writing clerks, one accounting clerk, four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌判天下庫藏錢帛出納之事，頒其節制，而司其簿領。

translations.literal: The Director and Assistant Director adjudicate receipt and disbursement of money and silk in treasuries throughout the realm, promulgate regulations, and keep ledgers.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw treasury receipts and payments empire-wide, issued regulations, and maintained account books.

sentences.zh: 凡度，以北方秬黍中者一黍之廣為分，十分為寸，十寸為尺，一尺二寸為大尺，十尺為丈。

translations.literal: For length: the width of one grain of standard northern millet is one fen; ten fen one cun, ten cun one chi, one chi two cun a large chi, ten chi one zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Length: one grain-width of standard millet as one fen; ten fen one cun, ten cun one chi, one chi two cun a large chi, ten chi one zhang.

sentences.zh: 凡量，以秬黍中者容一千二百為龠，二龠為合，十合為升，十升為鬥，三斗為大鬥，十斗為斛。

translations.literal: For capacity: one thousand two hundred grains of standard millet one yue; two yue one he, ten he one sheng, ten sheng one dou, three dou a large dou, ten dou one hu.
translations.idiomatic: Capacity: twelve hundred grains as one yue; two yue one he, ten he one sheng, ten sheng one dou, three dou a large dou, ten dou one hu.

sentences.zh: 凡權衡，以秬黍中者百黍之重為銖，二十四銖為兩，三兩為大兩，十六兩為斤。

translations.literal: For weight: one hundred grains of standard millet one zhu; twenty-four zhu one liang, three liang a large liang, sixteen liang one jin.
translations.idiomatic: Weight: one hundred grains one zhu; twenty-four zhu one liang, three liang a large liang, sixteen liang one jin.

sentences.zh: 凡積秬黍為度量權衡，調鐘律，測晷景，合湯藥，及冠冕之制用之。

translations.literal: Accumulated millet standards served to tune bells and pipes, measure sundial shadows, compound medicines, and regulate caps and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Millet-based standards tuned bells and pipes, measured the sundial, prepared medicines, and regulated caps and robes.

sentences.zh: 內外官私，悉用大者。

translations.literal: For official and private use, inner and outer alike, the large standards were all used.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private, palace and beyond, all used the larger measures.

sentences.zh: 凡庫藏出納，皆行文榜，季終會之。

translations.literal: All treasury receipts and disbursements issued written notices; accounts reconciled each quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury movements were posted in notices and tallied quarterly.

sentences.zh: 若承命出納，則于中書、門下省覆而行之。

translations.literal: If disbursement was by imperial command, the Secretariat and Chancellery reviewed before execution.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial-order disbursements were reviewed by the Secretariat and Chancellery first.

sentences.zh: 百司應請月俸，符牒到，所由皆遞覆而行之，乃置木契，與應出物之司相合。

translations.literal: When offices requested monthly salaries and authorization arrived, offices transmitted upward for review; wooden tallies matched the disbursing office.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly salary authorizations passed up for review; wooden tallies matched disbursing offices.

sentences.zh: 凡官私互市，物數有制。

translations.literal: For official-private mutual markets, quantities of goods were regulated.
translations.idiomatic: Government-private trade had fixed quantity limits.

sentences.zh: 凡縑帛之類，有長短、廣狹、端疋、屯綟之差。

translations.literal: For silks and cloths, differences in length, width, bolts, and cotton bundles.
translations.idiomatic: Silks and cloths differed by length, width, bolts, and cotton bundles.

sentences.zh: 凡賜十段，其率絹三疋，布三端，綿三屯。

translations.literal: For grants of ten sections, the standard was three pieces of silk, three bolts of cloth, three bundles of cotton.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-section grants: three silk pieces, three cloth bolts, three cotton bundles.

sentences.zh: 若雜彩十段，則絲布二疋，二疋，綾二疋，縵四疋。

translations.literal: If ten sections of assorted colored silks: two silk cloth, two pieces, two gauze, four plain silk.
translations.idiomatic: Ten sections mixed colors: two silk cloth, two pieces, two gauze, four plain silk.

sentences.zh: 若賜蕃客錦彩，率十段則錦一張，綾二疋，縵三疋，綿四屯。

translations.literal: If brocade granted to foreign guests, per ten sections: one brocade, two gauze, three plain silk, four cotton bundles.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign guests: per ten sections, one brocade, two gauze, three plain silk, four cotton bundles.

sentences.zh: 凡遣使覆囚，則給時服。

translations.literal: Whenever envoys reviewed prisoners, seasonal robes were provided.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys inspecting prisoners received seasonal court dress.

sentences.zh: 若諸使經二年不還，亦如之。

translations.literal: If envoys had not returned after two years, the same applied.
translations.idiomatic: The same applied after two years abroad.

sentences.zh: 凡時服稱一具者，全給之，一副者，減給之。

translations.literal: Seasonal robes called one full set granted in full; one partial set at reduced amount.
translations.idiomatic: Full sets issued complete; partial sets at reduced rate.

sentences.zh: 正冬之會，稱束帛有差者，皆賜絹，五品已上五疋，六品已下三疋，命婦視其夫、子。

translations.literal: At the midwinter assembly, graded silk gifts: five pieces fifth rank and above, three sixth rank and below; commissioned wives followed husbands and sons.
translations.idiomatic: Midwinter court: fifth rank and above five silk pieces, sixth and below three; ennobled wives per husband or son.

sentences.zh: 倉部郎中倉部郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Granaries Bureau Director — one post, junior fifth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries Bureau Director: one post, junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司度大夫，咸亨復也。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo styled Grand Master of Measures; restored under Xianheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 662 Grand Master of Measures; restored in 670.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: One Bureau Assistant Director, junior sixth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: One Bureau Assistant Director, junior sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事三人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Three chief clerks, junior ninth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Three chief clerks, junior ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史九人，書令史二十人，計史一人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Nine document clerks, twenty writing clerks, one accounting clerk, four custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Nine document clerks, twenty writing clerks, one accounting clerk, four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌判天下倉儲，受納租稅，出給祿廩之事。

translations.literal: The Director and Assistant Director adjudicate granary stores, receipt of rent and taxes, and disbursement of salary grain.
translations.idiomatic: They managed granaries, collected rent and taxes, and issued salary grain.

sentences.zh: 凡中外文武官，品秩有差，歲再給之。

translations.literal: For all civil and military officials, by rank differences, grain issued twice yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials received grain rations twice yearly by rank.

sentences.zh: 乃置木契一百枚，以與出給之司合。

translations.literal: One hundred wooden tallies set up to match the disbursing office.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred wooden tallies coordinated disbursing offices.

sentences.zh: 諸司官人及諸色人應給食者，皆給米。

translations.literal: Officials and all categories entitled to food rations were given rice.
translations.idiomatic: All entitled officials and categories received rice.

sentences.zh: 凡致仕之官，五品已上及解官充侍者，各給半祿。

translations.literal: Retired officials fifth rank and above and those resigning to serve as attendants each received half salary.
translations.idiomatic: Retired fifth rank and above and court attendants received half pay.

sentences.zh: 即遷官者，通計前祿，以充後數。

translations.literal: If immediately transferred, previous salary counted toward the new allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Immediate transfers counted prior salary toward the new allotment.

sentences.zh: 凡都已東租納含嘉倉，自含嘉轉運以實京太倉。

translations.literal: All rent east of the capital paid into Hanjia Granary; from Hanjia transported to fill the capital Great Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Grain rent east of the capital went to Hanjia Granary, then to the capital Great Granary.

sentences.zh: 自洛至陝為陸運，自陝至京為水運，置使，以監充之。

translations.literal: From Luoyang to Shanzhou overland; from Shanzhou to capital by water; commissioners appointed, filled by supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang-Shanzhou by land, Shanzhou-capital by water; overseers served as commissioners.

sentences.zh: 凡王公已下，每歲田苗，皆有簿書。

translations.literal: From imperial princes downward, each year's crop records kept in ledgers.
translations.idiomatic: From princes down, annual crop records were registered.

sentences.zh: 凡義倉所以備歲不足，常平倉所以均貴賤也。

translations.literal: Charity granaries prepared for years of shortage; Ever-Normal Granaries equalized high and low prices.
translations.idiomatic: Charity granaries guarded against shortage; Ever-Normal Granaries stabilized prices.

sentences.zh: 禮部禮部尚書禮部尚書一員，正三品。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites — one post, senior third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites: one post, senior third rank.

sentences.zh: 隋舊。

translations.literal: An office inherited from the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: The office dated from the Sui.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為司禮太常伯，光宅改為春官尚書，神龍復也。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo Grand Constant Master of Rites; under Guangzhai Minister of the Spring Office; restored under Shenlong.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo: Grand Constant Master of Rites; Guangzhai: Spring Office Minister; Shenlong restored the title.

sentences.zh: 侍郎一員。

translations.literal: One Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: One Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 正四品下。

translations.literal: Senior fourth rank lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Senior fourth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 名因隨曹改易也。

translations.literal: The title changed with alterations to the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The title changed with bureau reorganizations.

sentences.zh: 尚書、侍郎之職，掌天下禮儀、祭享、貢舉之政令。

translations.literal: The Minister and Vice Minister administer ceremonial rites, sacrifices, and examination policies.
translations.idiomatic: They governed ceremony, sacrifice, and examination policy.

sentences.zh: 其屬有四：一曰禮部，二曰祠部，三曰膳部，四曰主客。

translations.literal: Subordinates four: Rites, Sacrifices, Provisions, Hosts and Guests.
translations.idiomatic: Four departments: Rites, Sacrifices, Provisions, Hosts and Guests.

sentences.zh: 總其職務，而行其制命。

translations.literal: They summarized duties and executed regulatory orders.
translations.idiomatic: They coordinated departments and carried out orders.

sentences.zh: 凡中外百司之事，由於所屬，皆質正焉。

translations.literal: All bureau matters under their jurisdiction were verified.
translations.idiomatic: All jurisdiction business was reviewed there.

sentences.zh: 凡舉試之制，每歲仲冬，率與計偕。

translations.literal: Examinations each year mid-winter, candidates generally with annual accounting envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Examinations convened mid-winter with the annual accounting envoys.

sentences.zh: 其科有六：一曰秀才，試方略策五條。

translations.literal: Six categories: first Xiucai, tested on five policy essays.
translations.idiomatic: Six tracks: Xiucai, five policy essays.

sentences.zh: 此科取人稍峻，貞觀已後遂絕。

translations.literal: This category's selection was strict; after Zhenguan it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: That demanding track ended after Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 二曰明經，三曰進士，四曰明法，五曰書，六曰算。

translations.literal: Second Mingjing; third Jinshi; fourth Mingfa; fifth Calligraphy; sixth Mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: Then Mingjing, Jinshi, Mingfa, Calligraphy, Mathematics.

sentences.zh: 凡此六科，求人之本，必取精究理實，而升為第。

translations.literal: For these six, candidates required thorough mastery of principle and fact before ranking.
translations.idiomatic: All six required true mastery before passing.

sentences.zh: 其有博綜兼學，須加甄獎，不得限以常科。

translations.literal: Broad learning required special selection; not limited to regular categories.
translations.idiomatic: Exceptional breadth earned special recognition outside ordinary tracks.

sentences.zh: 其弘文、崇文館學生，雖同明經、進士，以其資廕全高，試取粗通文義。

translations.literal: Hongwen and Chongwen students, though same categories, tested only for rough literary comprehension due to high patronage.
translations.idiomatic: Academy students sat the same exams but needed only basic textual grasp.

sentences.zh: 其郊社齋郎簡試，如太廟齋郎。

translations.literal: Suburban and altar fast-officer examination same as Grand Temple fast-officer.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban fast-officer tests matched Grand Temple rules.

sentences.zh: 其國子監大成十二員，取明經及第人聰明灼然者，試日誦千言，並口試，仍策所習業，十條通七，然後補充。

translations.literal: Twelve Great Completion posts in the Directorate; from brilliant Mingjing graduates reciting one thousand characters daily, oral exam, ten essays seven to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve Directorate Great Completion students: brilliant Mingjing graduates, thousand-character recitation, oral exam, seven of ten essays.

sentences.zh: 各授散官，依舊令于學內習業，以通四經為限。

translations.literal: Each granted nominal rank, continued academy study, four classics mastery required.
translations.idiomatic: Each received nominal rank and remained until four classics were mastered.

sentences.zh: 禮部郎中郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Rites Bureau Director — one post, junior fifth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Rites Bureau Director: one post, junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: One Bureau Assistant Director, junior sixth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: One Bureau Assistant Director, junior sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 隋曰儀曹郎，武德改禮部郎中員外，龍朔為司禮大夫司禮員外，咸亨復。

translations.literal: Sui: Ceremonial Affairs Director; Wude: Rites director and assistant; Longshuo: Grand and vice grand master of Rites; Xianheng restored.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Ceremonial Affairs; Wude Rites bureau; Longshuo grand masters; Xianheng restored.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從八品上。

translations.literal: Two chief clerks, junior eighth rank upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Two chief clerks, junior eighth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史五人，書令史十一人，亭長六人，掌固八人。

translations.literal: Five document clerks, eleven writing clerks, six ward captains, eight custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Five document clerks, eleven writing clerks, six ward captains, eight custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌貳尚書、侍郎。

translations.literal: The Director and Assistant Director assist the Minister and Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: They assisted the Minister and Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 舉其儀制，而辨其名數。

translations.literal: They propose ceremonial regulations and distinguish names and numbers.
translations.idiomatic: They drafted ritual codes and kept ceremony names straight.

sentences.zh: 凡五禮之儀，一百五十有二。

translations.literal: Five ceremonial categories: one hundred fifty-two rites in all.
translations.idiomatic: Five ritual categories comprised 152 ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 一曰吉禮，其儀五十有五；

translations.literal: First auspicious rites, fifty-five ceremonies;
translations.idiomatic: First, auspicious rites: fifty-five;

sentences.zh: 二曰賓禮，其儀有六；

translations.literal: second guest rites, six;
translations.idiomatic: second, guest rites: six;

sentences.zh: 三曰軍禮，其儀二十有三：四曰嘉禮，其儀五十；

translations.literal: third military rites twenty-three; fourth felicitous rites fifty;
translations.idiomatic: third, military: twenty-three; fourth, felicitous: fifty;

sentences.zh: 五曰凶禮，其儀一十有八。

translations.literal: fifth inauspicious rites eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, inauspicious: eighteen.

sentences.zh: 凡元日，大陳設於含元殿，服袞冕臨軒，展宮縣之樂，陳歷代寶玉輿輅，備黃麾仗，二王后及百官、朝集使、皇親，並朝服陪位。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day grand array at Hanyuan Hall; emperor in dragon robes and crown, palace music, dynastic jade chariots, yellow guard; empress dowagers, officials, envoys, kin in court dress.
translations.idiomatic: New Year's Day at Hanyuan Hall: emperor in full regalia, palace music, imperial chariots displayed, yellow guard drawn up; dowagers, officials, envoys, and kin in court dress.

sentences.zh: 大會之日，陳設如初。

translations.literal: On the great assembly day, the array as at the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The great gathering used the same arrangements.

sentences.zh: 凡冬至，大陳設如元正之儀。

translations.literal: Winter Solstice grand array like New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: Winter Solstice followed New Year's format.

sentences.zh: 其異者，無諸州表奏祥瑞貢獻。

translations.literal: The difference: no prefectural memorials of auspicious omens or tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces did not report omens or bring tribute.

sentences.zh: 凡元正、冬至大會之明日，百官、朝集使等皆詣東宮慶賀。

translations.literal: Day after New Year and Winter Solstice assemblies, officials and envoys congratulated the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The day after, officials and envoys congratulated the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 凡千秋節，禦樓設九部之樂，百官袴褶陪位。

translations.literal: On the Longevity Festival, nine-section music from the tower; officials in riding dress.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's birthday, nine-section music played; officials in informal dress.

sentences.zh: 凡京司文武職事，九品已上，每朔、望朝參。

translations.literal: Capital civil and military officials ninth rank and above attended on new and full moon.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials of ninth rank and above attended on the first and fifteenth.

sentences.zh: 五品已上及供奉官、員外郎、監察御史、太常博士，每日參。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above, palace attendants, vice directors, censors, Grand Harmony doctors attended daily.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above, attendants, vice directors, censors, and doctors attended daily.

sentences.zh: 凡諸蕃國來朝，皆設宮縣之樂及黃麾仗。

translations.literal: When foreign states came to court, palace music and yellow guard provided.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign courts received palace music and the yellow guard.

sentences.zh: 若蕃國使，則減黃麾之半。

translations.literal: Foreign envoys alone: yellow guard reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys alone received half the yellow guard.

sentences.zh: 凡冊皇后、太子、太子妃、諸王、諸王妃、公主，並臨軒冊命，陳設如冬、正之儀。

translations.literal: Investiture of empress, crown prince, consort, princes, princesses consort, princesses before the gallery, array like New Year and Winter Solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Investitures used the same display as New Year and Winter Solstice.

sentences.zh: 訖，皆拜太廟。

translations.literal: When finished, all paid homage at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Each rite ended with homage at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 凡祥瑞，皆辨其名物。

translations.literal: All auspicious omens: names and forms distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Every omen was identified by name and form.

sentences.zh: 有大瑞、上瑞、中瑞，皆有等差。

translations.literal: Great, upper, and middle auspicious omens, each graded.
translations.idiomatic: Omens ranked great, upper, and middle.

sentences.zh: 凡太陽虧，所司預奏，其日置五鼓五兵於太社，而不視事。

translations.literal: Solar eclipse: office reported in advance; that day five drums and five weapons at Grand Earth Altar; no business.
translations.idiomatic: Before eclipse, advance notice; five drums and weapons at the Grand Earth Altar; court suspended business.

sentences.zh: 百官各素服守本司，不聽事。

translations.literal: All officials plain dress at their offices, hearing no affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Officials wore plain dress and conducted no business.

sentences.zh: 過時乃罷。

translations.literal: Only after the time passed were restrictions lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Restrictions ended when the period passed.

sentences.zh: 月蝕，則擊鼓于所司。

translations.literal: Lunar eclipse: drums beaten at the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar eclipses: drums at the responsible office.

sentences.zh: 若五嶽、四鎮四瀆崩竭，皆不視事三日。

translations.literal: If Five Sacred Mountains, Four Guardians, or Four Watercourses collapsed or dried, no business three days.
translations.idiomatic: Ruined mountains or dried rivers: three days without business.

sentences.zh: 凡二分之月，三公巡行山陵，則太常卿為之副。

translations.literal: Equinoctial months, Three Dukes inspect tombs; Minister of Grand Harmony deputy.
translations.idiomatic: At the equinoxes the Three Dukes inspected tombs with the Minister of Grand Harmony.

sentences.zh: 凡百官拜禮，各有差。

translations.literal: Official bowing rites each had differences.
translations.idiomatic: Bows differed by rank and occasion.

sentences.zh: 致敬之士，若非連屬，應敬之官相見，或自親戚者，各從其私禮。

translations.literal: Gentlemen paying respect outside direct subordination, or among kin, followed private rites.
translations.idiomatic: Outside hierarchy or among kin, private ritual applied.

sentences.zh: 凡樂，有五聲、八音、六律、六呂，陳四懸之度，分二舞之節，以和人倫，以調節氣，以享鬼神，以序賓客。

translations.literal: Music: five tones, eight sounds, twelve pitch-pipes, four suspended sets, two dances — harmonize relations, regulate qi, serve spirits, order host and guest.
translations.idiomatic: Music used five tones, eight instruments, twelve pipes, four ensembles, two dances — harmonizing society, seasons, spirits, and guests.

sentences.zh: 凡私家不得設鐘聲。

translations.literal: Private households not permitted bells or chimes.
translations.idiomatic: Private households could not keep bells or chimes.

sentences.zh: 三品已上，得備女樂。

translations.literal: Third rank and above might keep female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above could keep female musicians.

sentences.zh: 五品女樂不得過三人。

translations.literal: Fifth rank female musicians not exceeding three.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: no more than three musicians.

sentences.zh: 居大功已上喪，受冊及之官，雖有鼓皆給銅印，有魚符之制。

translations.literal: Mourning for close relatives, officials with investiture — bronze seals issued; fish tally rules applied.
translations.idiomatic: Close mourning and invested officials received bronze seals; fish tally rules applied.

sentences.zh: 並出於門下省。

translations.literal: All were issued through the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: All of this was issued through the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 凡服飾尚黃，旗幟尚赤。

translations.literal: Generally, dress favored yellow and banners favored red.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow was the preferred color for dress; red, for banners.

sentences.zh: 天子、皇后、太子已下之服，事在《輿服志》也。

translations.literal: The robes of the Son of Heaven, the empress, the crown prince, and those below them are treated in the Treatise on Carriages and Robes.
translations.idiomatic: Regalia for the emperor, empress, crown prince, and those beneath them is set out in the Treatise on Carriages and Robes.

sentences.zh: 凡百僚冠笏、傘幌、珂珮，各有差。

translations.literal: Generally, the caps, tablets, parasols, curtains, and jade ornaments of all officials each had their grades.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' caps, court tablets, parasols, curtains, and jade ornaments all differed by rank.

sentences.zh: 常服亦如之。

translations.literal: Everyday dress followed the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress was graded the same way.

sentences.zh: 凡凶服，不入公門。

translations.literal: Generally, mourning dress was not worn into public offices.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning dress was not permitted inside government gates.

sentences.zh: 凡授都督、刺史階未入五品者，並聽著緋珮魚，離任則停。

translations.literal: Generally, those appointed regional commanders or prefects whose rank had not yet reached the fifth grade were all permitted to wear scarlet sash and fish tally; on leaving office, this ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders and prefects below fifth rank might wear scarlet sash and fish tally while in office, but not after they left.

sentences.zh: 凡文武官赴朝詣府，導從各有差。

translations.literal: Generally, civil and military officials attending court or visiting government offices each had their allotted escorts.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials attending court or visiting offices were each assigned escorts according to rank.

sentences.zh: 凡職事官薨卒，有賻贈、柳翣、碑碣，各有制度。

translations.literal: Generally, when a functional official died, there were funeral gifts, willow fans, and steles, each governed by fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When a functional official died, funeral gifts, willow fans, and steles were allotted by regulation.

sentences.zh: 祠部郎中祠部郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Sacrifices Bureau Director — one post, junior fifth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices Bureau Director: one post, junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司禋大夫，咸亨復。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo the title became Grand Master of Sacrificial Rites; under Xianheng it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed the post Grand Master of Sacrificial Rites; Xianheng restored the old title.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: One Bureau Assistant Director, junior sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: One Assistant Director, junior sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Two chief clerks, junior ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Two chief clerks, junior ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史五人，書令史十一人，亭長六人，掌固八人。

translations.literal: Five document clerks, eleven writing clerks, six ward captains, and eight custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Five document clerks, eleven writing clerks, six ward captains, and eight custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌祠祀、享祭、天文、漏刻、國忌、廟諱、卜筮、醫藥、僧尼之事。

translations.literal: The duties of the Director and Assistant Director were to administer sacrifices and offerings, astronomy, clepsydra timekeeping, national mourning days, taboo names in the ancestral temples, divination, medicine, and monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: The Director and Assistant Director oversaw sacrifice, astronomy, clepsydra timekeeping, national mourning days, temple taboos, divination, medicine, and Buddhist and Daoist clergy.

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀之名有四：一曰祀天神，二曰祭地祇，三曰享人鬼，四曰釋奠於先聖先師。

translations.literal: Generally, the names of sacrifice were four: first, sacrificing to the spirits of Heaven; second, offering to the spirits of Earth; third, feasting the spirits of the dead; fourth, presenting oblations to the former sages and former teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice fell into four categories: to Heaven, to Earth, to human spirits, and the libation offering to the sages and teachers of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 其差有三：若昊天上帝、皇地祇、州、宗廟為大祀。

translations.literal: Their grades were three: August Heaven, August Earth, the sovereign altars of the realm, and the Ancestral Temple were great sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: There were three grades: August Heaven, August Earth, the realm's sovereign altars, and the Ancestral Temple ranked as great sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 祀天地皆以祖宗配享。

translations.literal: In sacrificing to Heaven and Earth, the imperial ancestors were always joined in the offering.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven-and-Earth sacrifices always included the imperial ancestors as associated spirits.

sentences.zh: 日月星辰、社稷、先代帝王、嶽鎮海瀆、帝社、先蠶、孔宣父、齊太公、諸太子廟為中祀。

translations.literal: The sun, moon, stars, the altars of soil and grain, former dynastic emperors, the sacred peaks, guardian mountains, and river-lords, the imperial soil altar, the First Silkworm, Confucius, Duke Tai of Qi, and the temples of former crown princes were medium sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Medium sacrifices included the sun, moon, and stars; soil and grain; former emperors; sacred peaks, guardian mountains, and river-lords; the imperial soil altar and First Silkworm; Confucius and Duke Tai of Qi; and temples of former crown princes.

sentences.zh: 司中、司命、風師、雨師、眾星、山林、川澤、五龍祠等，及州縣社稷、釋奠為小祀。

translations.literal: The Director of the Center, the Director of Fate, the Master of Wind, the Master of Rain, the host of stars, mountains and forests, rivers and marshes, the Five Dragons Shrine, and the like, together with prefectural and county altars of soil and grain and libation offerings, were minor sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Minor sacrifices included the Director of the Center, Director of Fate, Masters of Wind and Rain, the host of stars, mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes, the Five Dragons Shrine, prefectural and county altars of soil and grain, and libation offerings.

sentences.zh: 大祀，皇帝親祭，則太尉為亞獻，光祿卿為終獻。

translations.literal: At a great sacrifice where the emperor personally performed the rite, the Grand Commandant served as secondary offerer and the Minister of Imperial Entertainments as final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor personally sacrificed at a great rite, the Grand Commandant was secondary offerer and the Minister of Imperial Entertainments final offerer.

sentences.zh: 若有司攝事，則太尉為初獻，太常卿為亞獻。

translations.literal: If officials performed the rite by proxy, the Grand Commandant was first offerer and the Minister of Grand Harmony secondary offerer.
translations.idiomatic: When officials performed the rite by proxy, the Grand Commandant was first offerer and the Minister of Grand Harmony secondary offerer.

sentences.zh: 凡大祀，散齋四日，致齋二日。

translations.literal: Generally, for great sacrifices there were four days of dispersed fasting and two days of strict fasting.
translations.idiomatic: Great sacrifices required four days of dispersed fasting and two days of strict fasting.

sentences.zh: 小祀，散齋二日，致齋一日。

translations.literal: For minor sacrifices, there were two days of dispersed fasting and one day of strict fasting.
translations.idiomatic: Minor sacrifices required two days of dispersed fasting and one day of strict fasting.

sentences.zh: 皆祀前習禮、沐浴，並給明衣。

translations.literal: Before every sacrifice they rehearsed the ritual and bathed, and bright garments were also supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Before each sacrifice participants rehearsed the rite, bathed, and received bright garments.

sentences.zh: 凡官爵二品已上，祠四廟。

translations.literal: Generally, officials of second rank and above maintained four ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank and above maintained four ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 五品已上，祠三廟。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above maintained three ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above maintained three ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 六品已下達于庶人，祭祖禰而已。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below down to commoners sacrificed only to the founder and the immediate forebear.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank and below, down to commoners, sacrificed only to the founder and immediate forebear.

sentences.zh: 凡國有封禪之禮，則依圓丘方澤之神位。

translations.literal: Generally, when the state performed the feng and shan rites, the spirit seats followed those of the Round Mound and Square Pond.
translations.idiomatic: When the state performed feng and shan, the spirit seats followed those of the Round Mound and Square Pond.

sentences.zh: 凡天下寺有定數，每寺立三綱，以行業高者充。

translations.literal: Generally, monasteries throughout the realm had fixed quotas; each monastery established three administrators, filled by those of highest religious attainment.
translations.idiomatic: Monasteries nationwide had fixed quotas; each appointed three administrators from among its most accomplished clergy.

sentences.zh: 諸州寺總五千三百五十八所，三千二百三十五所僧，二千一百二十二所尼。

translations.literal: Monasteries in all prefectures totaled five thousand three hundred fifty-eight: three thousand two hundred thirty-five for monks and two thousand one hundred twenty-two for nuns.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural monasteries numbered 5,358 in all—3,235 for monks and 2,122 for nuns.

sentences.zh: 每寺上座一人，寺主一人，都維那一人。

translations.literal: Each monastery had one abbot, one prior, and one chief disciplinarian.
translations.idiomatic: Each monastery had one abbot, one prior, and one chief disciplinarian.

sentences.zh: 凡僧簿籍，三年一造。

translations.literal: Generally, monastic registers were compiled once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Monastic registers were compiled every three years.

sentences.zh: 凡別敕設齋，應行道並官給料。

translations.literal: Generally, for vegetarian feasts established by special edict, monks who were to perform the rite also received government provisions.
translations.idiomatic: For edict-mandated feasts, participating clergy received government provisions.

sentences.zh: 凡國忌日，兩京大寺各二，以散齋僧尼。

translations.literal: Generally, on national mourning days, two great monasteries in each capital held dispersed fasting for monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: On national mourning days, two great monasteries in each capital held dispersed fasting for monks and nuns.

sentences.zh: 文武五品已上，清官七品已上皆集，行香而退。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of fifth rank and above, and pure offices of seventh rank and above, all assembled, offered incense, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials fifth rank and above, and pure offices seventh rank and above, assembled, offered incense, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 天下州府亦然。

translations.literal: Prefectures and districts throughout the realm followed the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: The same rule applied in prefectures and districts throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 凡遠忌日，雖不廢務，然非軍務急切，亦不舉事。

translations.literal: Generally, on distant mourning anniversaries, though regular duties were not suspended, unless military affairs were urgent no new business was undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: On distant mourning anniversaries, routine work continued, but unless military affairs were urgent, no new business was begun.

sentences.zh: 餘如常式。

translations.literal: In other respects the usual forms applied.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the usual forms applied.

sentences.zh: 膳部郎中膳部郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Provisions Bureau Director — one post, junior fifth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions Bureau Director: one post, junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司膳大夫，咸亨復也。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo the title became Grand Master of Provisions; under Xianheng it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed the post Grand Master of Provisions; Xianheng restored the old title.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: One Bureau Assistant Director, junior sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: One Assistant Director, junior sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Two chief clerks, junior ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Two chief clerks, junior ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史四人，書令史九人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Four document clerks, nine writing clerks, and four custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Four document clerks, nine writing clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌邦之祭器、牲豆、酒膳，辨其品數，及藏冰食料之事。

translations.literal: The duties of the Director and Assistant Director were to administer the state's sacrificial vessels, meat trays, and wine and food offerings, distinguish their grades and quantities, and manage ice storage and food supplies.
translations.idiomatic: They managed sacrificial vessels, meat trays, wine and food offerings, graded their quantities, and oversaw ice storage and food supplies.

sentences.zh: 主客郎中主客郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Hosts and Guests Bureau Director — one post, junior fifth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Hosts and Guests Bureau Director: one post, junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 隋曰司蕃郎，武德改主客郎中，龍朔為司蕃大夫，咸亨復。

translations.literal: Under the Sui the title was Director of Foreign Affairs; in Wude it was changed to Hosts and Guests Bureau Director; under Longshuo it became Grand Master of Foreign Affairs; under Xianheng it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Sui: Director of Foreign Affairs; Wude: Hosts and Guests Bureau Director; Longshuo: Grand Master of Foreign Affairs; Xianheng restored the old title.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: One Bureau Assistant Director, junior sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: One Assistant Director, junior sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Two chief clerks, junior ninth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Two chief clerks, junior ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史四人，書令史九人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Four document clerks, nine writing clerks, and four custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Four document clerks, nine writing clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌二王后及諸蕃朝聘之事。

translations.literal: The duties of the Director and Assistant Director were to administer the two former royal houses and the tribute and visits of the various foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: They managed the two former royal houses and foreign tribute and embassies.

sentences.zh: 二王之後，酅公、介公。

translations.literal: The descendants of the two royal houses were the Duke of Xi and the Duke of Jie.
translations.idiomatic: The two royal houses were represented by the Duke of Xi and the Duke of Jie.

sentences.zh: 凡四蕃之國。

translations.literal: Generally, there were the states on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were the states on the four sides.

sentences.zh: 經朝貢之後，自相誅絕，及有罪滅者，蓋三百余國。

translations.literal: After the era of tribute missions, through mutual slaughter and extinction, and through punishment and destruction, there were roughly more than three hundred states.
translations.idiomatic: Since the age of tribute, through mutual destruction and punitive extinction, more than three hundred states had disappeared.

sentences.zh: 今所存者，七十餘蕃。

translations.literal: Those surviving today numbered more than seventy foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: Only a little more than seventy foreign states remained.

sentences.zh: 其朝貢之儀，享宴之數，高下之等，往來之命，皆載於鴻臚之職焉。

translations.literal: The rites of tribute, the number of banquets, the grades of precedence, and the credentials for coming and going were all recorded in the duties of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute protocol, banquet numbers, precedence, and travel credentials were all set out in the duties of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 兵部兵部尚書兵部尚書一員，正三品。

translations.literal: Minister of War — one post, senior third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War: one post, senior third rank.

sentences.zh: 南朝謂之五兵尚書，隋曰兵部尚書。

translations.literal: The Southern Dynasties called this the Minister of the Five Armies; under the Sui it was the Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Dynasties called it Minister of the Five Armies; the Sui called it Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為司戎太常伯，咸亨復。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo the title was changed to Grand Constant Master of Arms; under Xianheng it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed it Grand Constant Master of Arms; Xianheng restored the old title.

sentences.zh: 侍郎二員。

translations.literal: Two Vice Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Two Vice Ministers.

sentences.zh: 正四品下。

translations.literal: Senior fourth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Senior fourth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司戎少常伯，咸亨復。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo the title was Vice Grand Constant Master of Arms; under Xianheng it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed it Vice Grand Constant Master of Arms; Xianheng restored the old title.

sentences.zh: 尚書、侍郎之職，掌天下武官選授及地圖與甲仗之政令。

translations.literal: The duties of the Minister and Vice Ministers were to administer the selection and appointment of military officers throughout the realm, and the regulations governing maps, armor, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: They governed military appointments nationwide and regulations on maps, armor, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 其屬有四：一曰兵部，二曰職方，三曰駕部，四曰庫部。

translations.literal: Their subordinates were four: first, the War Bureau; second, the Office of Posts; third, the Chariot Bureau; fourth, the Arsenal Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Four departments answered to them: War, Posts, Chariot, and Arsenal.

sentences.zh: 總其職務，而行其制命。

translations.literal: They summarized departmental duties and carried out regulatory orders.
translations.idiomatic: They coordinated the departments and executed regulatory orders.

sentences.zh: 凡中外百官之事，由於所屬，鹹質正焉。

translations.literal: Generally, the affairs of all officials within and without, coming under their jurisdiction, were all verified.
translations.idiomatic: All business under their jurisdiction, civil and military, was reviewed there.

sentences.zh: 凡選授之制，每歲集于孟冬。

translations.literal: Generally, the system of selection and appointment convened each year in the first month of winter.
translations.idiomatic: Military selection convened each year in early winter.

sentences.zh: 去王城五百里以上旬，千里之內以中旬，千里之外以下旬。

translations.literal: Within five hundred li of the capital, the first ten-day period; within a thousand li, the middle ten-day period; beyond a thousand li, the last ten-day period.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates within five hundred li of the capital reported in the first ten-day period; within a thousand li, the middle period; beyond a thousand li, the last period.

sentences.zh: 尚書、侍郎分為三銓。

translations.literal: The Minister and Vice Ministers divided into three selection boards.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister and Vice Ministers divided selection into three boards.

sentences.zh: 尚書為中銓，侍郎分東西。

translations.literal: The Minister headed the Central Board; the Vice Ministers divided into East and West.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister chaired the Central Board; the Vice Ministers headed the Eastern and Western Boards.

sentences.zh: 凡試能有五，五謂長垛、馬步射、馬槍、步射、應對。

translations.literal: Generally, there were five tested abilities; the five were long-butt shooting, mounted and foot archery, mounted lance, foot archery, and verbal response.
translations.idiomatic: Five abilities were tested: long-butt shooting, mounted and foot archery, mounted lance, foot archery, and interview.

sentences.zh: 互有優長，即可取之。

translations.literal: Whoever excelled in any of them could be selected.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who excelled in any one could pass.

sentences.zh: 較異有三。

translations.literal: There were three comparative distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: Three comparative distinctions were applied.

sentences.zh: 三謂驍勇、材藝及可為統領之用也。

translations.literal: The three were fierce bravery, skill and talent, and suitability for command.
translations.idiomatic: They were fierce bravery, skill and talent, and suitability for command.

sentences.zh: 審其功能，而定其留放，所以錄才藝、備軍國、辨虛冒、敘勳勞也。

translations.literal: They examined function and ability and decided retention or dismissal, thereby recording talent, preparing the army and state, distinguishing false claims, and ordering meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: By assessing ability they decided who stayed or went, recorded talent, strengthened army and state, exposed fraud, and ranked merit.

sentences.zh: 然後據其資勞，量為注擬。

translations.literal: Then, according to seniority and service, appointments were measured and proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Then, by seniority and service, proposed appointments were matched.

sentences.zh: 五品已上送中書門下，六品已下量資註定。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above were sent to the Secretariat and Chancellery; sixth rank and below were assigned by measured qualification.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above went to the Secretariat and Chancellery; sixth rank and below were assigned by qualification.

sentences.zh: 其在軍鎮要籍，不得赴選，委節度使銓試其等第申省。

translations.literal: Those on critical military registers in garrison commands could not attend selection; the military commissioner was entrusted to test their grades and report to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Officers on critical garrison registers could not attend central selection; the military commissioner tested them and reported their grades.

sentences.zh: 凡官階注擬團甲進甲，皆如吏部之制。

translations.literal: Generally, the compilation of proposed rank assignments, board rosters, and submitted rosters all followed the Ministry of Personnel's system.
translations.idiomatic: Proposed appointments, board rosters, and submitted rosters followed Ministry of Personnel rules.

sentences.zh: 凡大選，終於季春之月，所以約資敘之淺深，審才略之優劣，軍國之用在焉。

translations.literal: Generally, the great selection ended in the last month of spring, thereby gauging the depth of seniority, judging the superiority or inferiority of talent and strategy, for the needs of army and state lay therein.
translations.idiomatic: The great selection ended in late spring, weighing seniority, talent, and strategy for the needs of army and state.

sentences.zh: 兵部郎中郎中二員，從五品上。

translations.literal: War Bureau Director — two posts, junior fifth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: War Bureau Director: two posts, junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司戎大夫，咸亨復也。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo the title became Grand Master of Arms; under Xianheng it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed the post Grand Master of Arms; Xianheng restored the old title.

sentences.zh: 員外郎二人，從六品上。

translations.literal: Two Bureau Assistant Directors, junior sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Two Assistant Directors, junior sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事四人，從八品下。

translations.literal: Four chief clerks, junior eighth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: Four chief clerks, junior eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 令史三十人，書令史六十人，亭長八人，掌固十二人。

translations.literal: Thirty document clerks, sixty writing clerks, eight ward captains, and twelve custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty document clerks, sixty writing clerks, eight ward captains, and twelve custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中一員掌判帳及天下武官之階品，衛府之名數。

translations.literal: One Director adjudicated registers and the ranks of military officers throughout the realm, and the quotas of guard offices.
translations.idiomatic: One Director managed registers, military ranks nationwide, and guard-office quotas.

sentences.zh: 凡敘階有二十九。

translations.literal: Generally, there were twenty-nine grades in ordering rank.
translations.idiomatic: Rank ordering comprised twenty-nine grades.

sentences.zh: 將軍之階。

translations.literal: These were the grades of generals.
translations.idiomatic: They were the grades of generals.

sentences.zh: 具於敘目。

translations.literal: They are set out in the roster of ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Details appear in the roster of ranks.

sentences.zh: 凡敘階之法，一如文散官之制。

translations.literal: Generally, the method of ordering rank followed exactly the system for honorary civil offices.
translations.idiomatic: Rank ordering followed the same rules as honorary civil offices.

sentences.zh: 凡天下之府，五百九十有四，有上中下，並載于諸衛之職。

translations.literal: Generally, guard headquarters throughout the realm numbered five hundred ninety-four, with upper, middle, and lower grades; all are recorded in the duties of the guard offices.
translations.idiomatic: Guard headquarters nationwide numbered 594, graded upper, middle, and lower, as recorded in the guard regulations.

sentences.zh: 凡應宿衛官，各從番第。

translations.literal: Generally, officers on palace-guard duty each followed the rotation schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Palace-guard officers each followed the rotation schedule.

sentences.zh: 凡千牛備身左右及太子千牛備身，皆取三品已上職事官子孫，四品清官子，儀容端正，武藝可稱者充。

translations.literal: Generally, the Thousand-Ox Bodyguards Left and Right and the crown prince's Thousand-Ox Bodyguards were all filled from descendants of functional officials of third rank and above, and sons of fourth-rank pure offices, provided their bearing was upright and their martial skill commendable.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-Ox Bodyguards and the crown prince's Thousand-Ox Bodyguards were drawn from descendants of third-rank functional officials and sons of fourth-rank pure offices with upright bearing and proven martial skill.

sentences.zh: 五考，本司隨文武簡試聽選。

translations.literal: After five performance reviews, their home office tested them according to civil or military standards and permitted them to enter selection.
translations.idiomatic: After five reviews, their home office tested them by civil or military standards and allowed them to enter selection.

sentences.zh: 四品，謂諸司侍郎、左右庶子也。

translations.literal: Fourth rank means vice ministers of the various bureaus and the Left and Right Subscribers of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank meant bureau vice ministers and the Left and Right Subscribers of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 凡殿中省進馬，取左右衛三衛及高廕，簡儀容可觀者補充，簡試同千牛例。

translations.literal: Generally, for presenting horses to the Palace Affairs Office, candidates were taken from the Three Guards of the Left and Right Guard and from high noble lineage; those with presentable bearing were appointed, and testing followed the Thousand-Ox precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Affairs Office selected presentable candidates from the Left and Right Guard Three Guards and high noble lineage, testing them as with the Thousand-Ox Bodyguards.

sentences.zh: 僕寺進馬，亦如之。

translations.literal: Presenting horses to the Palace Service followed the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Service followed the same rule for presenting horses.

sentences.zh: 五品已下、七品已上，五年，多至八年，年滿簡送吏部。

translations.literal: For fifth rank and below and seventh rank and above, the term was five years, and in many cases up to eight years; when the term was complete they were screened and sent to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Officers from seventh rank up to below fifth rank served five years, often up to eight; when the term ended they were screened and sent to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 不第者，如初。

translations.literal: Those who failed returned to their original status.
translations.idiomatic: Those who failed returned to their original status.

sentences.zh: 無文，聽以武選。

translations.literal: Without literary qualification, they were permitted to enter by military selection.
translations.idiomatic: Without literary qualification, they could enter through military selection.

sentences.zh: 凡左右衛親衛、勳衛、翊衛，及左右率府親勳翊衛，及諸衛之翊衛，通謂之三衛。

translations.literal: As a general rule, the intimate guards, merit guards, and auxiliary guards of the Left and Right Guards, the intimate, merit, and auxiliary guards of the Left and Right Rate Offices, and the auxiliary guards of the various guards are collectively called the Three Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The intimate, merit, and auxiliary guards of the Left and Right Guards and Rate Offices, together with auxiliary guards attached to other guards, were all classed as the Three Guards.

sentences.zh: 擇其資廕高者，為親衛，其次者，為勳衛及率府之親衛，又次者，為翊衛及率府之勳衛，又次者，為諸衛及率府之翊衛，又次者，為親王府之執仗乘。

translations.literal: Those of the highest hereditary privilege were made intimate guards; the next rank became merit guards and the Rate Office intimate guards; the next after that, auxiliary guards and Rate Office merit guards; the next, auxiliary guards of the various guards and Rate Offices; the lowest became bearers of arms and grooms in princes' households.
translations.idiomatic: Appointment followed hereditary rank: highest became intimate guards, then merit guards and Rate Office intimates, then auxiliary and Rate Office merit guards, then other guards' auxiliaries, and finally princely household arms-bearers and grooms.

sentences.zh: 量遠邇以定其番第。

translations.literal: Distance near and far was measured to fix the order of rotating duty.
translations.idiomatic: Rotating shifts were ordered according to how far men had to travel.

sentences.zh: 應補之人，周親已上有犯刑戮者，配令兵部上下。
