translations.literal: Among those eligible for appointment, if within five degrees of kin there was one who had suffered penal execution, they were assigned to be ranked up or down by the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates whose close kin within five degrees had been executed were referred to the Ministry of War for placement above or below the usual grade.

sentences.zh: 凡諸衛及率府三衛，貫京兆、河南、蒲、同、華、岐、陝、懷、汝、鄭等州，皆令番上。

translations.literal: As a general rule, for the Three Guards of the various guards and Rate Offices spanning Jingzhao, Henan, Pu, Tong, Hua, Qi, Shan, Huai, Ru, Zheng, and other prefectures, all were ordered to rotate to the capital for duty.
translations.idiomatic: Three Guards from guards and Rate Offices in Jingzhao, Henan, Pu, Tong, Hua, Qi, Shan, Huai, Ru, Zheng, and neighboring prefectures all performed capital rotation duty.

sentences.zh: 餘州皆納資。

translations.literal: The remaining prefectures all paid fees in lieu of service.
translations.idiomatic: Other prefectures commuted rotation with a cash payment.

sentences.zh: 凡左右衛之三衛，分為五仗。

translations.literal: As a general rule, the Three Guards of the Left and Right Guards were divided into five armed formations.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Guards' Three Guards were organized into five armed units.

sentences.zh: 凡王公已下，皆有親事帳內，限年十八已下，舉諸州率萬人以充之。

translations.literal: As a general rule, from princes downward, all had intimate attendants and household retainers, limited to those under eighteen, drawn from leading men of the various prefectures at ten thousand per prefecture to fill the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and nobles down the scale maintained intimate staff and household retainers under eighteen, levied at ten thousand men per contributing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 皆限十周年，則聽其簡試。

translations.literal: All were limited to ten-year terms, after which they were permitted selective examination.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years of service they could sit for selective review.

sentences.zh: 文理高者送吏部，其餘留本司，全下者退還本色。

translations.literal: Those high in literary and administrative skill were sent to the Ministry of Personnel; the rest remained with their original office; those wholly deficient were returned to their original status.
translations.idiomatic: Men of strong literary and administrative talent went to the Ministry of Personnel; others stayed in their bureau; complete failures reverted to civilian status.

sentences.zh: 凡兵士隸衛，各有其名。

translations.literal: As a general rule, soldiers attached to guards each had their own designations.
translations.idiomatic: Every guardsman under a guard corps bore a distinct service name.

sentences.zh: 左、右衛曰驍騎，左、右驍衛曰豹騎，左、右武衛曰熊渠，左、右威衛曰羽林，左、右領軍衛曰射聲，左、右金吾衛曰佽飛。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Guards were called Valiant Cavalry; the Left and Right Valiant Guards, Leopard Cavalry; the Left and Right Martial Guards, Bear Brigade; the Left and Right Awesomeness Guards, Forest of Feathers; the Left and Right Army-leading Guards, Sound of Archery; the Left and Right Golden Crow Guards, Flying Dagger.
translations.idiomatic: Service names ran: Left and Right Guards as Valiant Cavalry; Valiant Guards as Leopard Cavalry; Martial Guards as Bear Brigade; Awesomeness Guards as Forest of Feathers; Army-leading Guards as Sound of Archery; Golden Crow Guards as Flying Dagger.

sentences.zh: 東宮左、右衛率府曰超乘，左、右司禦率府曰旅賁，左、右清道率府曰直蕩。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace Left and Right Guard Rate Offices were called Superlative Charioteers; the Left and Right Imperial Transport Rate Offices, Traveler's Retinue; the Left and Right Clear Way Rate Offices, Straight Sweep.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's Guard Rate Offices used the names Superlative Charioteers, Traveler's Retinue, and Straight Sweep for transport and clear-way units.

sentences.zh: 總名曰衛士。

translations.literal: Collectively they were called guard soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Together they were known as guard soldiers.

sentences.zh: 皆取六品已下子孫，及白丁無職役者點充。

translations.literal: All were selected from descendants of sixth rank and below, and from commoners without corvée obligations, to fill vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: They were drawn from sons and grandsons of officials of sixth rank or lower and from unregistered commoners exempt from labor service.

sentences.zh: 凡三年一簡點，成丁而入，六十而免。

translations.literal: As a general rule, every three years there was a muster and review; upon reaching adulthood they entered service, and at sixty they were released.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years rolls were reviewed; men entered at adulthood and retired at sixty.

sentences.zh: 量其遠邇，以定番第。

translations.literal: Distance was measured to fix the order of rotating duty.
translations.idiomatic: Rotating duty again followed distance from the capital.

sentences.zh: 凡衛士，各立名簿。

translations.literal: As a general rule, each guard soldier had an individual register established.
translations.idiomatic: Each guardsman was entered on a personal roster.

sentences.zh: 其三年已來征防差遣，仍定優劣為三第。

translations.literal: For campaign, frontier defense, and special dispatch over the past three years, they were still graded into three ranks of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Service on campaign, garrison, or special assignment within three years was ranked in three grades of merit.

sentences.zh: 每年正月十日送本府印記，仍錄一道送本衛府。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the first month each year they sent the seal impression of their home prefecture, and also recorded one copy to send to their home guard office.
translations.idiomatic: Each year on the tenth of the first month they forwarded their prefecture's seal impression and a duplicate record to their guard headquarters.

sentences.zh: 若有差行上番，折沖府據簿而發之。

translations.literal: If there was special dispatch for rotation duty, the militia prefecture issued men according to the register.
translations.idiomatic: When guardsmen were detailed for rotation, the militia prefecture mobilized them from the roster.

sentences.zh: 凡差衛士征戍鎮防，亦有團伍。

translations.literal: As a general rule, when guard soldiers were dispatched on campaign, garrison, or frontier defense, they were also organized in companies and squads.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign, garrison, and frontier details likewise formed unit blocks.

sentences.zh: 其善弓馬者，為越騎團，餘為步兵團，主帥已下統領之。

translations.literal: Those skilled with bow and horse became Cross-Cavalry companies; the rest became infantry companies, commanded from the commander downward.
translations.idiomatic: Expert archers and riders formed Cross-Cavalry units; others formed infantry, all under a chain of command.

sentences.zh: 火十人，有六馱馬。

translations.literal: A fire of ten men had six pack horses.
translations.idiomatic: Each squad of ten had six pack animals.

sentences.zh: 若父兄子弟，不並遣之。

translations.literal: If father, elder brother, and younger kinsmen served together, they were not all sent on the same assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Father–son or brother pairs were not deployed on the same mission.

sentences.zh: 若祖父母老疾，家無兼丁，免征行及番上。

translations.literal: If grandparents were aged or ill and the household lacked a second able man, campaign duty and capital rotation were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Households with elderly or sick grandparents and no spare laborer were excused from campaign and rotation.

sentences.zh: 其居常則皆習射，唱大角歌。

translations.literal: In ordinary times they all practiced archery and sang the Great Horn song.
translations.idiomatic: In peacetime they drilled in archery and sang the Great Horn chant.

sentences.zh: 番集之日，府官率而課試。

translations.literal: On the day the rotation assembled, prefectural officials led them and tested their skills.
translations.idiomatic: When rotation cohorts mustered, prefectural officers supervised examination.

sentences.zh: 凡左、右金吾衛，有角手，諸衛有駑手，左、右羽林軍有飛騎及左右萬騎、彍騎。

translations.literal: As a general rule, the Left and Right Golden Crow Guards had horn players; the various guards had crossbow handlers; the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Army had Flying Cavalry and the Left and Right Ten Thousand Riders and Expansion Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Crow Guards fielded horn players; other guards crossbowmen; the Forest of Feathers Army flying cavalry and ten-thousand-rider units.

sentences.zh: 天下諸軍，有健兒。

translations.literal: Armies throughout the realm had stalwart youths.
translations.idiomatic: Every circuit maintained registered stalwart troops.

sentences.zh: 皆定其名籍，每季上中書、門下。

translations.literal: All had fixed registers of names; each quarter they reported to the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Registers were updated quarterly for the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 凡關內，有團結兵，秦、成、岷、渭、河、蘭六州，有高麗羌兵。

translations.literal: As a general rule, within the passes there were mustered militia; in Qin, Cheng, Min, Wei, He, and Lan six prefectures there were Goguryeo and Qiang troops.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the frontier passes stood mustered militia; six western prefectures also kept Goguryeo and Qiang auxiliaries.

sentences.zh: 黎、雅、邛、翼、茂五州，有鎮防團結兵。

translations.literal: In Li, Ya, Qiong, Yi, and Mao five prefectures there were garrison-defense mustered militia.
translations.idiomatic: Five southwestern prefectures maintained garrison militia.

sentences.zh: 天下諸州差失，募取戶殷丁多，人材驍勇，選前資官勳官部分強明堪統攝者，節級擢補主帥以領之。

translations.literal: Whenever prefectures fell short, they recruited from households rich in adult males, selecting men of fierce courage, and from former officials and merit officers chose the forceful and clear-sighted capable of command, promoting them by grades to lead as commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Shortfalls were filled by levying sturdy men from wealthy households and appointing experienced officers of proven leadership in graded ranks.

sentences.zh: 其義征者，別為行伍，不入募人之營。

translations.literal: Those levied for righteous campaign were formed into separate companies and did not enter the recruited camps.
translations.idiomatic: Volunteers for righteous expeditions formed separate units outside recruitment camps.

sentences.zh: 凡軍行器物，皆於當州分給之。

translations.literal: As a general rule, campaign equipment was all distributed from the prefecture where troops served.
translations.idiomatic: Field gear was issued by the operating prefecture.

sentences.zh: 如不足，以自備，貧富必以均焉。

translations.literal: If insufficient, men supplied their own, and rich and poor had to share the burden equally.
translations.idiomatic: Shortfalls were self-supplied, with equal obligation on rich and poor.

sentences.zh: 凡諸州軍府應行兵之名簿，器物之多少，皆申兵部。

translations.literal: As a general rule, registers of troops to be mobilized and quantities of equipment from every prefecture and army office were all reported to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and army offices reported mobilization rolls and equipment counts to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 軍散之日，亦錄其存亡多少，以申而勘會之。

translations.literal: On the day armies dispersed, they also recorded survivors and losses and reported for audit and reconciliation.
translations.idiomatic: When troops demobilized, surviving and lost men and materiel were reconciled with the ministry.

sentences.zh: 凡諸道回兵糧Я之物，衣資之費，皆令所在州縣分而給之。

translations.literal: As a general rule, grain, transport goods, and clothing expenses for returning soldiers on every circuit were all ordered to be distributed by the local prefecture and county.
translations.idiomatic: Grain, transport supplies, and clothing costs for homeward columns were apportioned by local counties and prefectures.

sentences.zh: 郎中一人掌判簿，以總軍戎差遣之名數。

translations.literal: One director handled ledger review and totaled the numbers of military dispatch by name.
translations.idiomatic: One bureau director audited registers and summed all troop movements.

sentences.zh: 凡天下節度使有八，若諸州在節度內者，皆受節度焉。

translations.literal: As a general rule, there were eight military commissioners throughout the realm; prefectures within their circuits all accepted their command.
translations.idiomatic: Eight frontier commissioners ruled their circuits; interior prefectures within those circuits obeyed them.

sentences.zh: 其福州經略使，登平州海軍，則不在節度之內。

translations.literal: The Fuzhou frontier commissioner and Dengping naval forces were outside commissioner jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou's frontier command and Dengping's navy lay outside those circuits.

sentences.zh: 節度名與所管軍鎮名，並見《地理志》也。

translations.literal: Commissioners' titles and the garrison towns they governed are all listed in the Geographic Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Names of commissioners and their garrisons appear in the Geographic Treatise.

sentences.zh: 凡親王總戎，曰元帥，文武官總統者，則曰總管。

translations.literal: As a general rule, when imperial princes commanded armies they were called marshals; when civil and military officials commanded jointly they were called overall commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Princes at the head of armies bore the title marshal; joint civil–military commanders were overall commanders.

sentences.zh: 以奉使言之，則曰節度使，有大使、副使、判官。

translations.literal: Speaking in terms of imperial commission, they were called military commissioners, with chief commissioner, vice commissioner, and adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial envoys they were military commissioners, with chief, vice, and adjutant.

sentences.zh: 若大使加旌節以統軍，置木契以行。

translations.literal: If the chief commissioner added signal banners and staff to command troops, a wooden tally was established for execution.
translations.idiomatic: A chief commissioner bearing imperial staff carried a wooden tally to mobilize troops.

sentences.zh: 凡將帥出行，兵滿一萬人已上，置長史、司馬、倉曹兵曹胄曹等參軍各一人。

translations.literal: As a general rule, when generals marched out, if troops numbered ten thousand or more, one chief secretary, marshal, granary, military, and education staff officer was placed for each.
translations.idiomatic: Generals leading ten thousand or more men received a full staff of secretaries and granary, military, and education aides.

sentences.zh: 五千人已上，減司馬。

translations.literal: At five thousand or more, the marshal was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: At five thousand the marshal post was omitted.

sentences.zh: 諸軍各置使一人，五千人已上置副使一人，一萬人已上置營田副使一人。

translations.literal: Each army placed one commissioner; at five thousand or more one vice commissioner; at ten thousand or more one garrison-colony vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Each army had a commissioner; five thousand added a vice; ten thousand added a garrison-colony vice.

sentences.zh: 每軍各有倉、兵、胄三參軍。

translations.literal: Each army had granary, military, and education staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: Every army included granary, military, and education aides.

sentences.zh: 其橫海、高陽、唐興、恆陽、北平等五軍，皆本州刺史為使。

translations.literal: The five armies of Transocean, Gaoyang, Tangxing, Hengyang, and Pingbei all had their prefect as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Transocean, Gaoyang, Tangxing, Hengyang, and Pingbei armies were headed by their prefects.

sentences.zh: 凡鎮，皆有使一人，副使一人。

translations.literal: As a general rule, every garrison had one commissioner and one vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Each garrison post had a commissioner and vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 萬人已上，置司馬、倉兵二曹參軍。

translations.literal: At ten thousand or more, marshal and granary and military staff officers were placed.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons of ten thousand added a marshal and granary and military staff.

sentences.zh: 五千人已下，減司馬。

translations.literal: At five thousand or below, the marshal was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Below five thousand the marshal was omitted.

sentences.zh: 凡諸軍鎮，每五百人置押官一人，千人置子總官一人，五千人置總管一人。

translations.literal: As a general rule, for every army garrison, every five hundred men had one escort officer; every thousand, one company chief; every five thousand, one overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons placed an escort officer per five hundred men, a company chief per thousand, and an overall commander per five thousand.

sentences.zh: 凡諸軍鎮使、副使已上，皆四年一替；

translations.literal: As a general rule, army garrison chief commissioners and vice commissioners and above all rotated every four years.
translations.idiomatic: Chief and vice commissioners of garrisons served four-year terms.

sentences.zh: 總管已下，二年一替；

translations.literal: Overall commanders and below rotated every two years.
translations.idiomatic: Officers below overall commander rotated every two years.

sentences.zh: 押官隨兵交替。

translations.literal: Escort officers rotated with their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Escort officers turned over with their units.

sentences.zh: 凡諸軍鎮大使、副使已下，皆有傔人，別奏以從之。

translations.literal: As a general rule, chief commissioners, vice commissioners, and below of army garrisons all had attendants; separate memorials were submitted to accompany them.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commissioners down the ranks traveled with personal attendants authorized by separate memorial.

sentences.zh: 凡幸三京，即東都南、北衛，皆置左、右屯營，別立使以統之。

translations.literal: As a general rule, when the emperor visited the three capitals, the southern and northern guards of the eastern capital each established Left and Right Encampments, with separate commissioners to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial visits to the three capitals required Left and Right Encampments for Luoyang's southern and northern guards under their own commissioners.

sentences.zh: 若在都，則京城亦如之。

translations.literal: If at the capital, the capital city did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same arrangement applied in the primary capital when the court was there.

sentences.zh: 凡大將出征，皆告廟授鉞，辭齊太公廟訖，不宿於家。

translations.literal: As a general rule, when great generals marched out on campaign, they announced at the ancestral temple and received the axe; having taken leave at Lord Tai's temple, they did not lodge at home.
translations.idiomatic: Generals departing for war announced at the ancestral shrine, received the battle-axe, bid Lord Tai's temple farewell, and did not sleep at home that night.

sentences.zh: 臨軍對寇，士卒不用命，並得專行其罰。

translations.literal: Facing the enemy in the field, if soldiers did not obey orders, they were permitted to punish on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders in battle could punish disobedient soldiers summarily.

sentences.zh: 既捷，及軍未散，皆會眾而書勞與其費用，乃告太廟。

translations.literal: After victory, and while armies had not yet dispersed, they all assembled the troops and recorded merit and expenses, then announced at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After victory, before demobilization, commanders mustered the army, recorded rewards and costs, and reported to the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 元帥凱旋之日，皆使郊勞。

translations.literal: On the day the marshal returned in triumph, suburban congratulations were always performed.
translations.idiomatic: Triumphant marshals were welcomed with suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 有司先獻捷於太廟，又告齊太公廟。

translations.literal: The responsible offices first presented the victory at the Grand Temple, and again announced at Lord Tai's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Victory was reported first to the Grand Temple and again at Lord Tai's shrine.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一人掌貢舉及雜請之事。

translations.literal: One vice director handled tribute examinations and miscellaneous petitions.
translations.idiomatic: One vice director oversaw military examinations and miscellaneous petitions.

sentences.zh: 凡貢舉，每歲孟春，亦與計偕。

translations.literal: As a general rule, for tribute examinations, every year in early spring they also went up with annual reports.
translations.idiomatic: Military examinations each early spring accompanied the annual personnel review.

sentences.zh: 有二科：一曰平射，二曰武舉。

translations.literal: There were two categories: first, level archery; second, military examination.
translations.idiomatic: Two examination tracks existed: level archery and the military examination.

sentences.zh: 凡科之優劣，勳獲之等級，皆審其實而受敘焉。

translations.literal: As a general rule, the quality of each category and the grade of merit obtained were all verified in fact before appointment was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Examination grades and merit ranks were verified before conferral of office.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一人掌判南曹。

translations.literal: One vice director handled review of the southern bureau.
translations.idiomatic: One vice director managed the southern personnel ledger.

sentences.zh: 每歲選人，有解狀、簿書、資歷、考課。

translations.literal: Each year selected candidates had dissolution documents, ledgers, qualifications, and performance evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Annual selections relied on resignation certificates, dossiers, seniority, and evaluation records.

sentences.zh: 必由之以核其實，乃上三銓。

translations.literal: They had to pass through this process to verify truth, then ascend to the Three Boards.
translations.idiomatic: Only after verification here did cases go to the Three Boards.

sentences.zh: 進甲則署焉。

translations.literal: Those advanced to first grade were signed off.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates promoted to first grade received endorsement.

sentences.zh: 職方郎中職方郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Director of the Bureau of Appointments: one post, Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau of Appointments director: one position, fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司域大夫也。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo it was called Grand Master of Domains.
translations.idiomatic: During Longshuo the title was Grand Master of Domains.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，正六品上。

translations.literal: Vice director: one post, Sixth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: One vice director, sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Section chief: two posts, Ninth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Two section chiefs, ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史四人，書令史九人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Clerks: four; recording clerks: nine; custodians: four.
translations.idiomatic: Four clerks, nine recording clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌天下地圖及城隍、鎮戍、烽堠之數，辨其邦國都鄙之遠近，及四夷之歸化。

translations.literal: The duties of the director and vice director were to manage maps of the realm, city walls, garrison posts, and beacon towers, distinguish the distance of capitals and border towns, and the submission of the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Directors maintained maps, walls, garrisons, and beacon chains, measured distances among capitals and frontiers, and tracked barbarian submission.

sentences.zh: 凡五方之區域，都邑之廢置，疆埸之爭訟者，舉而正之。

translations.literal: As a general rule, for the regions of the five directions, the abolition or establishment of capitals and towns, and border disputes, all were raised and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: They adjudicated regional boundaries, changes to administrative seats, and frontier disputes.

sentences.zh: 凡天下上鎮二十，中鎮九十，下鎮一百三十五。

translations.literal: As a general rule, upper garrisons throughout the realm numbered twenty; middle garrisons ninety; lower garrisons one hundred thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: The empire counted twenty upper, ninety middle, and one hundred thirty-five lower garrisons.

sentences.zh: 上戍十有一，中戍八十六，下戍二百四十五。

translations.literal: Upper outposts numbered eleven; middle outposts eighty-six; lower outposts two hundred forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison outposts totaled eleven upper, eighty-six middle, and two hundred forty-five lower.

sentences.zh: 凡烽堠所置，大率相去三十里。

translations.literal: As a general rule, beacon towers were placed roughly thirty li apart.
translations.idiomatic: Beacon towers stood about thirty li apart on average.

sentences.zh: 其逼邊境者，築城置之。

translations.literal: Those pressing the border had walled forts built to place them.
translations.idiomatic: Along tight frontiers they were set in fortified towns.

sentences.zh: 每烽置帥一人，副一人。

translations.literal: Each beacon had one commander and one vice.
translations.idiomatic: Each beacon station had a commander and assistant.

sentences.zh: 凡州縣城門及倉庫門，須有備守。

translations.literal: As a general rule, prefectural and county city gates and granary gates required garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: City and warehouse gates required defensive guards.

sentences.zh: 駕部郎中駕部郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Director of the Bureau of Carriages: one post, Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau of Carriages director: one position, fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司輿大夫也。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo it was called Grand Master of Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: During Longshuo the title was Grand Master of Chariots.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一人，從六品上。

translations.literal: Vice director: one post, Sixth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: One vice director, sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事三人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Section chief: three posts, Ninth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Three section chiefs, ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史十人，書令史二十人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Clerks: ten; recording clerks: twenty; custodians: four.
translations.idiomatic: Ten clerks, twenty recording clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌邦國輿輦、車乘、傳驛、廄牧、官私馬牛雜畜簿籍，辨其出入，司其名數。

translations.literal: The duties of the director and vice director were to manage imperial carriages, vehicles, relay posts, stud farms, and registers of official and private horses, cattle, and mixed livestock, distinguishing receipts and issues and controlling the numbers by name.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw chariots, relays, pastures, and livestock registers for all public and private animals.

sentences.zh: 凡三十里一驛，天下驛凡一千六百三十九，而監牧六十有五，皆分使統之。

translations.literal: As a general rule, every thirty li there was one relay; relays throughout the realm totaled one thousand six hundred thirty-nine, and supervisory pastures sixty-five, all administered by dispatched commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li per relay post; one thousand six hundred thirty-nine relays and sixty-five pastures under regional supervisors.

sentences.zh: 若畜養之宜，孳生之數，皆載於太僕之職。

translations.literal: If suitable for breeding and numbers of increase, all were recorded in the duties of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Breeding suitability and foal counts belonged to the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 凡諸衛有承直之馬，凡諸司有備運之牛，皆審其制，以定數焉。

translations.literal: As a general rule, the various guards had horses for straight escort duty; the various offices had oxen for transport reserve; all examined the regulations to fix the quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Guards kept escort horses and offices transport oxen according to fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 庫部郎中庫部郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Director of the Bureau of Stores: one post, Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau of Stores director: one position, fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司庫大夫也。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo it was called Grand Master of Stores.
translations.idiomatic: During Longshuo the title was Grand Master of Stores.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Vice director: one post, Sixth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: One vice director, sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Section chief: two posts, Ninth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Two section chiefs, ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史七人，書令史十五人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Clerks: seven; recording clerks: fifteen; custodians: four.
translations.idiomatic: Seven clerks, fifteen recording clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌邦國軍州戎器、儀仗。

translations.literal: The duties of the director and vice director were to manage weapons and ceremonial regalia of the realm, armies, and prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Directors controlled arms and ceremonial equipment for the state, armies, and prefectures.

sentences.zh: 凡元正、冬至陳設，並祠祭喪葬所貢之物，皆辨其出入之數，量其繕造之功，以分給焉。

translations.literal: As a general rule, for New Year's and winter solstice displays, and objects contributed for sacrifices, funerals, and burials, all distinguished the numbers issued and received, measured the labor of repair and manufacture, and distributed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: They tracked issue and return of gear for seasonal displays, rites, and funerals, weighing repair costs before distribution.

sentences.zh: 刑部刑部尚書刑部尚書一員，正三品。

translations.literal: Ministry of Justice — Minister of Justice — Minister of Justice: one post, Third Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Justice. Minister of Justice: one position, third rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 隋初改都官尚書，又改為刑部。

translations.literal: At the start of Sui it was changed to Minister of the Capital Office, then again to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Early Sui used Minister of the Capital Office, later Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為司刑太常伯，光宅改為秋官尚書，神龍復也。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo it became Grand Constant Minister of Punishments; under Guangzhai it became Minister of the Autumn Office; under Shenlong it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed it Grand Constant Minister of Punishments; Guangzhai the Autumn Office Minister; Shenlong restored the old title.

sentences.zh: 侍郎一員。

translations.literal: Vice minister: one post.
translations.idiomatic: One vice minister.

sentences.zh: 正四品下。

translations.literal: Fourth Rank, Lower.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司刑少常伯。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo it was Vice Grand Constant Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Under Longshuo, Vice Grand Constant Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 尚書、侍郎之職，掌天下刑法及徒隸、勾覆、關禁之政令。

translations.literal: The duties of the minister and vice minister were to manage penal law throughout the realm and the policies for convict laborers, review, and pass control.
translations.idiomatic: The minister and vice governed national penal law, convict labor, case review, and frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 其屬有四：一曰刑部，二曰都官，三曰比部，四曰司門。

translations.literal: Its subordinate bureaus were four: first, Punishments; second, Capital Office; third, Accounts; fourth, Gateways.
translations.idiomatic: Four subordinate bureaus: Punishments, Capital Office, Accounts, and Gateways.

sentences.zh: 總其職務，而行其制命。

translations.literal: It summed their duties and executed their regulations and orders.
translations.idiomatic: It coordinated their work and enforced their rules.

sentences.zh: 凡中外百司之事，由於所屬，鹹質正焉。

translations.literal: As a general rule, matters of central and outer hundred offices, proceeding from their subordination, were all verified for correctness.
translations.idiomatic: All business of central and local offices was authenticated through the proper chain of command.

sentences.zh: 刑部郎中郎中二員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Director of the Bureau of Punishments: two posts, Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Two directors of the Bureau of Punishments, fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 隋曰憲部郎，武德為刑部郎中，龍朔改為司刑大夫。

translations.literal: Sui called them Directors of the Discipline Bureau; Wude restored Bureau of Punishments directors; Longshuo changed them to Grand Masters of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Sui used Discipline Bureau directors; Tang Wude restored Punishments directors; Longshuo renamed them Grand Masters of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 員外郎二員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Vice directors: two posts, Sixth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Two vice directors, sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事四人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Section chief: four posts, Ninth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Four section chiefs, ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史十九人，書令史三十八人，亭長六人，掌固十人。

translations.literal: Clerks: nineteen; recording clerks: thirty-eight; station chiefs: six; custodians: ten.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen clerks, thirty-eight recording clerks, six station chiefs, and ten custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌貳尚書、侍郎，舉其典憲，而辨其輕重。

translations.literal: The duties of the directors and vice directors were to assist the minister and vice minister, uphold the statutes, and distinguish severity and leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Directors assisted the ministers, applied the code, and weighed harsh and mild penalties.

sentences.zh: 凡文法之名有四：一曰律，二曰令，三曰格，四曰式。

translations.literal: As a general rule, names of written law were four: first, statutes; second, orders; third, regulations; fourth, formulas.
translations.idiomatic: Written law comprised four forms: statutes, orders, regulations, and formulas.

sentences.zh: 凡律，十有二章：一名例，二禁衛，三職制，四戶婚，五廄庫，六擅興，七賊盜，八斗訟，九詐偽，十雜律，十一捕亡，十二斷獄，而大凡五百條。

translations.literal: As a general rule, statutes had twelve chapters: first General Principles, second Forbidden Guards, third Official System, fourth Household and Marriage, fifth Stables and Storehouses, sixth Unauthorized Campaigns, seventh Robbery and Theft, eighth Assault and Litigation, ninth Fraud and Counterfeiting, tenth Miscellaneous Statutes, eleventh Capture of Fugitives, twelfth Trial and Sentencing — five hundred articles in all.
translations.idiomatic: The penal code held twelve chapters from General Principles through Trial and Sentencing, five hundred articles total.

sentences.zh: 令，二十有七篇，分為三十卷。

translations.literal: Orders numbered twenty-seven sections in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Administrative orders ran twenty-seven sections in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 第一至第七曰官品職員，八祠，九戶，十選舉，十一考課，十二宮衛，十三軍防，十四衣服，十五儀制，十六鹵簿，十七公式，十八田，十九賦役，二十倉庫，二十一廄牧，二十二關市，二十三醫疾，二十四獄官，二十五營繕，二十六喪葬，二十七雜令，而大凡一千五百四十六條。

translations.literal: First through seventh were Official Ranks and Posts; eighth Sacrifices; ninth Households; tenth Selection; eleventh Evaluation; twelfth Palace Guards; thirteenth Military Defense; fourteenth Clothing; fifteenth Ritual Regulations; sixteenth Insignia and Escorts; seventeenth Forms and Protocols; eighteenth Fields; nineteenth Tax and Corvée; twentieth Granaries; twenty-first Pastures; twenty-second Passes and Markets; twenty-third Medicine and Illness; twenty-fourth Prison Officials; twenty-fifth Construction; twenty-sixth Funerals; twenty-seventh Miscellaneous Orders — one thousand five hundred forty-six articles in all.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven order scrolls listed ranks, rites, taxes, granaries, passes, prisons, construction, funerals, and more — one thousand five hundred forty-six articles.

sentences.zh: 凡格，二十四篇。

translations.literal: As a general rule, regulations numbered twenty-four sections.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four sections of supplementary regulations.

sentences.zh: 式，三十三篇。

translations.literal: Formulas numbered thirty-three sections.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-three sections of procedural formulas.

sentences.zh: 以尚書、御史台、九寺、三監、諸軍為目。

translations.literal: They took the ministries, the Censorate, the nine courts, the three directorates, and the various armies as headings.
translations.idiomatic: Headings followed ministries, the Censorate, courts, directorates, and armies.

sentences.zh: 凡律，以正刑定罪。

translations.literal: As a general rule, statutes were used to fix punishment and determine guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes defined crimes and fixed punishment.

sentences.zh: 令，以設範立制。

translations.literal: Orders were used to set scope and establish institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Orders established institutions and administrative scope.

sentences.zh: 格，以禁違正邪。

translations.literal: Regulations were used to forbid violation and correct deviance.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations barred violations and corrected abuse.

sentences.zh: 式，以軌物程事。

translations.literal: Formulas were used to standardize objects and measure affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Formulas standardized materials and measured work.

sentences.zh: 乃立刑名之制五焉：一笞，二杖，三徒，四流，五死。

translations.literal: Thus five forms of punishment were established: first beating; second flogging; third penal servitude; fourth exile; fifth death.
translations.idiomatic: Five punishments stood: beating, flogging, penal servitude, exile, and death.

sentences.zh: 笞刑五，杖刑五，徒刑五，流刑三，死刑二。

translations.literal: Beating had five degrees, flogging five, penal servitude five, exile three, death two.
translations.idiomatic: Each beating and flogging grade had five levels; exile three; death two methods.

sentences.zh: 而斷獄之大典，有十惡、八議、五聽、六贓。

translations.literal: Yet the great canon of trial and sentencing had the Ten Abominations, Eight Privileges, Five Hearings, and Six Corruptions.
translations.idiomatic: Sentencing also invoked the Ten Abominations, Eight Privileges, Five Hearings, and Six Corruptions.

sentences.zh: 贖配之典，具在《刑法志》。

translations.literal: The canon of redemption and exile is fully set out in the Treatise on Penal Law.
translations.idiomatic: Redemption and commutation rules appear in the Treatise on Penal Law.

sentences.zh: 凡決死刑，皆于中書門下詳覆。

translations.literal: As a general rule, all decisions on capital punishment were reviewed in detail at the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Capital sentences required joint review by the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 凡死罪，枷而杻。

translations.literal: As a general rule, for capital crimes, cangue and fetters.
translations.idiomatic: Capital convicts wore cangue and fetters.

sentences.zh: 婦人及流徒，枷而不杻。

translations.literal: Women and those in exile or penal servitude wore cangue but not fetters.
translations.idiomatic: Women and exiles or convict laborers wore cangue only.

sentences.zh: 官品及勳散之階第七已上，鎖而不枷。

translations.literal: Official rank and merit-dispersed grades of seventh rank and above were chained but not caged.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of seventh rank or higher, and merit holders, were chained without cangue.

sentences.zh: 在京諸司，則徒已上送大理，杖已下當司斷之。

translations.literal: For offices in the capital, penal servitude and above went to the Court of Judicial Review; flogging and below were decided by the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: Capital offices sent servitude cases upward to the Court of Judicial Review; lesser punishments they decided themselves.

sentences.zh: 若金吾糾獲，亦送大理。

translations.literal: If seized by the Golden Crow Guard, they were also sent to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Cases apprehended by the Golden Crow Guard likewise went to judicial review.

sentences.zh: 凡決大辟罪，在京者，行決之司，皆五覆奏；

translations.literal: As a general rule, for great capital crimes in the capital, the executing office always submitted five review memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Capital executions in the capital required five rounds of review memorials.

sentences.zh: 在外者，刑部三覆奏。

translations.literal: Outside the capital, the Ministry of Justice submitted three review memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces the Ministry of Justice filed three review memorials.

sentences.zh: 若犯惡逆已上，及部曲奴婢殺主者，一覆奏。

translations.literal: If the crime was rebellious sedition or above, or retainers or slaves who killed their master, one review memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion, great sedition, or a dependent or slave killing a master required only one review.

sentences.zh: 凡京城決囚之日，減膳徹樂。

translations.literal: As a general rule, on days when prisoners were executed in the capital, meals were reduced and music withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Execution days in the capital mandated frugal meals and silenced music.

sentences.zh: 每歲立春後至秋分，不得決死刑。

translations.literal: Each year from after the Beginning of Spring until the autumn equinox, capital punishment was not to be decided.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment was forbidden from after Beginning of Spring through the autumn equinox.

sentences.zh: 大祭祀及致齋、朔望、上下弦、二十四氣、雨未晴、夜未明、斷屠月日及休假，亦如之。

translations.literal: Great sacrifices and days of fasting, new and full moons, first and last quarter, the twenty-four qi, unceasing rain, before dawn, meat-abstention months and days, and holidays were likewise forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: The same ban applied on sacrifice days, fasts, moons, seasonal nodes, rain, darkness, abstention days, and holidays.

sentences.zh: 凡犯流罪已下，應除免官。

translations.literal: As a general rule, for crimes of exile and below that warranted removal and dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Exile and lesser crimes could also bring dismissal from office.

sentences.zh: 當未奏，身死者，免其追奪。

translations.literal: If before memorial was submitted the person died, pursuit and confiscation were waived.
translations.idiomatic: If the offender died before memorial, posthumous stripping of rank was waived.

sentences.zh: 流移之人，皆不得棄放妻妾，及私遁還鄉。

translations.literal: Persons in exile were all forbidden to abandon wife or concubine, or to flee home in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles could not desert spouses or slip home secretly.

sentences.zh: 至六載，然後聽仕。

translations.literal: After six years they were then permitted to take office.
translations.idiomatic: After six years they might enter office again.

sentences.zh: 即本犯不應流而特配流者，三載已後聽仕。

translations.literal: If the original crime did not warrant exile but exile was specially assigned, after three years they were permitted to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Special exiles for lesser original crimes allowed office after three years.

sentences.zh: 其應徒則皆配居作。

translations.literal: Those who should serve penal servitude were all assigned to residence labor.
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude meant assigned labor where convicts resided.

sentences.zh: 凡禁囚，五日一慮。

translations.literal: As a general rule, imprisoned convicts were reviewed every five days.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners were inspected every five days.

sentences.zh: 凡鞫獄官與被鞫人有親屬仇嫌者，皆聽更之。

translations.literal: As a general rule, if the interrogating official and the person interrogated had kinship or enmity, both were permitted to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogators related to or feuding with defendants could recuse themselves.

sentences.zh: 凡在京諸司見禁囚，每月二十五已前，本司錄其所犯及禁時月日，以報刑部，凡國有赦宥之事，先集囚徒于闕下，命衛尉樹金雞，待宣制訖，乃釋之。

translations.literal: As a general rule, for prisoners held by offices in the capital, before the twenty-fifth of each month the responsible office recorded the offense and the month and day of detention and reported to the Ministry of Justice; whenever the state granted amnesty, convicts were first gathered below the palace gate, the Commandant of the Guard erected the golden rooster, and after the proclamation they were released.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly capital prison reports went to the Ministry of Justice; amnesties gathered prisoners at the palace gate beneath the golden rooster before release.

sentences.zh: 都官郎中都官郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Director of the Capital Office: one post, Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Capital Office director: one position, fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改司僕大夫，咸亨復。

translations.literal: Longshuo changed it to Grand Master of Servants; Xianheng restored it.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed it Grand Master of Servants; Xianheng restored the old title.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Vice director: one post, Sixth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: One vice director, sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Section chief: two posts, Ninth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Two section chiefs, ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史發人，書令史十二人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Clerks: six; recording clerks: twelve; custodians: four.
translations.idiomatic: Six clerks, twelve recording clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌配役隸，簿隸俘囚以給衣糧藥療，以理訴競雪冤。

translations.literal: The duties of the directors and vice directors were to assign convict labor, register captive prisoners to supply clothing, grain, and medicine, and settle lawsuits to clear injustice.
translations.idiomatic: They assigned penal labor, provisioned prisoners, and resolved petitions of wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 凡公私良賤，必周知之。

translations.literal: As a general rule, free and bonded, public and private, all had to be fully known.
translations.idiomatic: They tracked free and bonded status across public and private registers.

sentences.zh: 凡反逆相坐，沒其家為官奴婢。

translations.literal: As a general rule, for rebellion and treason collective guilt, the household was confiscated and made palace slave women and men.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion and treason implicated the household, confiscated as palace slaves.

sentences.zh: 一免為蕃戶，再免為雜戶，三免為良民，皆因赦宥所及則免之。

translations.literal: First amnesty freed them as frontier households; second as miscellaneous households; third as commoners — all depending on what the amnesty reached.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesties could step slaves to frontier households, then miscellaneous households, then commoners.

sentences.zh: 年六十及廢疾，雖赦令不該，亦並免為蕃戶，七十則免為良人，任所樂處而編附之。

translations.literal: At age sixty and with crippling illness, even if the amnesty did not cover them, they were also freed as frontier households; at seventy freed as commoners, attaching wherever they wished.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-year-olds and the disabled became frontier households even outside amnesty scope; at seventy they became free commoners where they chose.

sentences.zh: 凡初被沒有伎藝者，各從其能，而配諸司。

translations.literal: As a general rule, those first confiscated who had skills were each assigned according to ability to the various offices.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled confiscated persons were assigned to offices matching their talents.

sentences.zh: 婦人工巧者，入於掖庭。

translations.literal: Women skilled in craft entered the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Craftswomen entered the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 其餘無能，咸隸司農。

translations.literal: The rest without ability all were attached to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Unskilled remainder went to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 比部郎中比部郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Director of the Accounts Bureau: one post, Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Accounts Bureau director: one position, fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司計大夫。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo it was Grand Master of Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Longshuo, Grand Master of Accounts.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Vice director: one post, Sixth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: One vice director, sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Section chief: two posts, Ninth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Two section chiefs, ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史十四人。

translations.literal: Clerks: fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen clerks.

sentences.zh: 書令史二十七人，計史一人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Recording clerks: twenty-seven; accounting clerk: one; custodians: four.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven recording clerks, one accounting clerk, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌勾諸司百僚俸料、公廨、贓贖、調斂、徒役、課程、逋懸數物，周知內外之經費，而總勾之。

translations.literal: The duties of the directors and vice directors were to audit salaries of all offices, public offices, fines and redemption, levies, convict labor, tax schedules, and arrears, fully knowing internal and external expenditures, and audit them in total.
translations.idiomatic: They audited salaries, fines, levies, labor, taxes, and arrears for every agency.

sentences.zh: 凡內外官料俸，以品第高下為差。

translations.literal: As a general rule, salaries of inner and outer officials differed by rank high and low.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer officials received salaries graded by rank.

sentences.zh: 外官以州縣府之上中下為差。

translations.literal: Outer officials differed by upper, middle, and lower prefecture, county, and district.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials' pay followed prefectural and county grade.

sentences.zh: 凡稅天下戶錢，以充州縣官月料，皆分公廨本錢之利。

translations.literal: As a general rule, household tax money throughout the realm supplied monthly salaries of prefectural and county officials, all from interest on public office capital.
translations.idiomatic: Household taxes funded local officials' monthly pay from interest on office capital funds.

sentences.zh: 羈縻州所補漢官，給以當土之物。

translations.literal: Han officials appointed in loose-rein prefectures received local products.
translations.idiomatic: Han officials in loose-rein prefectures were paid in native goods.

sentences.zh: 關監之官，以品第為差。

translations.literal: Pass and market officials differed by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Pass and market officers were paid by rank grade.

sentences.zh: 其給以年支輕貨。

translations.literal: They were supplied with lightweight goods on an annual basis.
translations.idiomatic: They received lightweight annual goods as salary.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍司馬，判官俸祿，同京官。

translations.literal: Garrison army marshals and adjutants received salary equal to capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: Army marshals and adjutants on campaign matched capital pay scales.

sentences.zh: 鎮戍之官，以鎮戍上中下為差。

translations.literal: Garrison and outpost officials differed by upper, middle, and lower garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier garrison pay followed garrison grade.

sentences.zh: 凡京師有別借食本，每季一申省，諸州歲終而申省，比部總勾覆之。

translations.literal: As a general rule, the capital had separate borrowed grain capital; each quarter they reported to the ministry; prefectures reported at year end; the Accounts Bureau audited in total.
translations.idiomatic: The capital borrowed grain capital quarterly to the ministry; prefectures reported yearly for Accounts Bureau audit.

sentences.zh: 凡倉庫、出內、營造、傭市、丁匠、功程、贓贖、賦斂、勳賞、賜與、軍資、器仗、和糴、屯牧，亦勾覆之。

translations.literal: As a general rule, granaries, receipts and issues, construction, hired markets, corvée craftsmen, work quotas, fines and redemption, tax collection, merit rewards, gifts, military supplies, weapons, regulated grain purchase, and garrison pastures were also audited.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries, construction, corvée, fines, taxes, rewards, military stores, and pastures fell under the same audit.

sentences.zh: 司門郎中司門郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Director of the Gateways Bureau: one post, Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Gateways Bureau director: one position, fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔曰司門大夫。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo it was called Grand Master of Gateways.
translations.idiomatic: Under Longshuo, Grand Master of Gateways.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Vice director: one post, Sixth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: One vice director, sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Section chief: two posts, Ninth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Two section chiefs, ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史六人，書令史十三人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Clerks: six; recording clerks: thirteen; custodians: four.
translations.idiomatic: Six clerks, thirteen recording clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌天下諸門及關出入往來之籍賦，而審其政。

translations.literal: The duties of the directors and vice directors were to manage registers and levies for all passes and gates of the realm for entry and exit, and examine their administration.
translations.idiomatic: They kept entry–exit registers and levies for every pass and gate.

sentences.zh: 凡關二十有六，為上中下之差。

translations.literal: As a general rule, passes numbered twenty-six, graded upper, middle, and lower.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-six passes ranked upper, middle, or lower.

sentences.zh: 京城四面關有驛道者，為上關。

translations.literal: Passes on the four sides of the capital with relay roads were upper passes.
translations.idiomatic: Capital passes on relay routes were upper grade.

sentences.zh: 余關有驛道及四面無驛道者，為中關。

translations.literal: Remaining passes with relay roads, and those on four sides without relay roads, were middle passes.
translations.idiomatic: Other relay-route passes and non-relay capital passes were middle grade.

sentences.zh: 他皆為下關。

translations.literal: All others were lower passes.
translations.idiomatic: All remaining passes were lower grade.

sentences.zh: 關所以限中外，隔華夷，設險作固，閑邪正禁者也。

translations.literal: Passes serve to divide inner and outer, separate Chinese and barbarian, set danger to make firm, and bar the crooked and uphold prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Passes divided empire from frontier, Han from barbarian, secured the terrain, and enforced prohibition.

sentences.zh: 凡關呵而不征，司貨賄之出入，其犯禁者，舉其貨，罰其人。

translations.literal: As a general rule, passes inspected but did not tax; they controlled the entry and exit of goods; violators had goods seized and persons fined.
translations.idiomatic: Passes inspected travelers rather than levying tolls; contraband was confiscated and offenders punished.

sentences.zh: 凡度關者，先經本部本司請過所，在京則省給之，在外則州給之。

translations.literal: As a general rule, those crossing a pass first requested a transit permit from their parent office; in the capital the ministry issued it; outside, the prefecture issued it.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers obtained transit permits from their home office — the ministry in the capital, the prefecture in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 而雖非所部，有來文者，所在亦給。

translations.literal: Yet even if not under their jurisdiction, if there was incoming documentation, the locality also issued one.
translations.idiomatic: Even outside jurisdiction, local offices issued permits when formal request documents arrived.

sentences.zh: 工部工部尚書工部尚書一員，正三品。

translations.literal: Ministry of Works — Minister of Works: one post, Third Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Works. The Minister of Works: one position at the third rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 南朝謂之起部。

translations.literal: The Southern Dynasties called it Qibu (Ministry of Construction).
translations.idiomatic: In the Southern Dynasties the office was known as the Ministry of Construction.

sentences.zh: 有所營造，則置起部尚書，畢則省之。

translations.literal: When there was construction, they set up a Minister of Construction; when complete, they abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever major building work was required, a Minister of Construction was appointed; when the project ended, the office was dissolved.

sentences.zh: 隋初改置工部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui, the Minister of Works was established in its place.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Sui dynasty the post was reorganized as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司平太常伯，光宅改為冬官尚書，神龍復舊也。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo it was Director of Works, Grand Master of Ceremonies; under Guangzhai, Minister of Winter Offices; under Shenlong the former titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: During Longshuo it bore the title Director of Works and Grand Master of Ceremonies; under Guangzhai it became Minister of Winter Offices; Shenlong restored the earlier names.

sentences.zh: 侍郎一員。

translations.literal: Vice-minister: one post.
translations.idiomatic: There was one vice-minister.

sentences.zh: 正四品下。

translations.literal: Fourth Rank, Lower.
translations.idiomatic: The rank was fourth grade, lower division.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司平少常伯。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo it was Vice Director of Works, Vice Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: During Longshuo the title was Vice Director of Works and Vice Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 尚書、侍郎之職，掌天下百工、屯田、山澤之政令。

translations.literal: The duties of the minister and vice-minister were to administer the government orders for all craftsmen, garrison farms, and mountains and marshes under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The minister and vice-minister oversaw national policy for artisans, military colony lands, and public mountains and wetlands.

sentences.zh: 其屬有四：一曰工部，二曰屯田，三曰虞部，四曰水部。

translations.literal: Its subordinate bureaus were four: first, Works; second, Garrison Colonies; third, Parks; fourth, Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: It had four subordinate bureaus: Works, Garrison Colonies, Parks, and Waterways.

sentences.zh: 總其職務，而行其制命。

translations.literal: It consolidated their duties and carried out their regulations and orders.
translations.idiomatic: It coordinated their responsibilities and enforced their rules and directives.

sentences.zh: 凡中外百司之事，由於所屬，鹹質正焉。

translations.literal: As for matters of all offices within and without, through their respective bureaus, all were verified and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: All business of central and local offices passed through the appropriate bureau for review and correction.

sentences.zh: 工部郎中郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Works Bureau — Director: one post, Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Works Bureau. Director: one position, fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司平大夫也。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo it was Grand Master of the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During Longshuo the title was Grand Master of the Directorate of Works.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Vice-director: one post, Sixth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: There was one vice-director at the sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Principal clerks: two, Ninth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Two principal clerks, ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史十二人，書令史二十一人，亭長六人，掌固八人。

translations.literal: Record clerks twelve, document clerks twenty-one, station chiefs six, custodians eight.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included twelve record clerks, twenty-one document clerks, six station chiefs, and eight custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌經營興造之眾務。

translations.literal: The director and vice-director managed the many tasks of planning and construction.
translations.idiomatic: The director and vice-director handled the full range of engineering and building projects.

sentences.zh: 凡城池之修浚，土木之繕葺，工匠之程式，咸經度之。

translations.literal: All repair and dredging of city walls and moats, maintenance of timber and earthworks, and standards for artisans were wholly planned and measured by them.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised moat and wall works, structural repairs, and the technical standards applied to craftsmen.

sentences.zh: 凡京師、東都有營繕，則下少府、將作，以供其事。

translations.literal: Whenever the capital or the eastern capital had building repairs, orders went down to the Palace Manufactories and the Directorate of Imperial Construction to supply the work.
translations.idiomatic: Capital and Luoyang maintenance projects were assigned to the Palace Manufactories and the Directorate of Imperial Construction.

sentences.zh: 屯田郎中屯田郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Garrison Colonies Bureau — Director: one post, Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison Colonies Bureau. Director: one position, fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司田大夫也。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo it was Grand Master of Field Administration.
translations.idiomatic: During Longshuo the title was Grand Master of Field Administration.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Vice-director: one post, Sixth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: One vice-director, sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Principal clerks: two, Ninth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Two principal clerks, ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史七人，書令史十二人，計史一人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Record clerks seven, document clerks twelve, accounting clerks one, custodians four.
translations.idiomatic: Seven record clerks, twelve document clerks, one accounting clerk, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌天下屯田之政令。

translations.literal: The director and vice-director administered the government orders for garrison colonies under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw national policy on military colony farming.

sentences.zh: 凡邊防鎮守，轉運不給，則設屯田，以益軍儲。

translations.literal: Whenever frontier garrisons could not be supplied by transport, colony fields were established to augment military stores.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier posts could not rely on supply lines, garrison farms were set up to increase grain reserves.

sentences.zh: 其水陸腴瘠，播種地宜，功庸煩省，收率等級，鹹取決焉。

translations.literal: Whether land was rich or poor by water or land, what crops suited the soil, whether labor was burdensome or light, and the grades of harvest yield — all decisions rested with them.
translations.idiomatic: They determined suitability of wet or dry land, appropriate crops, labor requirements, and harvest quotas.

sentences.zh: 諸屯田役力，各有程數。

translations.literal: Labor quotas for each colony had fixed schedules.
translations.idiomatic: Each colony's corvée labor was assigned a defined quota.

sentences.zh: 凡天下諸軍州管屯，總九百九十有二。

translations.literal: Under all military prefectures that administered colonies throughout the realm, the total was nine hundred ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: Nine hundred ninety-two colonies were administered by military prefectures empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 大者五十頃，小者二十頃。

translations.literal: Large ones were fifty qing; small ones twenty qing.
translations.idiomatic: Large colonies measured fifty qing; small ones twenty qing.

sentences.zh: 凡當屯之中，地有良薄，歲有豐儉，各定為三等。

translations.literal: Within each colony, where soil was good or poor and years abundant or lean, three grades were fixed for each.
translations.idiomatic: Each colony classified its land and annual yield into three grades.

sentences.zh: 凡屯皆有屯官、屯副。

translations.literal: Every colony had a colony officer and a deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Each colony was headed by a chief officer and an assistant.

sentences.zh: 凡京文武職事官，有職分田。

translations.literal: All civil and military officeholders in the capital had assigned duty fields.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials of both civil and military ranks held allotments of duty land.

sentences.zh: 京兆，河南府及京縣官，亦准此。

translations.literal: Officials of the Jingzhao and Henan prefectures and capital counties followed the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: The same applied to officials in Jingzhao, Henan, and the capital counties.

sentences.zh: 凡在京諸司，有公廨田，皆視其品命而審其分給。

translations.literal: All agencies in the capital with public office lands distributed shares according to rank and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Capital agencies with communal office fields allocated plots according to rank and status.

sentences.zh: 虞部郎中虞部郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Parks Bureau — Director: one post, Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Parks Bureau. Director: one position, fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司虞大夫。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo it was Grand Master of Parks.
translations.idiomatic: During Longshuo the title was Grand Master of Parks.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Vice-director: one post, Sixth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: One vice-director, sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Principal clerks: two, Ninth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Two principal clerks, ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史四人，書令史九人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Record clerks four, document clerks nine, custodians four.
translations.idiomatic: Four record clerks, nine document clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌京城街巷種植，山澤苑囿，草木薪炭，供頓田獵之事。

translations.literal: The director and vice-director managed planting in capital streets and lanes, mountain marshes and imperial parks, fuel and charcoal from plants, and fields for official stops and hunting.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw street plantings, imperial parks and wetlands, firewood and charcoal, and lands for official travel and hunts.

sentences.zh: 凡採捕漁獵，必以其時。

translations.literal: All gathering, fishing, and hunting had to observe the proper seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Harvesting, fishing, and hunting were permitted only in season.

sentences.zh: 凡京兆、河南二都，其近為四郊，三百里皆不得弋獵採捕。

translations.literal: For the two capitals, Jingzhao and Henan, within three hundred li of the near suburbs as the four outer districts, shooting, hunting, and gathering were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Within three hundred li of the inner and outer suburban zones of the two capitals, no hunting or foraging was allowed.

sentences.zh: 殿中、太僕所管閑廄馬，兩都皆五百里內供其芻槁。

translations.literal: Idle stable horses under the Palace Administration and the Court of the Imperial Stud supplied fodder within five hundred li of both capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Fodder for reserve horses of the palace and imperial stud was drawn from within five hundred li of both capitals.

sentences.zh: 其關內、隴右、西使、南使諸牧監馬牛駝羊，皆貯槁及茭草。

translations.literal: Horses, cattle, camels, and sheep of pasture offices in Guannei, Longyou, the western routes, and southern routes all stored hay and forage grass.
translations.idiomatic: Pasture offices on the western and southern routes maintained stores of hay and grazing fodder.

sentences.zh: 其柴炭木橦進內及供百官蕃客，並于農隙納之。

translations.literal: Firewood, charcoal, and timber for the palace and for officials and foreign guests were delivered during agricultural slack seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Fuel and timber for the court, officials, and tributary envoys were collected in the farming off-season.

sentences.zh: 水部郎中水部郎中一員，從五品上。

translations.literal: Waterways Bureau — Director: one post, Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Waterways Bureau. Director: one position, fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司川大夫。

translations.literal: Under Longshuo it was Grand Master of Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: During Longshuo the title was Grand Master of Rivers.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Vice-director: one post, Sixth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: One vice-director, sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Principal clerks: two, Ninth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Two principal clerks, ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 令史四人，書令史九人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Record clerks four, document clerks nine, custodians four.
translations.idiomatic: Four record clerks, nine document clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 郎中、員外郎之職，掌天下川瀆陂池之政令，以導達溝洫，堰決河渠。

translations.literal: The director and vice-director administered orders for rivers, streams, reservoirs, and ponds under Heaven, to guide and open ditches and canals and to dam or breach river channels.
translations.idiomatic: They regulated rivers, lakes, and irrigation works, opening canals and controlling embankments and breaches.

sentences.zh: 凡舟楫溉灌之利，鹹總而舉之。

translations.literal: All benefit from boats, irrigation, and drainage were wholly overseen and promoted by them.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised every advantage gained from shipping and irrigation.

sentences.zh: 凡天下水泉，三億二萬三千五百五十九。

translations.literal: Springs and waters under Heaven numbered three hundred twenty thousand three hundred fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The empire recorded three hundred twenty thousand three hundred fifty-nine water sources.

sentences.zh: 其在遐荒絕域，迨不可得而知矣。

translations.literal: Those in remote wastes and unreachable regions could not be known.
translations.idiomatic: Sources in distant borderlands lay beyond reliable survey.

sentences.zh: 其江、河，自西極達於東溟，中國之大川者也。

translations.literal: The Yangtze and Yellow rivers, reaching from the western extremity to the eastern sea, were the great rivers of the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze and Yellow River, running west to east, were China's principal waterways.

sentences.zh: 其餘百三十五水，是為中川。

translations.literal: The remaining one hundred thirty-five waters were medium rivers.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred thirty-five other rivers ranked as medium streams.

sentences.zh: 其又千二百五十二水，斯為小川也。

translations.literal: Another one thousand two hundred fifty-two waters were small streams.
translations.idiomatic: One thousand two hundred fifty-two lesser waterways counted as small streams.

sentences.zh: 若渭、洛、汾、濟、漳、淇、淮、漢，皆互達方域，通濟舳艫，從有之無，利於生人者也。

translations.literal: Such as the Wei, Luo, Fen, Ji, Zhang, Qi, Huai, and Han — all interconnected across regions, linking transport by boat from where goods existed to where they did not, benefiting the living.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei, Luo, Fen, Ji, Zhang, Qi, Huai, and Han linked regions by water transport, moving goods where they were scarce and sustaining the people.

sentences.zh: 凡天下造舟之梁四，河則蒲津、大陽、河陽，洛則孝義也。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm, boat bridges for building ships numbered four: on the Yellow River, Pujin, Dayang, and Heyang; on the Luo, Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Four pontoon bridges served ship traffic: Pujin, Dayang, and Heyang on the Yellow River, and Xiaoyi on the Luo.

sentences.zh: 石柱之梁四，洛則天津、永濟、中橋，灞則灞橋。

translations.literal: Stone-pier bridges numbered four: on the Luo, Tianjin, Yongji, and Zhongqiao; on the Ba, Baqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Four stone-pier bridges stood on the Luo (Tianjin, Yongji, Zhongqiao) and Baqiao on the Ba River.

sentences.zh: 木柱之梁三，皆渭川，便橋、中渭橋、東渭橋也。

translations.literal: Timber-pier bridges numbered three, all on the Wei: Bianqiao, Zhongweiqiao, and Dongweiqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Three timber-pier bridges crossed the Wei: Bianqiao, Zhongweiqiao, and Dongweiqiao.

sentences.zh: 巨梁十有一，皆國工修之。

translations.literal: Major bridges numbered eleven; all were maintained by imperial engineers.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven great bridges were maintained by the national works corps.

sentences.zh: 其餘皆所管州縣隨時營葺。

translations.literal: The rest were repaired as needed by the prefectures and counties in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Other bridges were maintained on schedule by local prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 其大津無梁，皆給船人，量其大小難易，以定其差。

translations.literal: At major fords without bridges, ferrymen were supplied; according to size and difficulty, their service grades were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Major fords without bridges were served by ferry crews, graded by the size and difficulty of the crossing.

sentences.zh: =門下省=秦、漢初，置侍中，曾無台省之名。

translations.literal: = Chancellery = Under Qin and early Han, attendant-inside was established; at first there was no name of terrace or department.
translations.idiomatic: = Chancellery = In Qin and early Han the attendant-inside was appointed, before the institution had the name of a department or 'terrace.'

sentences.zh: 自晉始置門下省，南、北朝皆因之。

translations.literal: From Jin the Chancellery was first established; Southern and Northern Dynasties all followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery was first established in Jin; the southern and northern courts kept the institution.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為東台，光宅改為鸞台，神龍復。

translations.literal: Longshuo changed it to the Eastern Terrace; Guangzhai to the Luan Terrace; Shenlong restored the former name.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed it the Eastern Terrace; Guangzhai the Luan Terrace; Shenlong restored the earlier title.

sentences.zh: 侍中侍中二員。

translations.literal: Attendant-inside: two posts.
translations.idiomatic: There were two attendants-inside.

sentences.zh: 隋曰納言，又名侍內。

translations.literal: Sui called them Remonstrating Speaker; also named attendants within.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui the title was Remonstrating Speaker; they were also called attendants within.

sentences.zh: 武德為納言，又改為侍中。

translations.literal: Under Wude they were Remonstrating Speakers; again changed to attendant-inside.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude era they were Remonstrating Speakers, then renamed attendants-inside.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改東台左相，光宅元年改為納言，神龍復為侍中。

translations.literal: Longshuo changed to Left Minister of the Eastern Terrace; in the first year of Guangzhai changed to Remonstrating Speaker; Shenlong restored attendant-inside.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo made them Left Ministers of the Eastern Terrace; Guangzhai year one restored Remonstrating Speaker; Shenlong returned the title attendant-inside.

sentences.zh: 開元元年改為黃門監，五年復為侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiyuan changed to Supervisor of the Yellow Gate; in the fifth year restored to attendant-inside.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan year one renamed them Supervisors of the Yellow Gate; year five restored attendant-inside.

sentences.zh: 天寶二年改為左相。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianbao changed to Left Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao year two renamed the office Left Minister.

sentences.zh: 至德二年復改為侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide again changed to attendant-inside.
translations.idiomatic: Zhide year two returned the title to attendant-inside.

sentences.zh: 武德定令，侍中正三品，大曆二年十一月九日，升為正二品。

translations.literal: Under the Wude statutes, attendant-inside was Third Rank, Upper; on the ninth day of the eleventh month of the second year of Dali, it was raised to Second Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Wude regulations ranked attendants-inside at third rank, upper grade; Dali 2/11/9 elevated them to second rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 舊制，宰相常于門下省議事，謂之政事堂。

translations.literal: By old practice, chancellors often deliberated at the Chancellery; this was called the Hall of Administration.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the chief ministers met in the Chancellery at what was called the Hall of Administration.

sentences.zh: 永淳二年七月，中書令裴炎以中書執政事筆，遂移政事堂於中書省。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Yongchun, Grand Counselor Pei Yan of the Secretariat, holding the brush of administration, moved the Hall of Administration to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchun 2/7: Secretariat chief Pei Yan, who wielded the administrative brush, moved the Hall of Administration into the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開元十一年，中書令張說改政事堂為中書門下，其政事印，改為中書門下之印也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kaiyuan, Grand Counselor Zhang Yue of the Secretariat changed the Hall of Administration to Secretariat-Chancellery; its seal of administration became the seal of Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 11: Zhang Yue renamed the Hall of Administration the Secretariat-Chancellery and changed its administrative seal accordingly.

sentences.zh: 侍中之職，掌出納帝命，緝熙皇極，總典吏職，贊相禮儀，以和萬邦，以弼庶務，所謂佐天子而統大政者也。

translations.literal: The duty of attendant-inside was to receive and issue the emperor's commands, illumine the imperial norm, oversee all official posts, assist in ritual, harmonize the myriad states, and support the multitude of affairs — the one who aids the Son of Heaven and governs great policy.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants-inside transmitted imperial orders, upheld the royal standard, oversaw the bureaucracy, aided ritual, harmonized the realm, and advised on governance — second only to the emperor in grand policy.

sentences.zh: 凡軍國之務，與中書令參而總焉，坐而論之，舉而行之，此其大較也。

translations.literal: All military and state affairs were jointly summarized with the Grand Counselor of the Secretariat; they sat and discussed them, then raised and executed them — this was the general principle.
translations.idiomatic: Military and civil affairs were decided jointly with the Secretariat chief: discussed in council, then enacted — that was the broad rule.

sentences.zh: 凡下之通上，其制有六：一曰奏抄，二曰奏彈，三曰露布，四曰議，五曰表，六曰狀；

translations.literal: For communication from below to above, the forms were six: first, memorial copy; second, impeachment memorial; third, bare report; fourth, deliberation; fifth, petition; sixth, statement;
translations.idiomatic: Six formats carried business upward: memorial copies, impeachments, open reports, deliberations, formal petitions, and statements;

sentences.zh: 皆審署申覆而施行焉。

translations.literal: all were reviewed, signed, reported back, and then implemented.
translations.idiomatic: each document was reviewed, endorsed, reported, and only then executed.

sentences.zh: 凡法駕行幸，則負寶而從。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage traveled, they bore the seals and followed.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial progress they carried the seals and accompanied the procession.

sentences.zh: 大朝會、大祭祀，則板奏中嚴外辦，以為出入之節。

translations.literal: At great court assemblies and great sacrifices, they announced the inner vigil and outer preparations on the board, setting the rhythm of entry and exit.
translations.idiomatic: At major audiences and sacrifices they sounded the board to mark inner vigil and outer readiness, regulating movement in and out.

sentences.zh: 輿駕還宮，則請解嚴，所以告禮成也。

translations.literal: When the carriage returned to the palace, they requested release from vigil, thereby announcing the rite was complete.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, they proclaimed the end of vigil to mark completion of the rite.

sentences.zh: 凡大祭祀，皇帝致齋，既朝，則請就齋室。

translations.literal: At great sacrifices, when the emperor entered abstinence, after the audience they requested he go to the abstinence chamber.
translations.idiomatic: During great sacrifices, after the court session they escorted the abstinent emperor to the fasting chamber.

sentences.zh: 將奠，則奉玉及幣以進。

translations.literal: When the offering was about to be placed, they presented jade and silks.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of offering they advanced jade and ritual silks.

sentences.zh: 盥手，則取匜以沃。

translations.literal: At hand-washing, they took the ewer and poured.
translations.idiomatic: For the ritual hand-washing they held the ewer and poured water.

sentences.zh: 洗爵，則酌罍水以奉。

translations.literal: At washing the cup, they ladled water from the jar and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: To rinse the wine vessel they drew water from the urn and offered it.

sentences.zh: 及贊酌泛齊，進福酒以成其禮焉。

translations.literal: When assisting in pouring the general libation, they presented the blessing wine to complete the rite.
translations.idiomatic: They assisted in pouring the preliminary libation and presented the auspicious wine to finish the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 若享宗廟，則進瓚而贊酌鬱酒以稞。

translations.literal: If offering at the ancestral temple, they advanced the libation cup and assisted in pouring the aromatic wine for the first libation.
translations.idiomatic: At the ancestral temple they bore the libation cup and helped pour the spiced wine for the initial offering.

sentences.zh: 既稞，則贊酌醴齊。

translations.literal: After the first libation, they assisted in pouring the clear wine.
translations.idiomatic: Following the first libation they assisted with the refined wine libation.

sentences.zh: 其餘如饗神祇之禮。

translations.literal: The rest followed the rites for feasting the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Other steps followed the standard rites for entertaining the deities.

sentences.zh: 藉田，則奉耒以贊事。

translations.literal: At the plowing ceremony, they presented the plow to assist in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: At the ceremonial plowing they held the plow to assist the emperor.

sentences.zh: 凡諸侯王及四夷之君長朝見，則承詔而勞問之。

translations.literal: When feudal lords and chieftains of the four directions came to audience, they received the decree and conveyed courteous inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When princes and foreign rulers attended court, they bore the imperial message and offered formal greetings.

sentences.zh: 臨軒命使，冊後及太子，則承詔以命之。

translations.literal: When the emperor at the hall appointed envoys, invested empresses or the crown prince, they received the decree to command it.
translations.idiomatic: For investitures and envoys announced from the throne, they received the edict and conveyed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 凡制敕慰問外方之臣及徵召者，則監其封題。

translations.literal: For edicts of comfort to officials abroad and those summoned, they supervised the sealing of the cover.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw sealing when imperial messages comforted distant officials or summoned them to court.
