sentences.zh: 若發驛遣使，則給其傳符，以通天下之信。

translations.literal: If dispatching post riders or envoys, they issued transit tallies so trust could pass throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When couriers or envoys were sent out, they provided relay credentials to secure communication across the empire.

sentences.zh: 凡官爵廢置，刑政損益，皆授之於記事之官。

translations.literal: All abolition or establishment of offices and ranks, and increase or decrease in punishments and government, were entrusted to the recording officers.
translations.idiomatic: Changes to offices, ranks, and penal policy were assigned to the record keepers.

sentences.zh: 既書於策，則監其記注焉。

translations.literal: Once written on the bamboo or wood record, they supervised the annotation.
translations.idiomatic: After entries were written on the chronicle, they supervised the annotations.

sentences.zh: 凡文武職事六品已下，所司進擬，則量其階資，校其才用，以審定之。

translations.literal: For civil and military posts of sixth rank and below, when the responsible office submitted nominations, they measured rank seniority and matched talent and use, to examine and fix the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: For appointments below sixth rank, they weighed seniority and merit against the nominee's ability before confirming the post.

sentences.zh: 若擬職不當，隨其優屈，退而量焉。

translations.literal: If the proposed post was unsuitable, according to strength or weakness they withdrew and reconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: If a nomination misfit the candidate, they sent it back for reassessment according to relative qualifications.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎門下侍郎二員。

translations.literal: Vice-minister of the Chancellery: two posts.
translations.idiomatic: There were two vice-ministers of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 隋曰黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Sui called them Vice-ministers of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui the title was Vice-minister of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為東台侍郎，咸亨改為黃門侍郎，垂拱改為鸞台侍郎，天寶二年改為門下侍郎，乾元元年改為黃門侍郎，大曆二年四月復為門下侍郎。

translations.literal: Longshuo: Vice-minister of the Eastern Terrace; Xianheng: Vice-minister of the Yellow Gate; Chuigong: Vice-minister of the Luan Terrace; Tianbao 2: Vice-minister of the Chancellery; Qianyuan 1: Vice-minister of the Yellow Gate; fourth month of Dali 2 restored Vice-minister of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Titles shifted from Eastern Terrace vice-minister to Yellow Gate, Luan Terrace, and Chancellery vice-minister through Longshuo, Xianheng, Chuigong, Tianbao, Qianyuan, and back under Dali 2.

sentences.zh: 武德定令，中書門下侍郎，同尚書侍郎，正四品上。

translations.literal: Under the Wude statutes, vice-ministers of the Secretariat and Chancellery, like vice-ministers of the Six Ministries, were Fourth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Wude law ranked Secretariat and Chancellery vice-ministers with ministry vice-ministers at fourth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 大曆二年九月敕升為正三品也。

translations.literal: An edict of the ninth month of the second year of Dali raised them to Third Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Dali 2/9 elevated them to third rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎掌貳侍中之職。

translations.literal: Vice-ministers of the Chancellery assisted the attendants-inside in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: They deputized for the attendants-inside.

sentences.zh: 凡政之弛張，事之與奪，皆參議焉。

translations.literal: Whether policy was relaxed or tightened, whether affairs were granted or denied, all were jointly deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: They joined in deciding every loosening or tightening of policy and every approval or rejection of business.

sentences.zh: 若大祭祀，則從升壇以陪禮。

translations.literal: At great sacrifices they ascended the altar with the emperor to assist in the rite.
translations.idiomatic: During major sacrifices they accompanied the emperor onto the altar.

sentences.zh: 皇帝盥手，則奉巾以進。

translations.literal: When the emperor washed his hands, they presented the towel.
translations.idiomatic: At the ritual hand-washing they offered the towel.

sentences.zh: 既帨，則奠巾於篚，奉瓠爵以贊獻。

translations.literal: After drying, they placed the towel in the basket, and presented the gourd cup to assist in the offering.
translations.idiomatic: They set the used towel in the basket and bore the gourd goblet for the libation.

sentences.zh: 凡元正、冬至天子視朝，則以天下祥瑞奏聞。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day and the winter solstice when the Son of Heaven held court, they reported auspicious omens from throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At New Year and winter solstice audiences they announced favorable portents from across the empire.

sentences.zh: 給事中給事中四員。

translations.literal: Gentlemen-in-attendance for Review: four posts.
translations.idiomatic: There were four gentlemen-in-attendance for review.

sentences.zh: 正五品上。

translations.literal: Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: The rank was fifth grade, upper division.

sentences.zh: 隋曰給事郎，置四員，位次門下侍郎。

translations.literal: Sui called them Attendants for Review; four posts, ranking below vice-ministers of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Sui titled them Attendants for Review — four posts, junior to Chancellery vice-ministers.

sentences.zh: 武德定令，曰給事中。

translations.literal: Under the Wude statutes, the name was gentlemen-in-attendance for review.
translations.idiomatic: Wude regulations used the title gentlemen-in-attendance for review.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為東台舍人，咸亨復。

translations.literal: Longshuo changed to Eastern Terrace secretaries; Xianheng restored the former title.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed them Eastern Terrace secretaries; Xianheng restored the original name.

sentences.zh: 給事中掌陪侍左右，分判省事。

translations.literal: They attended at the emperor's side, divided and decided provincial business.
translations.idiomatic: They served beside the throne and adjudicated matters for their assigned sections.

sentences.zh: 凡百司奏抄，侍中審定，則先讀而署之，以駁正違失。

translations.literal: For memorial copies from all offices, after the attendant-inside approved, they read them first and signed, to correct errors and violations.
translations.idiomatic: They read and countersigned memorials after the attendant-inside approved them, correcting mistakes.

sentences.zh: 凡制敕宣行，大事則稱揚德澤，褒美功業，覆奏而請施行；

translations.literal: When edicts were promulgated, for great matters they proclaimed virtue and praised achievements, reported back for approval, and requested implementation;
translations.idiomatic: Major edicts were read aloud with praise for virtue and merit, then resubmitted for approval before execution;

sentences.zh: 小事則署而頒之。

translations.literal: for small matters they signed and distributed them.
translations.idiomatic: minor ones they simply endorsed and issued.

sentences.zh: 凡國之大獄，三司詳決，若刑名不當，輕重或失，則援法例退而裁之。

translations.literal: For great cases of state, when the three offices judged in detail, if the charge did not fit or severity was wrong, they cited precedent, withdrew the case, and decided anew.
translations.idiomatic: In major trials, if sentencing was improper they invoked precedent and sent the case back for reconsideration.

sentences.zh: 凡發驛遣使，則審其事宜，與黃門侍郎給之；

translations.literal: When dispatching post riders or envoys, they examined the business and, with the vice-minister of the Yellow Gate, issued credentials;
translations.idiomatic: They vetted courier missions and, with the Yellow Gate vice-minister, issued travel documents;

sentences.zh: 其緩者給傳，即不應給，罷之。

translations.literal: for slow travel they issued transit passes; if issuance was not warranted, they canceled it.
translations.idiomatic: routine travel received relay passes; unjustified requests were denied.

sentences.zh: 凡文武六品已下授職官，所司奏擬，則校其仕曆淺深，功狀殿最，訪其德行，量其才藝；

translations.literal: For civil and military appointments of sixth rank and below, when the office submitted nominations, they checked length of service, merit ratings, inquired into conduct, and measured talent and skill;
translations.idiomatic: Below sixth rank they verified service records, merit scores, character, and ability when offices nominated candidates;

sentences.zh: 若官非其人，理失其事，則白侍中而退量焉。

translations.literal: if the man did not fit the office or reason failed the affair, they reported to the attendant-inside and withdrew for reassessment.
translations.idiomatic: misfits were reported to the attendant-inside and sent back for review.

sentences.zh: 若弘文館圖書之繕寫、讎校，亦課而察之。

translations.literal: They also examined and inspected copying and collation of books in the Hongwen Library.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised transcription and proofreading in the Hongwen Library.

sentences.zh: 凡天下冤滯未申及官吏刻害者，必聽其訟，與御史、中書舍人同計其事宜，而申理之。

translations.literal: For grievances unresolved and officials who oppressed the people, they had to hear their suits, together with the censor and secretaries of the Secretariat calculating the matter, and set it right.
translations.idiomatic: They heard unresolved wrongs and abusive officials jointly with censors and Secretariat secretaries and rectified the cases.

sentences.zh: 錄事錄事四人，從七品上。

translations.literal: Recording clerks: four, Seventh Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Four recording clerks, seventh rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 主事四人，從八品下。

translations.literal: Principal clerks: four, Eighth Rank, Lower.
translations.idiomatic: Four principal clerks, eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 令史十一人，書令史二十二人，甲庫令史七人，傳制八人，亭長六人，掌固十人，修補制敕匠五人。

translations.literal: Record clerks eleven, document clerks twenty-two, arsenal record clerks seven, message clerks eight, station chiefs six, custodians ten, artisans repairing edicts five.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included eleven record clerks, twenty-two document clerks, seven arsenal clerks, eight message clerks, six station chiefs, ten custodians, and five edict-repair artisans.

sentences.zh: 左散騎常侍左散騎常侍二人。

translations.literal: Left Regularly Attendant Cavalier: two posts.
translations.idiomatic: Two left regularly attendant cavaliers.

sentences.zh: 從三品。

translations.literal: Third Rank, Lower.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉置散騎常侍、侍郎，與侍中、黃門侍郎共平尚書奏事。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin established regularly attendant cavaliers and vice-attendants, who together with attendants-inside and vice-ministers of the Yellow Gate balanced and reported on Secretariat memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin created these posts to review Secretariat memorials alongside attendants-inside and Yellow Gate vice-ministers.

sentences.zh: 其後用人或雜，江左不重此官，或省或置。

translations.literal: Later appointments were sometimes mixed; east of the Yangtze this office was not valued, and it was sometimes cut or restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later the post was often filled irregularly; southern courts sometimes omitted or revived it.

sentences.zh: 隋初省散騎侍郎，置常侍四人，從三品，掌陪從朝直。

translations.literal: Early Sui abolished the vice-attendant cavalier and set four regular attendants, Third Rank, Lower, to attend and follow at court.
translations.idiomatic: Early Sui eliminated vice-attendants and appointed four regular cavaliers at third rank, lower grade, for court attendance.

sentences.zh: 煬帝又省之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang again abolished them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang of Sui abolished the posts again.

sentences.zh: 武德初，以為加官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude they were used as supplementary titles.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tang they served as honorary additions.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，置常侍二人，隸門下省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, two regular attendants were established, subordinate to the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan restored two regular cavaliers under the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 明慶二年，又置二員，隸中書省，始有左右之號，並金蟬珥貂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingqing, two more were added, subordinate to the Secretariat; then began the titles Left and Right, all with golden cicada and dangling marten.
translations.idiomatic: Mingqing 2 added two under the Secretariat, creating distinct Left and Right posts with golden cicada and marten insignia.

sentences.zh: 左常侍與侍中左貂，右常侍與中書令右貂，謂之八貂。

translations.literal: The left regular attendant with the left marten of the attendant-inside, and the right regular attendant with the right marten of the Grand Counselor — called the Eight Martens.
translations.idiomatic: Left cavalier paired with the attendant-inside's left marten and right cavalier with the Secretariat chief's right marten — the 'Eight Martens.'

sentences.zh: 龍朔為左侍極，咸亨復。

translations.literal: Longshuo: Left Attendant Ultimate; Xianheng restored.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed the left post Attendant Ultimate; Xianheng restored the old title.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年五月，升為正三品，加置四員。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Guangde, raised to Third Rank, Upper, and four posts were added.
translations.idiomatic: Guangde 2/5 promoted them to third rank, upper grade, and added four posts.

sentences.zh: 興元元年正月，左右各加一員。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xingyuan, one post was added on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan 1/1 added one cavalier to each flank.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年正月敕，依舊四員也。

translations.literal: An edict of the first month of the fourth year of Zhenyuan restored the former four posts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyuan 4/1 returned the establishment to four posts.

sentences.zh: 常侍掌侍奉規諷，備顧問應對。

translations.literal: Regular attendants attended, admonished, and remonstrated, standing ready for consultation and response.
translations.idiomatic: They served the throne, offering remonstrance and counsel on demand.

sentences.zh: 寶應二年敕，左右散騎常侍各置參官兩人，令自揀擇聞奏，參典亦置兩人，後省。

translations.literal: An edict of the second year of Baoying: each left and right regularly attendant cavalier might appoint two participating officials, chosen and reported by themselves; participating clerks were also set at two — later cut.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying 2 allowed each side two handpicked aides reported to the throne; the aide posts were later abolished.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫諫議大夫四員。

translations.literal: Remonstrating Grand Masters: four posts.
translations.idiomatic: Four remonstrating grand masters.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢曰諫大夫，光武加議字。

translations.literal: Under Qin and Han, Remonstrating Grand Master; Guangwu added the character for 'deliberate.'
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han used Remonstrating Grand Master; Emperor Guangwu added 'deliberation' to the title.

sentences.zh: 隋于門下省置諫議大夫七員，從四品下。

translations.literal: Sui placed seven Remonstrating Grand Masters in the Chancellery, Fourth Rank, Lower.
translations.idiomatic: Sui appointed seven remonstrators in the Chancellery at fourth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 武德四年敕置四員，正五品上。

translations.literal: An edict of the fourth year of Wude set four posts, Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Wude 4 fixed four posts at fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為正諫大夫，神龍復。

translations.literal: Longshuo changed to Regular Remonstrating Grand Master; Shenlong restored.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed them Regular Remonstrators; Shenlong restored the earlier title.

sentences.zh: 大曆四年敕只四員，正五品上。

translations.literal: An edict of the fourth year of Dali fixed only four posts, Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Dali 4 reaffirmed four posts at fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 龍朔七年三月敕，其諫議四員，內供奉不得為正員。

translations.literal: An edict of the third month of the seventh year of Longshuo: of the four remonstrators, inner attendants could not be regular posts.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo 7/3 barred inner attendants from holding regular remonstrator slots.

sentences.zh: 至貞元四年五月十五日敕，諫議分為左右，加置八員，四員隸門下為左，會昌二年十一月中書奏：隋于門下省置諫議大夫七員，從四品下。

translations.literal: To the edict of the fifteenth day of the fifth month of the fourth year of Zhenyuan, remonstrators were divided into left and right and eight posts were added — four subordinate to the Chancellery as Left; in the eleventh month of the second year of Huichang the Secretariat memorialized: Sui placed seven Remonstrating Grand Masters in the Chancellery, Fourth Rank, Lower.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyuan 4/5/15 split remonstrators into left and right with eight new posts; Huichang 2/11 noted Sui's seven fourth-rank remonstrators in the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 今正五品上。

translations.literal: Now Fifth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: They now held fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 自大曆二年門下中書侍郎升為正三品，兩省遂闕四品官。

translations.literal: From the second year of Dali, when Chancellery and Secretariat vice-ministers rose to Third Rank, Upper, both departments lacked fourth-rank posts.
translations.idiomatic: After Dali 2 promoted vice-ministers to third rank, neither department retained a fourth-rank office.

sentences.zh: 其諫議大夫望升為正四品下，分為左右，以備兩省四品之闕。

translations.literal: It was proposed that Remonstrating Grand Masters be raised to Fourth Rank, Lower, divided into left and right, to fill the fourth-rank gap in both departments.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial proposed elevating remonstrators to fourth rank, lower grade, in left and right wings to restore fourth-rank posts.

sentences.zh: 向後與丞郎出入迭用，以重其選。

translations.literal: Henceforth they would alternate in and out with directors and vice-directors, to weight the selection.
translations.idiomatic: They would rotate with bureau directors and vice-directors to raise the prestige of the appointment.

sentences.zh: 敕可之。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫掌侍從贊相，規諫諷諭。

translations.literal: Remonstrating Grand Masters attended, assisted, admonished, remonstrated, and instructed.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators attended the court, assisted in ceremony, and offered corrective counsel.

sentences.zh: 凡諫有五：一曰諷諫，二曰順諫，三曰規諫，四曰致諫，五曰直諫。

translations.literal: Remonstrance had five kinds: first, indirect remonstrance; second, compliant remonstrance; third, norm remonstrance; fourth, dedicated remonstrance; fifth, direct remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Five modes of remonstrance were defined: indirect, compliant, normative, earnest, and direct.

sentences.zh: 起居郎起居郎二員，從六品上。

translations.literal: Diary Officer: two posts, Sixth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Two diary officers, sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 古無其名，隋始置起居舍人二員。

translations.literal: Antiquity had no such name; Sui first established two Diary Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: The title was new; Sui first appointed two diary secretaries.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年省起居舍人，移其職于門下，置起居郎二員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan the Diary Secretaries were abolished and their duties moved to the Chancellery, with two Diary Officers established.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 2 abolished diary secretaries and assigned their work to two Chancellery diary officers.

sentences.zh: 明慶中又置起居舍人，始與起居郎分在左右。

translations.literal: In Mingqing Diary Secretaries were again established; then Diary Officers and Diary Secretaries were divided left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Mingqing restored diary secretaries, splitting duties between left and right officers and secretaries.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年改為左史，咸亨復。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo changed to Left Historian; Xianheng restored.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo 2 renamed them Left Historians; Xianheng restored the former title.

sentences.zh: 天授元年又改為左史，神龍復也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshou again changed to Left Historian; Shenlong restored.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshou 1 again used Left Historian; Shenlong returned to Diary Officer.

sentences.zh: 楷書手三人。

translations.literal: Regular-script copyists: three.
translations.idiomatic: Three clerks in regular script.

sentences.zh: 起居郎掌起居注，錄天子之言動法度，以修記事之史。

translations.literal: Diary Officers kept the diary, recording the Son of Heaven's words, actions, and standards, to compile the history of record.
translations.idiomatic: They maintained the imperial diary, logging the emperor's speech, conduct, and protocol for the official chronicle.

sentences.zh: 凡記事之制，以事系日，以日系月，以月系時，以時系年。

translations.literal: The system of record tied affairs to days, days to months, months to seasons, and seasons to years.
translations.idiomatic: Entries linked events to days, days to months, months to seasons, and seasons to years.

sentences.zh: 必書其朔日甲乙，以紀歷數，典禮文物，以考制度，遷拜旌賞以勸善，誅伐黜免以懲惡。

translations.literal: New moon days and the sexagenary cycle had to be written to mark the calendar; ritual and artifacts were recorded to examine institutions; promotions and rewards to encourage good; punishments, executions, and dismissals to chastise evil.
translations.idiomatic: They noted calendrical days, rites and regalia, honors and promotions, and punishments and removals.

sentences.zh: 季終則授之國史焉。

translations.literal: At the end of the season it was handed to the National Historian.
translations.idiomatic: Each quarter the record passed to the official historians.

sentences.zh: 自漢獻帝后，歷代帝王有起居注，著作編之，每季為卷，送史館也。

translations.literal: From after Emperor Xian of Han, successive emperors had diaries; the Compilation Office edited them, each season one scroll, sent to the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han Xian, each reign kept a diary; compilers edited quarterly volumes for the History Office.

sentences.zh: 左補闕、左拾遣左補闕二員，從七品上。

translations.literal: Left Omission Filler and Left Petition Receiver: Left Omission Filler, two posts, Seventh Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Left omission fillers and petition receivers: two omission fillers, seventh rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 左拾遣二員。

translations.literal: Left Petition Receiver: two posts.
translations.idiomatic: Two left petition receivers.

sentences.zh: 從八品上。

translations.literal: Eighth Rank, Upper.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 古無此官名。

translations.literal: Antiquity had no such official title.
translations.idiomatic: No such office existed in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 天后垂拱元年二月二十九日敕：「記言書事，每切於旁求；

translations.literal: An edict of the twenty-ninth day of the second month of the first year of Chuigong of the Empress: 'Recording words and writing events urgently seeks those at one's side;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu's Chuigong 1/2/29 edict read: 'To record the emperor's words we must seek talent close at hand;

sentences.zh: 補闕拾遣，未弘於注選。

translations.literal: Omission fillers and petition receivers have not been widely extended in registered selection;
translations.idiomatic: yet omission fillers and receivers have not been fully integrated into regular appointment;

sentences.zh: 瞻言共理，必藉眾才，寄以登賢，期之進善。

translations.literal: looking to shared governance, one must rely on many talents; entrusting promotion of the worthy expects advancement of the good.
translations.idiomatic: good government requires many able men; this office is meant to elevate the worthy and improve policy.

sentences.zh: 宜置左右補闕各二員，從七品上，左右拾遣各二員，從八品上，掌供奉諷諫，行立次左右史之下。

translations.literal: Left and right omission fillers two each, Seventh Rank, Upper; left and right petition receivers two each, Eighth Rank, Upper — to attend, remonstrate, and stand in rank below the left and right historians.
translations.idiomatic: Establish two left and two right omission fillers at seventh rank and two petition receivers per side at eighth rank, to remonstrate and rank below the historians.

sentences.zh: 仍附於令。

translations.literal: Still attached to the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: The posts were added to the legal code.

sentences.zh: 」天授二年二月，加置三員，通前五員。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Tianshou, three posts were added, five in all including the former.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshou 2/2 increased the quota by three, for five total.

sentences.zh: 大曆四年，補闕、拾遣，各置內供奉兩員。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dali, omission fillers and petition receivers each had two inner-attendant posts added.
translations.idiomatic: Dali 4 added two inner-attendant slots for each title.

sentences.zh: 七年五月十一日敕，補闕、拾遣，宜各置兩員也。

translations.literal: An edict of the eleventh day of the fifth month of the seventh year: omission fillers and petition receivers should each be fixed at two posts.
translations.idiomatic: Dali 7/5/11 fixed two regular posts for each office.

sentences.zh: 補闕、拾遣之職，掌供奉訥諫，扈從乘輿。

translations.literal: The duties of omission fillers and petition receivers were to attend, remonstrate, and follow the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: They served at court, offered remonstrance, and accompanied the emperor on travel.

sentences.zh: 凡發令舉事，有不便於時，不合於道，大則廷議，小則上封。

translations.literal: Whenever orders or undertakings were inconvenient for the time or not in accord with the Way, great matters were debated at court, small ones submitted in sealed memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Policies harmful to the times or contrary to principle were challenged in court debate or by sealed memorial.

sentences.zh: 若賢良之遺滯于下，忠孝之不聞於上，則條其事狀而薦言之。

translations.literal: If worthy men languished below or loyalty and filial piety did not reach the ruler, they set forth the facts and recommended them in speech.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized when talent was overlooked or loyal service went unheard at court.

sentences.zh: 典儀典儀二員。

translations.literal: Masters of Ceremony: two posts.
translations.idiomatic: Two masters of ceremony.

sentences.zh: 從九品。

translations.literal: Ninth Rank, Lower.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 南齊有典儀錄事一員，梁有典儀之官，後省。

translations.literal: Southern Qi had one recording clerk for ceremony; Liang had officers of ceremony; later cut.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Qi kept one ceremony recorder; Liang had ceremony officers; later the posts were dropped.

sentences.zh: 皇朝又置典儀二人，隸門下省。

translations.literal: Our dynasty again set two Masters of Ceremony, subordinate to the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang restored two masters of ceremony under the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 初用人皆輕，貞觀末，李義府為之，自是用士人為之。

translations.literal: At first appointees were lightly regarded; at the end of Zhenguan, when Li Yifu held the post, thereafter scholars were used.
translations.idiomatic: Early holders were low status; after Li Yifu in late Zhenguan, educated gentlemen filled the role.

sentences.zh: 贊者十二人。

translations.literal: Announcers: twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve announcers.

sentences.zh: 隋太常、鴻臚二寺，皆有贊者，皇朝因置之，隸門下省，掌贊唱，為行事之節。

translations.literal: Sui's Grand Music and Honglu Offices both had announcers; our dynasty kept them, subordinate to the Chancellery, managing intoned announcements as the rhythm of proceedings.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's ritual and reception offices employed announcers; Tang placed twelve under the Chancellery to chant procedural cues.

sentences.zh: 分番上下，謂之番官。

translations.literal: They rotated shifts up and down, called rotation officers.
translations.idiomatic: They served in rotating shifts, known as shift officers.

sentences.zh: 典儀掌殿上贊唱之節，及殿廷版位之次。

translations.literal: The Master of Protocol manages the cadence of acclamation on the upper hall and the ordering of rank placards in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Protocol directs the rhythm of hall acclamation and the sequence of rank placards in the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 凡國有大禮，侍中行事，及進中嚴外辦之版，皆贊相焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the state holds a great ceremony, the Vice Grand Counselor performs the rites, and when presenting the boards for the inner vigil and outer preparation, he assists in all of these.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the state observes a major rite, the Vice Grand Counselor conducts the ceremony and, when the boards for inner vigil and outer readiness are submitted, assists throughout.

sentences.zh: 城門郎城門郎四員。

translations.literal: Gate Commandants: four posts of Gate Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Gate Commandants: four officers.

sentences.zh: 從六品上。

translations.literal: Secondary sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Upper subordinate sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 漢有城門校尉，掌京城諸門啟閉之節。

translations.literal: The Han had the Colonel of the Gates, who controlled the schedule for opening and closing the capital's gates.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han there was the Colonel of the Gates, charged with the timing of opening and closing the capital's gates.

sentences.zh: 隋改校尉為城門郎，置四員，從六品，皇朝因之也。

translations.literal: The Sui changed the colonel to Gate Commandant, set four posts at secondary sixth rank; the dynasty follows this.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui replaced the colonel with the Gate Commandant, appointing four officers at the subordinate sixth rank; the Tang kept the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 令史一人，書令史二人，門僕八百人。

translations.literal: One chief clerk, two document clerks, and eight hundred gate servants.
translations.idiomatic: One chief clerk, two writing clerks, and eight hundred gate servants.

sentences.zh: 門僕，晉代有之。

translations.literal: Gate servants existed already in the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Gate servants date back to the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 皇朝隸城門局，分番上下，掌送管鑰。

translations.literal: In our dynasty they are subordinate to the Gate Bureau, rotate in shifts, and are charged with delivering the keys.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang they belong to the Gate Bureau, serve in rotating shifts, and deliver the gate keys.

sentences.zh: 城門郎掌京城皇城宮殿諸門啟閉之節，奉出納管鑰。

translations.literal: Gate Commandants control the schedule for opening and closing the gates of the capital, the imperial city, and the palace, and charge the issuing and receiving of keys.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Commandants regulate opening and closing the capital, imperial city, and palace gates and oversee the issue and return of keys.

sentences.zh: 開則先外而後內，合則先內而後外，所以重中禁，尊皇居也。

translations.literal: To open, first the outer then the inner; to close, first the inner then the outer—thus to emphasize the inner forbidden precinct and honor the imperial residence.
translations.idiomatic: Opening proceeds from outside to inside; closing from inside to outside—so the inner precinct is weighted most heavily and the sovereign's dwelling is honored.

sentences.zh: 候其晨昏擊鼓之節而啟閉之。

translations.literal: They await the morning and evening drum signals and open and close accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: They open and close the gates according to the morning and evening drum signals.

sentences.zh: 凡皇城宮城合門之鑰，先酉而出，後戌而入；

translations.literal: Keys for closing the imperial city and palace gates: out first at the you hour, in afterward at the xu hour;
translations.idiomatic: Keys for locking the imperial city and palace gates leave first at the you hour and return after the xu hour;

sentences.zh: 開門之鑰，後醜而出，夜盡而入。

translations.literal: Keys for opening: out after the chou hour, in when the night is ended.
translations.idiomatic: Keys for opening leave after the chou hour and return when night is complete.

sentences.zh: 京城合門之鑰，後申而出，先子而入；

translations.literal: Keys for closing the capital city: out after the shen hour, in before the zi hour;
translations.idiomatic: Keys for locking the capital leave after the shen hour and return before the zi hour;

sentences.zh: 開門之鑰，後子而出，先卯而入。

translations.literal: Keys for opening: out after the zi hour, in before the mao hour.
translations.idiomatic: Keys for opening leave after the zi hour and return before the mao hour.

sentences.zh: 若非其時而有命啟閉，則詣閣覆奏。

translations.literal: If there is an order to open or close outside these times, one goes to the pavilion to report back and receive confirmation.
translations.idiomatic: If the gates must be opened or closed at an improper hour by imperial order, the officer goes to the pavilion to report and await confirmation.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎符寶郎四員。

translations.literal: Seal and Credential Officers: four posts of Seal and Credential Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Seal and Credential Officers: four officers.

sentences.zh: 從六品上。

translations.literal: Secondary sixth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Upper subordinate sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 周有典瑞之職，秦有符璽令，漢曰符璽郎。

translations.literal: The Zhou had the office of Keeper of Regalia; the Qin had the Seal Commander; the Han called them Seal and Credential Officers.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou had keepers of regalia; the Qin had a seal commander; the Han styled them seal and credential officers.

sentences.zh: 兩漢得秦六璽及傳國璽，後代傳之。

translations.literal: The two Han dynasties received the six Qin seals and the seal transmitting the realm, and later ages passed them down.
translations.idiomatic: Han received the six Qin seals and the seal of transmission of the realm, which later dynasties preserved.

sentences.zh: 隋置符璽郎二員，從六品。

translations.literal: The Sui appointed two Seal and Credential Officers, secondary sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui set two seal and credential officers at the subordinate sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 天后惡璽字，改為寶。

translations.literal: The Empress Wu disliked the character for 'seal' (xi) and changed it to 'treasure' (bao).
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu disliked the word for seal and substituted treasure in its place.

sentences.zh: 其受命傳國等八璽文。

translations.literal: The eight seals including Ordered-by-Heaven and the seal transmitting the realm, and their inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: This covered the Ordered-by-Heaven seal, the seal transmitting the realm, and six others—eight inscriptions in all.

sentences.zh: 並改雕寶字。

translations.literal: All were recarved with the character for 'treasure.'
translations.idiomatic: All were recut to read with the character for treasure.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，復為符璽郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong the title was restored to Seal and Credential Officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenlong era the office again became Seal and Credential Officer.

sentences.zh: 開元初，又改為符寶，從璽文也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan it was again changed to Seal and Credential, following the seal inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Kaiyuan the name became Seal and Credential once more, matching the seal texts.

sentences.zh: 令史二人，書令史三人，主寶六人，主符三十人，主節十八人。

translations.literal: Two chief clerks, three document clerks, six treasure keepers, thirty tally keepers, and eighteen credential keepers.
translations.idiomatic: Two chief clerks, three writing clerks, six keepers of the treasures, thirty keepers of tallies, and eighteen keepers of credentials.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎掌天子八寶及國之符節，辨其所用。

translations.literal: Seal and Credential Officers manage the Son of Heaven's eight treasures and the state's tallies and credentials, and distinguish their uses.
translations.idiomatic: They guard the emperor's eight treasures and the state's tallies and credentials and determine which is used for each purpose.

sentences.zh: 有事則請於內，既事則奉而藏之。

translations.literal: When there is business they request them from the inner palace; when the business is finished they present them for storage.
translations.idiomatic: When needed they requisition them from the inner quarters; when the affair is done they return them to storage.

sentences.zh: 八寶：一曰神寶，所以承百王，鎮萬國。

translations.literal: The eight treasures: first, the Spirit Treasure, by which to receive the hundred kings and stabilize the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: First, the Spirit Treasure, used to receive homage from all rulers and to steady the myriad realms.

sentences.zh: 二曰受命寶，所以修封禪，禮神祇。

translations.literal: Second, the Ordered-by-Heaven Treasure, by which to perform feng and shan rites and worship the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the Ordered-by-Heaven Treasure, used when performing the feng and shan sacrifices and honoring the gods.

sentences.zh: 三曰皇帝行寶，答疏于王公則用之；

translations.literal: Third, the Emperor's Travel Treasure, used when replying in writing to kings and dukes;
translations.idiomatic: Third, the Emperor's Travel Treasure, for written replies to kings and dukes;

sentences.zh: 四曰皇帝之寶，勞來勳賢則用之。

translations.literal: Fourth, the Emperor's Treasure, used when encouraging and rewarding meritorious worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the Emperor's Treasure, for encouraging and rewarding the meritorious;

sentences.zh: 五曰皇帝信寶，徵召臣下則用之。

translations.literal: Fifth, the Emperor's Trust Treasure, used when summoning officials below.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, the Emperor's Trust Treasure, for summoning subordinate officials.

sentences.zh: 六曰天子行寶，答四夷書則用之。

translations.literal: Sixth, the Son of Heaven's Travel Treasure, used when answering letters from the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, the Son of Heaven's Travel Treasure, for answering correspondence from the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 七曰天子之寶，慰撫蠻夷則用之；

translations.literal: Seventh, the Son of Heaven's Treasure, used when comforting and soothing the barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, the Son of Heaven's Treasure, for comforting frontier peoples;

sentences.zh: 八曰天子信寶，發番國兵則用之。

translations.literal: Eighth, the Son of Heaven's Trust Treasure, used when mobilizing troops of the frontier states.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, the Son of Heaven's Trust Treasure, for mobilizing the armies of subject border states.

sentences.zh: 凡大朝會，則捧寶以進於御座。

translations.literal: At great court assemblies they hold the treasures forward to the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: At major court gatherings they carry the treasures before the throne.

sentences.zh: 車駕行幸，則奉寶以從于黃鉞之內。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage travels, they bear the treasures and follow within the guard of the yellow axe.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor travels, they carry the treasures within the escort of the yellow battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 凡國有大事，則出納符節，辨其左右之異，藏其左而班其右，以合中外之契焉。

translations.literal: When the state has great affairs, they issue and receive tallies and credentials, distinguish the difference of left and right, store the left and distribute the right, to match the contract between inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: For great affairs of state they issue tallies and credentials, distinguish left from right, keep the left half in store and dispatch the right, so inner and outer halves match.

sentences.zh: 一曰銅魚符，所以起軍旅，易守長。

translations.literal: First, the bronze fish tally, by which to raise armies and replace commandants and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: First, the bronze fish tally, for raising troops and replacing garrison commanders and local chiefs.

sentences.zh: 二曰傳符，所以給郵驛，通制命。

translations.literal: Second, the transmission tally, by which to supply the post stations and communicate edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the transmission tally, for the courier relay and transmission of orders.

sentences.zh: 三曰隨身魚符，所以明貴賤，應徵召。

translations.literal: Third, the personal fish tally, by which to mark noble and base and respond to summons.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the personal fish tally, marking rank and answering imperial summons.

sentences.zh: 四曰木契，所以重鎮守，慎出納。

translations.literal: Fourth, the wooden tally, by which to weight frontier defense and carefully control issue and receipt.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the wooden tally, to secure frontier garrisons and strictly control issuance.

sentences.zh: 五曰旌節，所以委良能，假賞罰。

translations.literal: Fifth, the banner and credential, by which to entrust the capable and delegate reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, the banner and credential, for entrusting able men and delegating authority to reward and punish.

sentences.zh: 魚符之制，王畿之內，左三右一；

translations.literal: Regulations for fish tallies: within the royal domain, three on the left and one on the right;
translations.idiomatic: For fish tallies, within the metropolitan region there are three left halves and one right;

sentences.zh: 王畿之外，左五右一。

translations.literal: Outside the royal domain, five on the left and one on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the region, five left and one right.

sentences.zh: 左者在內，右者在外。

translations.literal: The left is kept inside; the right is kept outside.
translations.idiomatic: The left half is held within; the right half without.

sentences.zh: 行用之日，從第一為首，後事須用，以次發之，周而復始。

translations.literal: On the day of use, starting from the first; when later business requires them, they are issued in sequence, cycling back to the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: When used, the series begins with the first tally; later needs draw the next in order, and the cycle repeats.

sentences.zh: 大事兼敕書，小事但降符，函封遣使，合而行之。

translations.literal: For great affairs an edict letter is added; for small affairs only a tally is sent down, sealed in a case and dispatched by messenger, and both are carried out together.
translations.idiomatic: Major business combines an edict with the tally; minor business sends the tally alone, sealed and sent by courier, and both parts must align.

sentences.zh: 傳符之制，太子監國曰雙龍之符，左右各十。

translations.literal: Regulations for transmission tallies: when the crown prince supervises the realm, it is called the Double Dragon tally, ten each left and right.
translations.idiomatic: For transmission tallies, when the heir apparent regents the state he uses the Double Dragon tally—ten on each side.

sentences.zh: 京都留守曰麟符，左二十，其右一十有九。

translations.literal: The capital regent uses the Unicorn tally, twenty on the left and nineteen on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern capital regent uses the Unicorn tally: twenty left and nineteen right.

sentences.zh: 東方曰青龍之符，西方曰騶虞之符，南方曰硃雀之符，北方曰玄武之符，左四右三。

translations.literal: The east is called the Azure Dragon tally, the west the Zouyu tally, the south the Vermilion Bird tally, the north the Dark Warrior tally—four left and three right.
translations.idiomatic: East, west, south, and north use the Azure Dragon, Zouyu, Vermilion Bird, and Dark Warrior tallies respectively—four left, three right.

sentences.zh: 左者進內，右者付外。

translations.literal: The left is brought within; the right is delivered outside.
translations.idiomatic: The left half is brought inward; the right is issued outward.

sentences.zh: 隨身魚符之制，左二右一，太子以玉，親王以金，庶官以銅，佩以為飾。

translations.literal: Regulations for personal fish tallies: two left and one right; the crown prince uses jade, imperial princes gold, other officials bronze, worn as insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Personal fish tallies are two left, one right; the heir uses jade, princes gold, other officers bronze, worn on the belt as insignia.

sentences.zh: 刻姓名者，去官而納焉；

translations.literal: Those inscribed with a name are surrendered when one leaves office;
translations.idiomatic: Tallies engraved with the bearer's name are returned on leaving office;

sentences.zh: 不刻者，傳而佩之。

translations.literal: Those not inscribed are passed on and worn.
translations.idiomatic: Those without names are handed down and worn in succession.

sentences.zh: 木契之制，太子監國，則王畿之內，左右各三；

translations.literal: Regulations for wooden tallies: when the crown prince supervises the realm, within the royal domain three each left and right;
translations.idiomatic: For wooden tallies, when the heir regents within the domain there are three on each side;

sentences.zh: 王畿之外，左右各五；

translations.literal: Outside the royal domain, five each left and right;
translations.idiomatic: Outside the domain, five on each side;

sentences.zh: 庶官鎮守，則左右各十。

translations.literal: When common officials garrison, ten each left and right.
translations.idiomatic: For ordinary officers on frontier duty, ten on each side.

sentences.zh: 旌節之制，命大將帥及遣使于四方，則請而佩之。

translations.literal: Regulations for banners and credentials: when appointing great generals or dispatching envoys to the four directions, one requests and wears them.
translations.idiomatic: For banners and credentials, when commissioning great commanders or sending envoys abroad, the officer requests and carries them.

sentences.zh: 旌以專賞，節以專殺。

translations.literal: The banner is for exclusive reward; the credential for exclusive execution.
translations.idiomatic: The banner confers sole authority to reward; the credential, sole authority to punish by death.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》之制，山國用虎節，土國用人節，澤國用龍節，皆金也。

translations.literal: The system of the Rites of Zhou: mountain states used the tiger credential, land states the human credential, marsh states the dragon credential—all of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Rites of Zhou, mountain domains used tiger credentials, plain domains human credentials, and wetland domains dragon credentials—all of gold.

sentences.zh: 又雲，道路用旌節，即漢使所持者是也。

translations.literal: It also says that on the roads one used banner and credential; this is what Han envoys carried.
translations.idiomatic: The text also states that on the highways one used banner and credential—the type Han envoys bore.

sentences.zh: 弘文館弘文館：後漢有東觀，魏有崇文館，宋有玄、史二館，南齊有總明館，梁有士林館，北齊有文林館，後周有崇文館，皆著撰文史，鳩聚學徒之所也。

translations.literal: Hongwen Academy: Later Han had the Eastern Pavilion; Wei had the Cultivation of Letters Hall; Song had the Mystery and History halls; Southern Qi had the General Illumination Hall; Liang had the Forest of Letters Hall; Northern Qi had the Forest of Literature Hall; Later Zhou had the Cultivation of Letters Hall—all places where literary and historical works were compiled and students gathered.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwen Academy: the Later Han had the Eastern Pavilion, Wei the Cultivation of Letters Hall, Liu-Song the Mystery and History halls, Southern Qi the General Illumination Hall, Liang the Forest of Letters, Northern Qi the Forest of Literature, and Later Zhou again the Cultivation of Letters Hall—each a site for compiling texts and gathering students.

sentences.zh: 武德初置修文館，後改為弘文館。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude the Cultivation of Letters Hall was established; later it was changed to the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In early Wude the Cultivation of Letters Hall was founded; it was later renamed the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 後避太子諱，改曰昭文館。

translations.literal: Later, to avoid the crown prince's tabooed name, it was changed to the Illumination of Letters Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Later, to avoid the heir apparent's personal name, it became the Illumination of Letters Hall.

sentences.zh: 開元七年，復為弘文館，隸門下省。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan it was again made the Hongwen Academy, subordinate to the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 7 it was restored as the Hongwen Academy under the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 學士。

translations.literal: Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians.

sentences.zh: 學士無員數，自武德已來，皆妙簡賢良為學士。

translations.literal: Academicians had no fixed quota; from Wude onward worthy men were finely selected as academicians.
translations.idiomatic: There was no fixed number of academicians; since Wude the posts had been filled by careful selection of the worthy.

sentences.zh: 故事，五品已上稱學士，六品已下為直學士，又有文學直館學士，不定員數。

translations.literal: By precedent, fifth rank and above were called academicians, sixth rank and below were direct academicians; there were also literary direct academy academicians, with no fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, officials of fifth rank or higher were styled academicians and those of sixth rank or lower direct academicians; literary direct academy academicians also existed without a set quota.

sentences.zh: 館中有四部書及圖籍，自垂拱已後，皆宰相兼領，號為館主，常令給事中一人判館事。

translations.literal: The hall held the four divisions of books and maps and registers; from the Chuigong era onward a chief minister concurrently headed it as academy director, and customarily a supervising secretary judged academy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The academy housed the four library divisions and maps; from Chuigong a chief minister usually doubled as director, while a supervising secretary routinely handled day-to-day business.

sentences.zh: 學生三十人，校書郎二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Thirty students; two collators, secondary ninth rank upper.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty students; two collators at upper subordinate ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 令史二人，楷書手三十人，典書二人，拓書手三人，筆匠三人，熟紙裝潢匠九人，亭長二人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Two chief clerks, thirty regular scribes, two archive keepers, three copyists, three brush makers, nine paper-mounting craftsmen, two station chiefs, and four watchmen.
translations.idiomatic: Two chief clerks, thirty copyists, two archivists, three rub-copy scribes, three brush makers, nine paper-mounting artisans, two station chiefs, and four guards.

sentences.zh: 弘文館學士掌詳正圖籍，教授生徒。

translations.literal: Hongwen academicians manage detailed verification of maps and registers and instruct students.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians of the Hongwen Academy verify bibliographic records and teach the students.

sentences.zh: 凡朝廷有制度沿革，禮儀輕重，得參議焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the court revises institutions or weighs ritual propriety, they may join in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: They may participate when the court revises regulations or adjudicates ritual questions.

sentences.zh: 校書郎掌校理典籍，刊正錯謬。

translations.literal: Collators manage collating the classics and correcting errors.
translations.idiomatic: The collators proof the canon and emend mistakes.

sentences.zh: 其學生教授考試，如國子學之制焉。

translations.literal: Instruction and examination of students follow the regulations of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Student instruction and examinations follow the National University's rules.

sentences.zh: =中書省=

translations.literal: = The Secretariat =
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat

sentences.zh: 中書省秦始置中書謁者，漢元帝去「謁者」二字。

translations.literal: The Secretariat: Qin first established Secretariat Attendants; Emperor Yuan of Han removed the two characters for 'attendant.'
translations.idiomatic: Qin first created secretariat attendants; Han Emperor Yuan dropped the word attendant from the title.

sentences.zh: 歷代但雲中書。

translations.literal: Through the dynasties it was simply called the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages knew the office simply as the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後周謂之內史省，隋因為內史省，置內史監、令各一員。

translations.literal: Later Zhou called it the Inner Scribe Department; Sui followed this as the Inner Scribe Department, setting one Inner Scribe Director and one Inner Scribe Chief each.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou named it the Inner Scribe Department; the Sui kept that name and appointed one director and one chief.

sentences.zh: 煬帝改為內書省。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang changed it to the Inner Documents Department.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang renamed it the Inner Documents Department.

sentences.zh: 武德復為內史省，三年改為中書省。

translations.literal: Wude restored the Inner Scribe Department; in the third year it became the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude it was again the Inner Scribe Department; in Wude 3 it became the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為西台，光宅改為鳳閣，神龍復為中書省。

translations.literal: Longshuo changed it to the Western Terrace, Guangzai to the Phoenix Pavilion, Shenlong restored the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Longshuo it was the Western Terrace, under Guangzai the Phoenix Pavilion, and under Shenlong again the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開元元年改為紫微省，五年復舊。

translations.literal: The first year of Kaiyuan changed it to the Purple Micro Department; in the fifth year the old name returned.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 1 made it the Purple Micro Department; in Kaiyuan 5 the former name was restored.

sentences.zh: 中書令中書令二員。

translations.literal: Secretariat Chiefs: two posts of Secretariat Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Chiefs: two officers.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏品卑而付重。

translations.literal: Under Han and Wei the rank was low but the trust was heavy.
translations.idiomatic: In Han and Wei the post was modest in rank yet heavy in responsibility.

sentences.zh: 魏置監、令各一員，曆南朝不改。

translations.literal: Wei set one director and one chief each; through the southern courts this was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed one director and one chief; the southern dynasties kept the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 隋省監，置令二人，正三品。

translations.literal: The Sui abolished the director and set two chiefs, primary third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sui removed the director and placed two chiefs at the third rank.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝廢三公府僚，令中書令與侍中知政事，遂為宰相之職。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui abolished the Three Dukes' staff; he had the Secretariat Chief and Vice Grand Counselor manage state affairs, and thus they became chancellor posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui Wendi abolished the Three Dukes' offices, he charged the secretariat chief and vice grand counselor with government, making them de facto chancellors.

sentences.zh: 隋曰內書令。

translations.literal: Under Sui it was called Inner Documents Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui the title was Inner Documents Chief.

sentences.zh: 武德日內史令，尋改為中書令。

translations.literal: In Wude it was Inner Scribe Chief; soon it was changed to Secretariat Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude the title was Inner Scribe Chief, soon changed to Secretariat Chief.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為西台右相，咸亨復為中書令。

translations.literal: Longshuo made it Chief of the Western Terrace Right Chancellor; Xianheng restored Secretariat Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo styled it Chief of the Western Terrace and Right Chancellor; Xianheng restored Secretariat Chief.

sentences.zh: 光宅為鳳閣令。

translations.literal: Guangzai made it Phoenix Pavilion Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangzai it was Phoenix Pavilion Chief.

sentences.zh: 開元元年改為紫微令，五年復為中書令。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan year one changed it to Purple Micro Chief; year five restored Secretariat Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 1 made it Purple Micro Chief; in Kaiyuan 5 it again became Secretariat Chief.

sentences.zh: 天寶改為右相，至德二年復為中書令。

translations.literal: Tianbao changed it to Right Chancellor; in the second year of Zhide it again became Secretariat Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao renamed it Right Chancellor; Zhide 2 restored Secretariat Chief.

sentences.zh: 本正三品，大曆二年十一月九日，與侍中同升正二品，自後不改也。

translations.literal: Originally primary third rank; on the ninth day of the eleventh month of the second year of Dali, it was raised with the Vice Grand Counselor to primary second rank, and afterward was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Originally third rank; on Dali 2, month 11, day 9, it was promoted with the Vice Grand Counselor to second rank and remained there thereafter.

sentences.zh: 中書令之職，掌軍國之政令，緝熙帝載，統和天人。

translations.literal: The duty of the Secretariat Chief is to hold the military and civil edicts of state, illumine the emperor's record, and harmonize Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Chief holds military and civil policy, brightens the sovereign's mandate, and harmonizes Heaven and humanity.

sentences.zh: 入則告之，出則奉之，以厘萬邦，以度百揆，蓋佐天子而執大政也。

translations.literal: Entering he reports to the emperor; departing he carries out his orders—to govern the myriad states and measure the hundred affairs; in sum he assists the Son of Heaven in wielding great government.
translations.idiomatic: He enters to inform the sovereign and goes forth to execute his will, ordering the myriad realms and sizing up every branch of administration—assistant to the Son of Heaven in the great affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 凡王言之制有七：一曰冊書，二曰制書，三曰慰勞制書，四曰發敕，五曰敕旨，六曰論事敕書，七曰敕牒，皆宣署申覆而施行之。

translations.literal: Regulations for the sovereign's words are seven: first, book edicts; second, edict documents; third, edicts of consolation and encouragement; fourth, issued commands; fifth, command rescripts; sixth, edicts on deliberation of affairs; seventh, command slips—all are proclaimed, signed, reported, and then put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial pronouncements fall into seven forms: book edicts, formal edicts, consolation edicts, issued commands, command rescripts, deliberative edicts, and command slips—each is drafted, countersigned, reported, and executed.

sentences.zh: 凡大祭祀群神，則從升壇以相禮。

translations.literal: At great sacrifices to the host of spirits he follows in ascending the altar to assist in the rites.
translations.idiomatic: At major sacrifices to the gods he accompanies the emperor onto the altar to assist the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 享宗廟，則從升阼階。

translations.literal: When offering at the ancestral temple he follows in ascending the eastern steps.
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial temple he follows the sovereign up the eastern steps.

sentences.zh: 親征篡嚴，戒敕百僚，冊命親賢，臨軒則使讀冊。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally campaigns and assembles the host, admonishes the hundred officials, enfeoffs the worthy by book, at the imperial window he has the book read.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor leads an expedition in person, assembles the army, warns the bureaucracy, and enfeoffs the worthy by written mandate, he has the text read at the imperial window.

sentences.zh: 若命之於朝，則宣而授之。

translations.literal: If the appointment is made at court, it is proclaimed and conferred.
translations.idiomatic: If the investiture takes place at court, the edict is announced and the appointee receives it.

sentences.zh: 凡冊太子，則授璽。

translations.literal: Whenever enfeoffing the crown prince, the seal is conferred.
translations.idiomatic: When investing the heir apparent, the seal is handed over.

sentences.zh: 凡制詔宣傳，文章獻納，皆授之於記事之官。

translations.literal: Whenever edicts and proclamations are issued, essays submitted or rejected, all are entrusted to the recording officers.
translations.idiomatic: Promulgation of edicts and memorials submitted or returned is entrusted to the recorders.

sentences.zh: 武德、貞觀故事，以尚書省左右僕射各一人及侍中、中書令各二人，為知政事官。

translations.literal: Wude and Zhenguan precedent made one Left and one Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and two Vice Grand Counselors and two Secretariat Chiefs each the officials who manage government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wude and Zhenguan precedent, the left and right vice directors of the Department of State Affairs and two vice grand counselors and two secretariat chiefs served as the officials in charge of policy.

sentences.zh: 其時以他官預議國政者，雲與宰相參議朝政，或云平章國計，或云專典機密，或參議政事。

translations.literal: At that time when other officers joined in deliberating state affairs, some were said to join the chancellor in deliberating court governance, or to harmonize and plan the state's accounts, or to specialize in secrets, or to join in deliberating government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When other officials were drawn into policy, they might be said to deliberate with the chancellor, to harmonize national planning, to handle confidential matters, or simply to join in government deliberation.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十七年，李勣為太子詹事，特詔同知政事，始謂同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, Li Ji was Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent; a special edict made him co-manager of government affairs, and this was first called 'Same as Third Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery.'
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 17 Li Ji, as grand mentor to the heir, received an edict to share in managing affairs—the origin of the title 'Same as Third Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery.'

sentences.zh: 自是，僕射常帶此稱。

translations.literal: From this time the Vice Directors often bore this title.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter vice directors commonly carried that designation.

sentences.zh: 自余非兩省長官預知政事者，亦皆以此為名。

translations.literal: All others who were not chiefs of the two departments but joined in managing affairs also used this name.
translations.idiomatic: Other officials not heads of the two departments but sharing in policy likewise took the name.

sentences.zh: 永淳中，始詔郭正一、郭待舉、魏玄同等，與中書門下同承受進旨平章事。

translations.literal: In the Yongchun era an edict first addressed Guo Zhengyi, Guo Daiju, Wei Xuantong, and others to join the Secretariat and Chancellery in receiving and carrying out imperial intent as Harmonizers of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchun an edict first named Guo Zhengyi, Guo Daiju, Wei Xuantong, and others to join the secretariat and chancellery in receiving imperial instructions as Harmonizers of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 自天后已後，兩省長官及同中書門下三品並平章事，為宰相。

translations.literal: From the Empress Wu onward, chiefs of the two departments and those of Same Third Rank who were Harmonizers of Affairs were chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wu, heads of the two departments plus holders of Same Third Rank with Harmonizer of Affairs were counted as chancellors.

sentences.zh: 其僕射不帶同中書門下三品者，但厘尚書省而已。

translations.literal: Vice Directors who did not bear Same Third Rank only administered the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Vice directors without the Same Third Rank title merely ran the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 總章二年，東台侍郎張文瓘，西台侍郎戴至德等，始以同中書門下三品著之入銜。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zongzhang, Eastern Terrace Vice Director Zhang Wenguan, Western Terrace Vice Director Dai Zhide, and others first entered the title Same Third Rank in their formal commissions.
translations.idiomatic: In Zongzhang 2 Eastern Terrace vice director Zhang Wenguan and Western Terrace vice director Dai Zhide were the first to have Same Third Rank inscribed in their appointment titles.

sentences.zh: 自是相承至今。

translations.literal: From then the practice has continued to the present.
translations.idiomatic: That usage has continued ever since.

sentences.zh: 永淳二年，黃門侍郎劉齊賢知政事，稱同中書門下平章事，自後兩省長官，及他官執政未至侍中書令者，皆稱同中書門下平章事也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchun, Yellow Gate Vice Director Liu Qixian managed government affairs and was styled Harmonizer of Affairs Same as the Secretariat and Chancellery; afterward chiefs of the two departments and other officers in power who had not reached Vice Grand Counselor or Secretariat Chief all used Harmonizer of Affairs Same as the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchun 2 Liu Qixian as yellow gate vice director governed as Harmonizer of Affairs Same as the Secretariat and Chancellery; thereafter chiefs of the two departments and acting ministers below vice grand counselor or secretariat chief used that fuller title.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎中書侍郎二員。

translations.literal: Secretariat Vice Directors: two posts of Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Vice Directors: two officers.

sentences.zh: 漢置中書，掌密詔，有令、僕、丞、郎四官。

translations.literal: The Han established the Secretariat, managing secret edicts, with chief, steward, aide, and officer—the four offices.
translations.idiomatic: Han created the secretariat for confidential edicts with chief, steward, aide, and officer.

sentences.zh: 魏曰中書郎，晉加「侍」字。

translations.literal: Wei called them Secretariat Officers; Jin added the character for 'attending.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei styled them secretariat officers; Jin prefixed attending.

sentences.zh: 隋置內書省，改為內書侍郎，正四品。

translations.literal: The Sui set the Inner Documents Department and changed the title to Inner Documents Vice Director, primary fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's Inner Documents Department used Inner Documents Vice Director at the fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 武德初為內史侍郎，三年改為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude it was Inner Scribe Vice Director; in the third year it became Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Early Wude called them Inner Scribe Vice Directors; in Wude 3 they became Secretariat Vice Directors.

sentences.zh: 龍朔、光宅、開元，隨曹易號。

translations.literal: Longshuo, Guangzai, and Kaiyuan changed names with the department.
translations.idiomatic: Under Longshuo, Guangzai, and Kaiyuan the title shifted with the department's name.

sentences.zh: 至德復為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhide restored Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Zhide restored the title Secretariat Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 武德定令，與尚書侍郎俱第四品。

translations.literal: The Wude code made them equal with Department of State Affairs vice directors at the fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Wude statutes ranked them with department vice directors at fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 大曆二年九月，與門下侍郎共升為正三品也。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Dali they were jointly raised to primary third rank with Chancellery Vice Directors.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 2, month 9, they were promoted with chancellery vice directors to third rank.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎掌貳令之職。

translations.literal: The Secretariat Vice Director assists the chief in his duties.
translations.idiomatic: The vice director assists the secretariat chief.

sentences.zh: 凡邦國之庶務，朝廷之大政，皆參議焉。

translations.literal: All routine affairs of the realm and great policies of the court he joins in deliberating.
translations.idiomatic: He deliberates on routine business of the state and major court policy.

sentences.zh: 凡臨軒冊命大臣，令為之使，則持冊書以授之。

translations.literal: Whenever enfeoffing great ministers at the imperial window, if the chief makes him envoy, he holds the book edict and confers it.
translations.idiomatic: When great ministers are enfeoffed at the imperial window and the chief appoints him envoy, he carries the book edict and invests the recipient.

sentences.zh: 凡四夷來朝，監軒則受其表疏，升於西階而奏。

translations.literal: Whenever the four barbarians come to court, at the imperial window he receives their memorials and ascends the western steps to present them.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign envoys attend court he receives their petitions at the imperial window and mounts the western steps to present them.

sentences.zh: 若獻贄幣，則受之以授于所司。

translations.literal: If they present tribute gifts, he receives them and passes them to the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: If tribute is offered, he accepts it and hands it to the appropriate agency.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人中書舍人六員。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafters: six posts of Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafters: six officers.

sentences.zh: 正五品上。

translations.literal: Primary fifth rank, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Upper fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 曹魏於中書置通事一人，掌呈奏按章。

translations.literal: Cao Wei at the Secretariat set one Communications Officer who managed presenting memorials and reviewing documents.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wei placed one communications officer at the secretariat to handle memorials and document review.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公於通事下加「舍人」二字。

translations.literal: The Duke of Gaogu added the two characters for 'drafter' below Communications Officer.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Gaogu added the word drafter to the communications officer's title.

sentences.zh: 晉於中書置舍人、通事各一人。

translations.literal: Jin at the Secretariat set one drafter and one communications officer each.
translations.idiomatic: Jin appointed one drafter and one communications officer at the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自魏、晉、齊、梁，詔誥皆出於中書令、中書侍郎，中書通事舍人但掌呈奏而已。

translations.literal: From Wei, Jin, Qi, and Liang, edicts and orders all came from the Secretariat Chief and Vice Director; the Secretariat Communications Drafter only managed presenting memorials.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei through Liang, edicts issued from the chief and vice director while the communications drafter merely forwarded memorials.

sentences.zh: 或通事有文字者，別敕知詔誥。

translations.literal: Sometimes if the communications officer was literate, a separate edict put him in charge of edicts and orders.
translations.idiomatic: Occasionally a literate communications officer received a special commission to draft edicts.

sentences.zh: 至梁武，制誥專令舍人掌之，兼去「通事」二字，但雲中書舍人。

translations.literal: By Emperor Wu of Liang, edicts were assigned exclusively to drafters; 'Communications' was also removed, and they were simply called Secretariat Drafters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang entrusted edicts solely to drafters, dropped communications from the title, and called them secretariat drafters.

sentences.zh: 隋曰內史舍人，置八員，掌制誥，品第六。

translations.literal: Sui called them Inner Scribe Drafters, set eight posts, managed edicts, rank sixth.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui styled them inner scribe drafters—eight posts at sixth rank, charged with drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 尋升五品上。

translations.literal: Soon raised to upper fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: They were soon promoted to upper fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 煬帝改內書舍人，置四員。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang changed to Inner Documents Drafter, four posts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang made them inner documents drafters, four in number.

sentences.zh: 武德初為內史舍人，三年，改為中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude they were Inner Scribe Drafters; in the third year they became Secretariat Drafters.
translations.idiomatic: Early Wude they were inner scribe drafters; in Wude 3 secretariat drafters.

sentences.zh: 龍朔、光宅、開元，隨曹改易。

translations.literal: Longshuo, Guangzai, and Kaiyuan changed with the department.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo, Guangzai, and Kaiyuan renamed them with the department.

sentences.zh: 舍人掌侍奉進奏，參議表章。

translations.literal: Drafters manage attendance and forwarding memorials and join in deliberating petitions.
translations.idiomatic: Drafters attend court, forward memorials, and deliberate on petitions.

sentences.zh: 凡詔旨敕制，及璽書冊命，皆按典故起草進畫；

translations.literal: All edicts, commands, rescripts, and sealed letters and book appointments are drafted according to precedent and submitted for approval;
translations.idiomatic: Edicts, commands, rescripts, sealed letters, and book investitures are drafted by precedent and submitted for imperial approval;

sentences.zh: 既下，則署而行之。

translations.literal: Once issued, they sign and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: After promulgation they countersign and carry them out.

sentences.zh: 其禁有四：一曰漏泄，二曰稽緩，三曰違失，四曰忘誤；

translations.literal: There are four prohibitions: first, leakage; second, delay; third, error; fourth, forgetfulness and mistake;
translations.idiomatic: Four offenses are forbidden: disclosure, tardiness, breach, and careless error—

sentences.zh: 所以重王命也。

translations.literal: Thus to weight the sovereign's commands.
translations.idiomatic: —so the weight of imperial words is upheld.

sentences.zh: 制敕既行，有誤則奏而正之。

translations.literal: Once an edict or command is issued, if there is error it is reported and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: If a promulgated edict or command is wrong, they memorialized to rectify it.

sentences.zh: 凡大朝會，諸方起居，則受其表狀而奏之。

translations.literal: At great court assemblies, when all regions report attendance, they receive the petitions and present them.
translations.idiomatic: At major assemblies they receive regional status reports and present them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 國有大事，若大克捷及大祥瑞，百僚表賀，亦如之。

translations.literal: When the state has great affairs, such as great victory or great auspicious omens, and the hundred officials submit congratulatory memorials, it is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same applies when officials submit felicitations for great victories or extraordinary omens.

sentences.zh: 凡冊命大臣于朝，則使持節讀冊命之。

translations.literal: Whenever enfeoffing great ministers at court, they are sent to hold the credential and read the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Court investitures of great ministers are read by envoys bearing the credential.

sentences.zh: 凡將帥有功及有大賓客，皆使勞問之。

translations.literal: Whenever generals have merit or there are great guests, they are sent to inquire after them with imperial consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious generals and eminent guests receive imperial inquiries dispatched through the drafters.

sentences.zh: 凡察天下冤滯，與給事中及御史三司鞫其事。

translations.literal: Whenever examining wrongs and delays under Heaven, together with supervising secretaries and censors the three offices investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: They join supervising secretaries and censors as a triad to examine grievances and backlog cases throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 凡百司奏議，文武考課，皆預裁焉。

translations.literal: All offices' memorials and deliberations, civil and military performance reviews, they all pre-judge.
translations.idiomatic: They preliminary review memorials from every agency and civil and military merit evaluations.

sentences.zh: 主書主書四人，從七品上。

translations.literal: Document Supervisors: four document supervisors, secondary seventh rank upper.
translations.idiomatic: Document supervisors: four officers at upper subordinate seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 主事四人，從八品下。

translations.literal: Principal clerks four, secondary eighth rank lower.
translations.idiomatic: Principal clerks: four at lower subordinate eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 令史二十五人，書令史五十人，傳制十人，亭長十八人，修補敕匠五十人。

translations.literal: Twenty-five chief clerks, fifty document clerks, ten edict transmitters, eighteen station chiefs, fifty edict-repair craftsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five chief clerks, fifty writing clerks, ten edict couriers, eighteen station chiefs, and fifty edict-binding artisans.

sentences.zh: 右散騎常侍、右補闕、右拾遣、起居舍人右散騎常侍二員，從三品。

translations.literal: Right Palace Attendant, Right Remonstrance Officer, Right Admonisher, Court Diarist—Right Palace Attendants two posts, secondary third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Right palace attendant, right remonstrance officer, right admonisher, court diarist: two right palace attendants at subordinate third rank.

sentences.zh: 右補闕二員，從七品上。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Officers two posts, secondary seventh rank upper.
translations.idiomatic: Two right remonstrance officers at upper subordinate seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 右拾遣二員，從八品上。

translations.literal: Right Admonishers two posts, secondary eighth rank upper.
translations.idiomatic: Two right admonishers at upper subordinate eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 起居舍人二員。

translations.literal: Court Diarists two posts.
translations.idiomatic: Two court diarists.

sentences.zh: 從六品上。

translations.literal: Secondary sixth rank upper.
translations.idiomatic: Upper subordinate sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 右常侍、補闕、拾遣。

translations.literal: Right Attendants, Remonstrance Officers, and Admonishers.
translations.idiomatic: Right attendants, remonstrance officers, and admonishers.

sentences.zh: 掌事同左省。

translations.literal: Their duties are the same as the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: Their responsibilities match those of the left department.

sentences.zh: 起居舍人，掌修記言之史，錄天子之制誥德音，如記事之制，以記時政損益。

translations.literal: Court diarists manage the history that records words, recording the Son of Heaven's edicts and gracious pronouncements, like the recorders' system, to record gains and losses in current governance.
translations.idiomatic: Court diarists keep the verbal record, noting the emperor's edicts and benevolent pronouncements as recorders do, to track changes in policy.

sentences.zh: 季終，則授之於國史。

translations.literal: At the end of the season they hand them to the National Historian.
translations.idiomatic: Each quarter they deliver their notes to the official historians.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人通事舍人十六人。

translations.literal: Communications Drafters: sixteen posts of Communications Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Communications drafters: sixteen officers.

sentences.zh: 從六品上。

translations.literal: Secondary sixth rank upper.
translations.idiomatic: Upper subordinate sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人，奏謁者之官也。

translations.literal: Communications drafters are the office of memorial presenters.
translations.idiomatic: Communications drafters belong to the corps of petition presenters.

sentences.zh: 掌賓贊、贊受事，隸光祿勳。

translations.literal: They manage guest protocol and receiving business, subordinate to the Director of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: They handle guest etiquette and receipt of business under the Director of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 晉置舍人、通事各一人，隸中書。

translations.literal: Jin set one drafter and one communications officer each, subordinate to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jin appointed one drafter and one communications officer under the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 東晉曰通事舍人。

translations.literal: Eastern Jin called them Communications Drafters.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin styled them communications drafters.

sentences.zh: 隋因晉制，置十六人，從六品上，又為通事謁者。

translations.literal: Sui followed the Jin system, set sixteen, secondary sixth rank upper, also called Communications Presenters.
translations.idiomatic: Sui copied Jin with sixteen officers at upper subordinate sixth rank, also termed communications presenters.

sentences.zh: 武德初，廢謁者台，改通事謁者為通事舍人，隸四方館，屬中書省也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude the Presenters' Office was abolished; Communications Presenters were changed to Communications Drafters, subordinate to the Four Directions Hall, belonging to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early Wude abolished the presenters' office, renamed communications presenters communications drafters, placed them in the Four Directions Hall under the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人掌朝見引納及辭謝者，於殿廷通奏。

translations.literal: Communications drafters manage audience introduction and those taking leave, transmitting memorials in the hall court.
translations.idiomatic: They introduce visitors at court audiences, handle farewells, and relay petitions in the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 凡近臣入侍，文武就列，引以進退，而告其拜起出入之節。

translations.literal: Whenever close ministers enter attendance, civil and military take their places—they lead advance and withdrawal and announce the rhythm of bowing, rising, entering, and leaving.
translations.idiomatic: When intimate ministers attend and civil and military officials form ranks, they guide movement and announce when to bow, rise, enter, or withdraw.

sentences.zh: 凡四方通表，華夷納貢，皆受而進之。

translations.literal: Whenever memorials arrive from the four directions, and Chinese and barbarians present tribute, all are received and forwarded.
translations.idiomatic: Petitions from all quarters and tribute from both empire and frontier are received and passed upward.

sentences.zh: 凡軍旅之出，則命受慰勞而遣之。

translations.literal: Whenever armies go forth, they are ordered to receive consolation and be dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: When troops march out they receive imperial consolation and are sent off.

sentences.zh: 既行，則每月存問將士之家，以視其疾苦。

translations.literal: Once they have gone, each month they visit the soldiers' families to observe their hardship.
translations.idiomatic: After departure they monthly inquire at soldiers' homes to learn their distress.

sentences.zh: 凱旋，則郊迓之，皆復命。

translations.literal: On triumphant return they welcome them at the suburban altar; all report back on their mission.
translations.idiomatic: On victorious return they greet the army at the suburban rites and all file mission reports.

sentences.zh: 凡致仕之臣，與邦之耋老，時巡問亦如之。

translations.literal: Retired officials and the state's aged are likewise visited on periodic rounds.
translations.idiomatic: Retired ministers and the realm's elderly receive the same periodic visits.

sentences.zh: 令史十人，亭長十八人，掌固二十四人。

translations.literal: Ten chief clerks, eighteen station chiefs, twenty-four watchmen.
translations.idiomatic: Ten chief clerks, eighteen station chiefs, and twenty-four guards.

sentences.zh: =集賢殿書院=

translations.literal: = Hall of Assembled Worthies Academy =
translations.idiomatic: Hall of Assembled Worthies Academy

sentences.zh: 集賢殿書院：開元十三年置。

translations.literal: Hall of Assembled Worthies Academy: established in the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Assembled Worthies Academy was founded in Kaiyuan 13.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏已來，職在秘書。
