translations.literal: From Han and Wei onward the duty lay in the Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Wei the work had belonged to the Archive.

sentences.zh: 梁于文德殿內藏聚群書。

translations.literal: Liang within the Cultivation of Virtue Hall secretly stored collected books.
translations.idiomatic: Liang housed its book collections inside the Cultivation of Virtue Hall.

sentences.zh: 北齊有文林館學士，後周有麟趾殿學士，皆掌著述。

translations.literal: Northern Qi had Forest of Literature academicians; Later Zhou had Unicorn Hall academicians—all managed compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi maintained Forest of Literature academicians and Later Zhou Unicorn Hall academicians, all charged with writing and editing.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳之後，寫群書正副二本，藏于宮中，其餘以實秘書外閣。

translations.literal: After Sui pacified Chen they copied the collected books in principal and duplicate sets, storing them in the palace; the remainder filled the Archive's outer pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After conquering Chen the Sui copied the imperial library in master and duplicate sets for the palace and shelved the rest in the archive's outer wing.

sentences.zh: 煬帝于東都觀文殿東西廂貯書。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang at the eastern capital stored books in the east and west wings of the Viewing Culture Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang kept books in the east and west annexes of the Viewing Culture Hall at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 自漢延熹至隋，皆秘書掌國籍，而禁中之書，時或有焉。

translations.literal: From Han's Yanxi era through Sui the Archive managed the national registers, while books within the forbidden palace were sometimes kept there as well.
translations.idiomatic: From Han Yanxi through Sui the archive held the national bibliographic registers, though palace collections were sometimes kept separately.

sentences.zh: 及太宗在籓府時，有秦府學士十八人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong was prince of the Qin fief there were eighteen Qin Mansion academicians.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizong held the Qin princely fief he gathered eighteen mansion academicians.

sentences.zh: 其後弘文、崇文二館皆有。

translations.literal: Later both the Hongwen and Chongwen halls existed.
translations.idiomatic: Later both the Hongwen and Chongwen halls were maintained.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，大校群書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne he greatly collated the collected books.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanzong's accession he undertook a major collation of the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，於乾元殿東廊下寫四部書，以充內庫，置校定官四人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan they copied the four divisions of books beneath the east corridor of the Qianyuan Hall to fill the inner storehouse, setting four collation officers.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 5 copied the four library divisions along the east corridor of Qianyuan Hall for the inner repository and appointed four collation officers.

sentences.zh: 七年，駕在東都，於麗正殿置修書使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the emperor was at the eastern capital, he set a Book-Revision Commissioner at the Lizheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 7, while at the eastern capital, he established a book-revision commissioner at Lizheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 十二年，駕在東都，十三年與學士張說等宴於集仙殿，因改名集賢，改修書使為集賢書院學士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the emperor was at the eastern capital; in the thirteenth he banqueted with Academician Zhang Yue and others at the Hall of Assembled Immortals, and therefore renamed it Assembled Worthies and changed the Book-Revision Commissioner to Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 12 the court was at Luoyang; in Kaiyuan 13 Xuanzong feasted with Academician Zhang Yue and others in the Hall of Assembled Immortals, renamed it Hall of Assembled Worthies, and retitled the book-revision commissioner academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies Academy.

sentences.zh: 其大明宮所置書院，本命婦院，屋宇宏敞。

translations.literal: The academy established in Daming Palace was originally the Women's Inner Quarters; its halls were vast and spacious.
translations.idiomatic: The academy in Daming Palace had begun as the women's inner quarters; its buildings were grand and capacious.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年三月，詔僕射裴冕等十三人，每日於集賢書院待詔。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Yongtai, an edict ordered Vice Director Pei Mian and twelve others to await edicts daily at the Hall of Assembled Worthies Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Yongtai 1, third month: an edict assigned Vice Director Pei Mian and twelve colleagues to daily attendance at the Hall of Assembled Worthies awaiting imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 集賢學士。

translations.literal: Academicians of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 初定制以五品已上官為學士，六品已下為直學士。

translations.literal: At first the regulation fixed officials of fifth rank and above as academicians and those of sixth rank and below as direct academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Originally fifth-rank officials and above served as academicians; sixth rank and below as direct academicians.

sentences.zh: 每宰相為學士者，為知院事。

translations.literal: Whenever a chancellor served as academician, he was styled Director of Academy Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When a chancellor held the post of academician, he was called director of academy affairs.

sentences.zh: 常侍一人，為副知院事。

translations.literal: One regular attendant served as deputy director of academy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A regular attendant served as deputy director.

sentences.zh: 學士知院事一人，開元初，以褚無量、馬懷素、元行沖相次知乾元殿寫書，及在麗正，乃有使名。

translations.literal: One academician director of academy affairs: in early Kaiyuan, Chu Wuliang, Ma Huaisu, and Yuan Xingchong in succession oversaw copying at Qianyuan Hall; when the work moved to Lizheng, the title of commissioner was introduced.
translations.idiomatic: The post of academician director of affairs began in early Kaiyuan when Chu Wuliang, Ma Huaisu, and Yuan Xingchong in turn supervised copying at Qianyuan Hall; after the academy moved to Lizheng Hall the office received a formal commissioner title.

sentences.zh: 張說代元行沖，改院為集賢，以說為大學士，知院事，說懇讓大字，詔許之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue replaced Yuan Xingchong, changed the hall's name to Assembled Worthies, and was made grand academician and director of affairs; Yue earnestly declined the character "grand," and an edict granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue succeeded Yuan Xingchong, renamed the institution Hall of Assembled Worthies, and became director of affairs as grand academician—though he begged off the word "grand," and the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 自是，每以宰相一人知院事。

translations.literal: From this time one chancellor always directed academy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter one chancellor customarily directed the academy.

sentences.zh: 副知院事一人，初，宰相張說知院事，以左常侍徐堅為副知院事，因為故事。

translations.literal: One deputy director of affairs: at first Chancellor Zhang Yue directed affairs and Left Regular Attendant Xu Jian served as deputy, and this became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy directorship began when Chancellor Zhang Yue headed the academy and Left Regular Attendant Xu Jian served as his deputy—a pattern that stuck.

sentences.zh: 判院一人，初在乾元殿，刊正官一人判事，其後因之。

translations.literal: One chief judge of the academy: at first at Qianyuan Hall one collation officer judged affairs, and later offices followed this.
translations.idiomatic: A chief judge post began at Qianyuan Hall with one collation officer adjudicating business; later incumbents kept the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 押院中使一人。

translations.literal: One palace commissioner supervising the academy.
translations.idiomatic: One eunuch commissioner supervised the academy.

sentences.zh: 自乾元殿寫書，則置掌出入，宣進奏，兼頌中官，監守院門，掌同宮禁。

translations.literal: From the Qianyuan copying project they appointed one to manage ingress and egress, announce memorials, and concurrently praise inner officials, guard the academy gate, and share palace security duties.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyuan Hall copying an eunuch managed access, forwarded memorials, supervised inner staff, and guarded the gate with palace security powers.

sentences.zh: 侍講學士，開元初，褚無量、馬懷素侍講禁中，名為侍讀。

translations.literal: Lecturing academicians: in early Kaiyuan Chu Wuliang and Ma Huaisu lectured within the forbidden palace and were called readers-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Early Kaiyuan lecturing academicians Chu Wuliang and Ma Huaisu taught inside the palace and were styled readers-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 其後康子元為侍講學士。

translations.literal: Later Kang Ziyuan served as lecturing academician.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Ziyuan later held the lecturing academician post.

sentences.zh: 修撰官，校理官，並無常員，以官人兼之。

translations.literal: Compilation officers and collation officers had no fixed quota and were filled by officials concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Compilation and collation posts had no standing headcount; regular officials held them in addition to other duties.

sentences.zh: 待制官，古之待詔金馬門是。

translations.literal: Awaiting-edict officers—the ancient awaiting edicts at Golden Horse Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting-edict officers descended from the Han custom of awaiting edicts at Golden Horse Gate.

sentences.zh: 留院官，檢討官。

translations.literal: Officers retained at the academy and examination officers.
translations.idiomatic: Retained academy officers and examination officers.

sentences.zh: 皆以學士別敕留之。

translations.literal: All were kept at the academy by separate edict of the academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians kept them at the hall by special edict.

sentences.zh: 孔目官一人，專知御書典四人，並開元五年置。

translations.literal: One registry officer, four specialists in imperial books—all established in the fifth year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: One registry clerk and four curators of imperial books were added in Kaiyuan 5.

sentences.zh: 知書官八人，開元五年置，掌分四庫書。

translations.literal: Eight book officers, established Kaiyuan 5, in charge of dividing work among the four library divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Eight book officers, created in Kaiyuan 5, apportioned labor across the four repository divisions.

sentences.zh: 書直、寫御書一百人，拓書六人，書直八人，裝書直十四人，造筆直四人。

translations.literal: Book clerks and copyists of imperial books one hundred persons, rubbers six, book clerks eight, binding clerks fourteen, brush-making clerks four.
translations.idiomatic: The staff included one hundred imperial copyists, six rubbers, eight book clerks, fourteen binders, and four brush makers.

sentences.zh: 並開元六年置。

translations.literal: All established in the sixth year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: All these posts dated from Kaiyuan 6.

sentences.zh: 集賢學士之職，掌刊緝古今之經籍，以辨明邦國之大典。

translations.literal: The duty of Assembled Worthies academicians was to edit and compile ancient and modern classics so as to clarify the great statutes of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Assembled Worthies academicians edited classical and contemporary texts to clarify the state's fundamental institutions.

sentences.zh: 凡天下圖書之遺逸，賢才之隱滯，則承旨而徵求焉。

translations.literal: Where books were lost throughout the empire or worthy talent lay hidden and stagnant, they received the imperial order and sought them out.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial order they hunted lost books empire-wide and sought out neglected talent.

sentences.zh: 其有籌策之可施于時，著述之可行於代者，較其才藝而考其學術，而申表之。

translations.literal: If there were stratagems applicable to the age or writings viable for the generation, they weighed talent and tested learning and submitted memorials recommending them.
translations.idiomatic: When policy proposals or writings suited the times, they assessed ability and scholarship and memorialized the throne with recommendations.

sentences.zh: 凡承旨撰集文章，校理經籍，月終則進課於內，歲終則考最於外。

translations.literal: Whenever they received orders to compile essays or collate classics, at month's end they submitted progress reports within the palace; at year's end their performance was evaluated outside.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned compilations and collations were reported monthly within the palace and graded annually in the outer administration.

sentences.zh: =史館=

translations.literal: = History Bureau =
translations.idiomatic: History Bureau

sentences.zh: 史館：歷代史官，隸秘書省著作局，皆著作郎掌修國史。

translations.literal: History Bureau: historians of successive dynasties, subordinate to the Compilation Bureau of the Archive, were all compilation officers who maintained the national history.
translations.idiomatic: The History Bureau: dynastic historians under the Archive's Compilation Bureau were compilation officers charged with the national chronicle.

sentences.zh: 武德因隋舊制。

translations.literal: Wude followed Sui's old system.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wude the Tang kept Sui practice.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年閏十二月，始移史館於禁中，在門下省北，宰相監修國史，自是著作郎始罷史職。

translations.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month of the third year of Zhenguan the History Bureau was first moved inside the forbidden palace north of the Chancellery; the chancellor supervised revision of the national history, and from this the compilation officer ceased historical duties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 3, intercalary twelfth month: the bureau moved inside the palace north of the Chancellery with the chancellor supervising the national history—whereupon compilation officers gave up direct historiography.

sentences.zh: 及大明宮初成，置史館于門下省之南。

translations.literal: When Daming Palace was first completed the History Bureau was placed south of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Daming Palace was finished the bureau was installed south of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 館門下東西有棗樹七十四株，無雜樹。

translations.literal: East and west of the bureau gate were seventy-four jujube trees without other species mixed in.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-four jujube trees stood east and west of the gate—no other trees among them.

sentences.zh: 開元二十五年三月，右相李林甫以中書地切樞密，記事者官宜附近，史官尹愔奏移史館於中書省北，以舊尚藥院充館也。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan Right Counselor Li Linfu, because the Secretariat adjoined vital secrets and recorders should be nearby, History Officer Yin Yin memorialized moving the History Bureau north of the Secretariat, using the old Imperial Pharmacy as the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 25, third month: Li Linfu argued that historians should sit near the Secretariat's secrets; Yin Yin moved the bureau north of the Secretariat into the former Imperial Pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 史官。

translations.literal: History officers.
translations.idiomatic: History officers.

sentences.zh: 古者天子諸侯，皆有史官，以紀言動、歷數之事。

translations.literal: In antiquity Son of Heaven and feudal lords all had history officers to record words and deeds and calendrical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient rulers and feudal lords kept historians to record speech, action, and the calendar.

sentences.zh: 到後漢明帝，如當時名士入東觀，撰《光武紀》，而史官因以他官兼之。

translations.literal: By Later Han Mingdi, noted men of the time entered the Eastern Pavilion to compile the Annals of Guangwu, and history officers were thereafter filled by other officials concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Han Ming, eminent scholars entered the Eastern Pavilion to write the Annals of Guangwu; thereafter historians were other officials serving in addition.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝始置著作郎，專掌國史，隸中書。

translations.literal: Wei Mingdi first established compilation officers exclusively in charge of national history, subordinate to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ming established dedicated compilation officers for the national history under the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 晉改隸秘書省，因而不改。

translations.literal: Jin changed subordination to the Archive and thereafter did not alter it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin transferred the office to the Archive and left the arrangement unchanged.

sentences.zh: 貞觀年修《五代史》，移史館於禁中。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era when the Five Dynasties History was revised, the History Bureau was moved inside the forbidden palace.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhenguan historians revised the Five Dynasties History, the bureau returned inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 史官無常員，如有修撰大事，則用他官兼之，事畢日停。

translations.literal: History officers had no fixed quota; when a major compilation arose other officials were assigned concurrently and ceased when the work ended.
translations.idiomatic: There was no standing corps of historians—major projects drew concurrent appointees who left when the work finished.

sentences.zh: 監修國史。

translations.literal: Supervisor of revision of national history.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 貞觀已後，多以宰相監修國史，遂成故事也。

translations.literal: After Zhenguan chancellors often supervised revision of the national history, and this became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenguan a chancellor usually supervised the national history—a fixed custom.

sentences.zh: 修撰直館。

translations.literal: Compiler and direct curator.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler and direct curator of the bureau.

sentences.zh: 天寶已後，他官兼領史職者，謂之史館修撰，初入為直館也。

translations.literal: After Tianbao other officials who concurrently held history duties were called History Bureau compilers; on first entry they were direct curators.
translations.idiomatic: Post-Tianbao concurrent historians were styled History Bureau compilers; newcomers began as direct curators.

sentences.zh: 元和六年，宰相裴垍奏：「登朝官領史職者，並為修撰，未登朝官入館者，並為直館。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe Chancellor Pei Ji memorialized: "Court officials holding history duties shall all be compilers; those entering the bureau who have not yet attended court shall all be direct curators.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe 6: Chancellor Pei Ji proposed that court-ranked historians be styled compilers and pre-court entrants direct curators.

sentences.zh: 修撰中以一人官高者判館事，其餘名目，並請不置。

translations.literal: Among compilers let the one highest in rank judge bureau affairs; all other titles, please do not establish them."
translations.idiomatic: "Among compilers the senior officer should adjudicate bureau business; abolish the other titles."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The throne approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 楷書手二十五人，典書四人，亭長二人，掌固六人，裝滿直一人，熟紙匠六人。

translations.literal: Twenty-five regular-script copyists, four book custodians, two hall chiefs, six watchmen, one binding clerk, six paper-cooking artisans.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included twenty-five copyists, four custodians, two hall chiefs, six guards, one binder, and six paper preparers.

sentences.zh: 史官掌修國史，不虛美，不隱惡，直書其事。

translations.literal: History officers maintain the national history, neither flattering falsely nor hiding wrong, writing events straight.
translations.idiomatic: Historians wrote the national chronicle without false praise or concealed fault—recording events plainly.

sentences.zh: 凡天地日月之祥，山川封域之分，昭穆繼代之序，禮樂師旅之事，誅賞廢興之政，皆本於起居注、時政記，以為實錄，然後立編年之體，為褒貶焉。

translations.literal: All omens of heaven, earth, sun, and moon, divisions of mountains and borders, order of ancestral succession, rites, music, and military affairs, policies of punishment, reward, abolition, and revival—all root in the Daily Records and Current Policy Records as true records, then take annalistic form for praise and blame.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly portents, geography, succession, ritual, music, armies, and the rise and fall of policies all drew on Daily Records and Current Policy Records as factual base before taking annalistic shape for moral judgment.

sentences.zh: 既終藏之於府。

translations.literal: When finished they were stored in the archive.
translations.idiomatic: Completed histories were deposited in the archive.

sentences.zh: =知匭使=

translations.literal: = Commissioner of the Petition Boxes =
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of the Petition Boxes

sentences.zh: 知匭使。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Petition Boxes.
translations.idiomatic: The petition-box commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天后垂拱二年，置匭以達冤滯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chuigong the Empress Wu established boxes to reach the stagnant and wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Chuigong 2: Empress Wu installed petition boxes to reach grievances trapped in the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 其制，一房四面，各以方色，東曰延恩，西曰申冤，南曰招諫，北曰通玄。

translations.literal: The design: one cabinet on four sides, each with its square color—east called Extending Grace, west Declaring Wrong, south Inviting Remonstrance, north Penetrating Mystery.
translations.idiomatic: Four-sided cabinets in directional colors: east Extending Grace, west Declaring Wrong, south Inviting Remonstrance, north Penetrating Mystery.

sentences.zh: 所以申天下之冤滯，達萬人之情狀。

translations.literal: Thus to declare wrongs throughout the empire and convey the conditions of the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: They gave voice to empire-wide injustice and the plight of common people.

sentences.zh: 蓋古善旌、誹謗木之意也。

translations.literal: It broadly follows the ancient meaning of the commendation banner and the slander wood.
translations.idiomatic: The idea echoed Han commendation banners and criticism posts.

sentences.zh: 天寶九年，改匭為獻納。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianbao the boxes were renamed Submission and Reception.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 9 renamed them Submission and Reception.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，復名曰匭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan the name boxes was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyuan 1 restored the name petition boxes.

sentences.zh: 垂拱已來，常以諫議大夫及補闕、拾遣一人充使，受納訴狀。

translations.literal: Since Chuigong remonstrance grandees and one rectifier or remonstrance collector usually filled the commissioner post and received complaint petitions.
translations.idiomatic: Since Chuigong a remonstrance official or rectifier typically served as commissioner and received petitions.

sentences.zh: 每日暮進內，而晨出之也。

translations.literal: Each evening they were forwarded inside; each morning they were taken out.
translations.idiomatic: Petitions went in each evening and came out each morning.

sentences.zh: =翰林院=

translations.literal: = Hanlin Academy =
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academy

sentences.zh: 翰林院。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 天子在大明宮，其院在右銀台門內。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven was at Daming Palace the academy was inside Right Yintai Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At Daming Palace the academy stood inside Right Yintai Gate.

sentences.zh: 在興慶宮，院在金明門內。

translations.literal: At Xingqing Palace the academy was inside Jinming Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingqing Palace it lay inside Jinming Gate.

sentences.zh: 若在西內，院在顯福門。

translations.literal: If at the Western Inner Palace the academy was at Xianfu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the western inner palace it was at Xianfu Gate.

sentences.zh: 若在東都、華清宮，皆有待詔之所。

translations.literal: If at the eastern capital or Huaqing Palace there were always places for awaiting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang and Huaqing Palace likewise maintained awaiting-edict quarters.

sentences.zh: 其待詔者，有詞學、經術、合煉、僧道、卜祝、術藝、書奕，各別院以稟之，日晚而退。

translations.literal: Those awaiting edicts included literary learning, classical studies, alchemy, monks and Daoists, diviners and prayers, arts and skills, calligraphy and chess—each in separate halls reporting upward, retiring at day's end.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting-edict scholars covered belles lettres, classics, alchemy, clergy, divination, arts, calligraphy, and chess—each group in its own hall, dismissed at nightfall.

sentences.zh: 其所重者詞學。

translations.literal: What was most valued was literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Literary talent weighed most heavily.

sentences.zh: 武德、貞觀時，有溫大雅、魏徵、李百藥、岑文本、許敬宗、褚遂良。

translations.literal: In Wude and Zhenguan there were Wen Daya, Wei Zheng, Li Baiyao, Cen Wenben, Xu Jingzong, and Chu Suiliang.
translations.idiomatic: Wude and Zhenguan drew Wen Daya, Wei Zheng, Li Baiyao, Cen Wenben, Xu Jingzong, and Chu Suiliang.

sentences.zh: 永徽後，有許敬宗、上官儀，皆召入禁中驅使，未有名目。

translations.literal: After Yonghui there were Xu Jingzong and Shangguan Yi, all summoned into the forbidden palace for service without formal titles.
translations.idiomatic: After Yonghui Xu Jingzong and Shangguan Yi served inside the palace without fixed designations.

sentences.zh: 乾封中，劉懿之劉禕之兄弟、周思茂、元萬頃、範履冰，皆以文詞召入待詔，常於北門候進止，時號北門學士。

translations.literal: In Qianfeng Liu Yizhi and Liu Yizhi, the brothers, Zhou Simao, Yuan Wanqing, and Fan Lübing were all summoned by literary skill to await edicts, often waiting at the north gate for orders, and were called North Gate academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianfeng Liu Yizhi and Liu Yizhi, Zhou Simao, Yuan Wanqing, and Fan Lübing awaited edicts at the north gate for lack of formal titles—the "North Gate academicians."

sentences.zh: 天后時，蘇味道、韋承慶，皆待詔禁中。

translations.literal: In the Empress Wu's time Su Weidao and Wei Chengqing both awaited edicts within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, Su Weidao and Wei Chengqing served as palace awaiting-edict scholars.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，上官昭容獨當書詔之任。

translations.literal: In Zhongzong's time Shangguan Zhaorong alone bore the duty of drafting imperial writings.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongzong, Shangguan Zhaorong alone drafted imperial prose.

sentences.zh: 睿宗時、薛稷、賈膺福、崔湜，又代其任。

translations.literal: In Ruizong's time Xue Ji, Jia Yingfu, and Cui Shi again replaced her in the duty.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong's reign saw Xue Ji, Jia Yingfu, and Cui Shi succeed her.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，張說，陸堅、張九齡、徐安貞、張垍等，召入禁中，謂之翰林待詔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne Zhang Yue, Lu Jian, Zhang Jiuling, Xu Anzhen, and Zhang Ya were summoned into the forbidden palace and called Hanlin awaiting-edict scholars.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanzong's accession Zhang Yue, Lu Jian, Zhang Jiuling, Xu Anzhen, and Zhang Ya entered the palace as Hanlin awaiting-edict scholars.

sentences.zh: 王者尊極，一日萬機，四方進奏、中外表疏批答，或詔從中出。

translations.literal: The king's supreme dignity—ten thousand affairs in a day; memorials from the four quarters and inner and outer memorials for rescript, or edicts issued from within.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's exalted station meant ten thousand matters daily—memorials from every direction, rescripts on inner and outer papers, edicts flowing from the inner court.

sentences.zh: 宸翰所揮，亦資其檢討，謂之視草，故嘗簡當代士人，以備顧問。

translations.literal: Imperial brushwork also relied on their examination and editing, called viewing the draft; therefore men of the age were selected to stand ready for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial drafts passed through their review—"viewing the grass"—so contemporary literati were chosen as counselors at hand.

sentences.zh: 至德已後，天下用兵，軍國多務，深謀密詔，皆從中出。

translations.literal: After Zhide the empire took up arms; military and state affairs multiplied; deep plans and secret edicts all issued from within.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhide warfare engulfed the realm; secret strategy and confidential edicts issued from the inner court alone.

sentences.zh: 尤擇名士，翰林學士得充選者，文士為榮。

translations.literal: Especially choosing famous scholars, those Hanlin academicians who gained selection—literati took it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Selection as Hanlin academician became the summit of literary honor.

sentences.zh: 亦如中書舍人例置學士六人，內擇年深德重者一人為承旨，所以獨承密命故也。

translations.literal: Also like the Secretariat drafter precedent six academicians were established; within them one of deepest years and heavy virtue was made bearer of the order, because he alone received secret commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Following secretariat drafters, six Hanlin posts were fixed; the senior and most respected became bearer of the order, sole recipient of confidential commissions.

sentences.zh: 德宗好文，尤難其選。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong loved literature and made selection especially difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong, a lover of letters, made admission fiercely selective.

sentences.zh: 貞元已後，為學士承旨者，多至宰相焉。

translations.literal: After Zhenyuan those who served as academician bearer of the order often rose to chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenyuan many bearers of the Hanlin order ascended to the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: =內教坊=

translations.literal: = Inner Music Office =
translations.idiomatic: Inner Music Office

sentences.zh: 內教坊。

translations.literal: Inner Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Music Office.

sentences.zh: 武德已來，置於禁中，以按習雅樂，以中官人充使。

translations.literal: Since Wude it was placed in the forbidden palace to rehearse elegant music, with eunuchs as commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wude it rehearsed court music inside the palace under eunuch directors.

sentences.zh: 則天改為雲韶府，神龍復為教坊。

translations.literal: Empress Wu changed it to Cloud Harmony Office; Shenlong restored the name Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu renamed it Cloud Harmony Office; Shenlong restored Music Office.

sentences.zh: =習藝館=

translations.literal: = Practice Arts Hall =
translations.idiomatic: Practice Arts Hall

sentences.zh: 習藝館。

translations.literal: Practice Arts Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Practice Arts Hall.

sentences.zh: 本名內文學館，選宮人有儒學者一人為學士，教習宮人。

translations.literal: Originally named Inner Literary Academy, one palace woman versed in Confucian learning was chosen as academician to teach palace women.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the Inner Literary Academy, it chose one literate palace woman as academician to instruct the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 則天改為習藝館，又改為翰林內教坊，以事在禁中故也。

translations.literal: Empress Wu changed it to Practice Arts Hall, then again to Hanlin Inner Music Office, because the work lay within the forbidden palace.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu renamed it Practice Arts Hall, then Hanlin Inner Music Office, reflecting its palace location.

sentences.zh: =秘書省=秘書省。

translations.literal: = Archive = Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Archive

sentences.zh: 隸中書之下。

translations.literal: Subordinate beneath the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: It stood under the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 漢代藏書之所，有延閣、廣內、石渠之藏。

translations.literal: Han dynasty places for storing books included the Extended Pavilion, Broad Inner, and Stone Channel collections.
translations.idiomatic: Han book repositories included Extended Pavilion, Broad Inner, and Stone Channel.

sentences.zh: 又御史中丞，在殿內，掌蘭台秘書圖籍。

translations.literal: Also the censor-in-chief, within the hall, managed Orchid Terrace secretariat books and registers.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief also kept Orchid Terrace archives within the palace.

sentences.zh: 後漢桓帝延熹二年，始置秘書監，屬太常寺，掌禁中圖書秘文，後併入中書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanxi of Later Han Emperor Huan first established the Director of the Archive, subordinate to the Grand Music Master, in charge of forbidden palace books and secret texts; later it was merged into the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han Yanxi 2: Emperor Huan created the Archive Director under the Grand Music Master for palace books and secret texts; later the office merged into the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至晉惠帝，別置秘書寺，掌中外二閣圖書。

translations.literal: By Jin Emperor Hui a separate Archive Office was established in charge of inner and outer two-pavilion books.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Emperor Hui split off an Archive Office for both inner and outer pavilion libraries.

sentences.zh: 梁武改寺為省。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang changed the office to a directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wudi converted the office into a directorate.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為蘭台，光宅改為麟台，神龍復為秘書省。

translations.literal: Longshuo changed it to Orchid Terrace, Guangzhai to Unicorn Terrace, Shenlong restored Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo renamed it Orchid Terrace, Guangzhai Unicorn Terrace, Shenlong the Archive again.

sentences.zh: 秘書監秘書監一員，從三品。

translations.literal: Director of the Archive: one post, third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Archive Director: one officer, third rank.

sentences.zh: 監之名，後漢桓帝置，魏、晉不改。

translations.literal: The title director: Later Han Emperor Huan established it; Wei and Jin did not change it.
translations.idiomatic: The directorship dated to Later Han Emperor Huan; Wei and Jin kept the title.

sentences.zh: 後周謂之外史下大夫。

translations.literal: Later Zhou called it Outer Historian Lower Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou styled it Outer Historian Lower Grandee.

sentences.zh: 隋復為秘書監，從第三品。

translations.literal: Sui restored Director of the Archive, third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sui restored the Archive Director at third rank.

sentences.zh: 煬帝改為秘書令，武德復為監。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang changed it to Archive Chief; Wude restored director.
translations.idiomatic: Yang of Sui renamed it Archive Chief; Wude restored Director.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為蘭台太史，天授改為麟台監，神龍復為秘書監也。

translations.literal: Longshuo changed it to Orchid Terrace Grand Astrologer, Tianshou to Unicorn Terrace Director, Shenlong restored Director of the Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo made it Orchid Terrace Grand Astrologer, Tianshou Unicorn Terrace Director, Shenlong Archive Director again.

sentences.zh: 少監二員，從四品上。

translations.literal: Two vice directors, upper fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two vice directors, upper fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 少監，隋煬帝置。

translations.literal: Vice director: Sui Emperor Yang established it.
translations.idiomatic: The vice directorship began under Sui Yang.

sentences.zh: 龍朔改為蘭台侍郎，天授為麟台少監，神龍復為秘書少監。

translations.literal: Longshuo changed it to Orchid Terrace Vice Director, Tian shou to Unicorn Terrace Vice Director, Shenlong restored Archive Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo: Orchid Terrace Vice Director; Tian shou: Unicorn Vice Director; Shenlong: Archive Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 比置一員，太極初增置一員也。

translations.literal: Compared with one post established, at the beginning of Taichi one more was added.
translations.idiomatic: Originally one post; Taichi added a second.

sentences.zh: 丞一員。

translations.literal: One aide.
translations.idiomatic: One aide.

sentences.zh: 從五品上。

translations.literal: Upper fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Upper fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝置，丞二人。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Wu established it; two aides.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wu created the post with two aides.

sentences.zh: 隋置一人，正第五品也。

translations.literal: Sui established one person, proper fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sui fixed one aide at proper fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 秘書監之職，掌邦國經籍圖書之事。

translations.literal: The duty of the Archive Director was to manage the realm's classics, books, and registers.
translations.idiomatic: The Archive Director oversaw the empire's texts, libraries, and catalogues.

sentences.zh: 有二局：一曰著作，二曰太史，皆率其屬而修其職。

translations.literal: There were two bureaus: first Compilation, second Grand Astrologer—each leading subordinates in performing duties.
translations.idiomatic: Two bureaus served under him—Compilation and Grand Astrologer—each commanding its staff.

sentences.zh: 少監為之貳，丞掌判省事。

translations.literal: The vice director served as second; the aide managed and decided bureau business.
translations.idiomatic: The vice director was deputy; the aide adjudicated daily business.

sentences.zh: 秘書郎秘書郎四員。

translations.literal: Archive Secretaries: four posts.
translations.idiomatic: Archive Secretaries: four posts.

sentences.zh: 從六品上。

translations.literal: Upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 校書郎八人，正九品上。

translations.literal: Eight collation officers, upper ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Eight collation officers, upper ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 正字四人，正九品下。

translations.literal: Four proofreaders, lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Four proofreaders, lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 主事一人，從九品上。

translations.literal: One principal clerk, upper ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: One principal clerk, upper ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 令史四人，書令史九人，典書八人，楷書手八十人，亭長六人。

translations.literal: Four clerks, nine document clerks, eight book custodians, eighty regular-script copyists, six hall chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Four clerks, nine document clerks, eight custodians, eighty copyists, six hall chiefs.

sentences.zh: 掌固八人。

translations.literal: Eight watchmen.
translations.idiomatic: Eight watchmen.

sentences.zh: 秘書郎掌甲乙丙丁四部之圖籍，謂之四庫。

translations.literal: Archive secretaries managed books of divisions A, B, C, and D—called the four repositories.
translations.idiomatic: Archive secretaries oversaw the A, B, C, and D divisions—the four repositories.

sentences.zh: 經庫類十，史庫類十三，子庫類十四，集庫類三。

translations.literal: Classics repository ten categories, history thirteen, masters fourteen, belles lettres three.
translations.idiomatic: The classics held ten categories, history thirteen, masters fourteen, collected writings three.

sentences.zh: 事在《經籍志》。

translations.literal: The details are in the Bibliographic Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Particulars appear in the Bibliographic Treatise.

sentences.zh: =著作局=

translations.literal: = Compilation Bureau =
translations.idiomatic: Compilation Bureau

sentences.zh: 著作局：龍朔為司文局。

translations.literal: Compilation Bureau: Longshuo was Documents Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Compilation Bureau: under Longshuo, the Documents Bureau.

sentences.zh: 著作郎二人，從五品上。

translations.literal: Two compilation officers, upper fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two compilation officers, upper fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 龍朔為司文郎中，咸亨復也。

translations.literal: Longshuo was Documents Bureau Director; Xianheng restored the old title.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo styled them Documents Bureau directors; Xianheng restored compilation officer.

sentences.zh: 佐郎四人，從六品上。

translations.literal: Four assistant officers, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Four assistant officers, upper sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 校書郎二人，正九品上。

translations.literal: Two collation officers, upper ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two collation officers, upper ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 正字二人，正九品下。

translations.literal: Two proofreaders, lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two proofreaders, lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 楷書手五人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Five regular-script copyists, four watchmen.
translations.idiomatic: Five copyists, four watchmen.

sentences.zh: 著作郎、佐郎掌修撰碑誌、祝文、祭文，與佐郎分判局事也。

translations.literal: Compilation officers and assistant officers managed drafting stele inscriptions, prayer texts, and sacrificial texts, and with assistant officers divided bureau business.
translations.idiomatic: Compilation and assistant officers drafted steles, prayers, and sacrificial texts and split bureau duties among themselves.

sentences.zh: =司天臺=

translations.literal: = Directorate of Astronomy =
translations.idiomatic: Directorate of Astronomy

sentences.zh: 司天臺：舊太史局，隸秘書監。

translations.literal: Directorate of Astronomy: formerly the Grand Astrologer Bureau, subordinate to the Archive Director.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate of Astronomy: formerly the Grand Astrologer Bureau under the Archive Director.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年改為秘閣局，久視元年改為渾儀監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo it became Secret Repository Bureau; in the first year of Jiushi it became Armillary Sphere Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Longshuo 2 renamed it Secret Repository Bureau; Jiushi 1 the Armillary Sphere Directorate.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年改為太史監，復為太史局，隸秘書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun it became Grand Astrologer Directorate, again Grand Astrologer Bureau, subordinate to the Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyun 1 made it Grand Astrologer Directorate, then again Grand Astrologer Bureau under the Archive.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年三月十九日敕，改太史監為司天臺，改置官屬，舊置於子城內秘書省西，今在永甯坊東南角也。

translations.literal: Edict of the nineteenth day of the third month of the first year of Qianyuan changed Grand Astrologer Directorate to Directorate of Astronomy and reestablished officials; formerly placed inside the inner city west of the Archive, now at the southeast corner of Yongning Ward.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyuan 1, third month, day 19: Grand Astrologer Directorate became Directorate of Astronomy with new staff; it moved from west of the Archive inside the inner city to Yongning Ward's southeast corner.

sentences.zh: 監一人，從三品。

translations.literal: One director, third rank.
translations.idiomatic: One director, third rank.

sentences.zh: 本太史局令，從五品下。

translations.literal: Originally Grand Astrologer Bureau chief, lower fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the bureau chief at lower fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年改為監，升從三品，一如殿中秘書品秩也。

translations.literal: Qianyuan first year changed to director, raised to third rank, the same grade as Palace Administration and Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyuan 1 elevated the chief to director at third rank, matching Palace Administration and Archive.

sentences.zh: 少監二人。

translations.literal: Two vice directors.
translations.idiomatic: Two vice directors.

sentences.zh: 本曰太史丞，從七品下。

translations.literal: Originally called Grand Astrologer aides, lower seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Grand Astrologer aides, lower seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 乾元升為少監，與諸司少監卿同品也。

translations.literal: Qianyuan raised them to vice directors, same grade as vice directors of other offices.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyuan promoted them to vice directors equal to other agencies.

sentences.zh: 太史令掌觀察天文，稽定歷數。

translations.literal: The Grand Astrologer Chief observes heaven and verifies the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The chief observed the sky and fixed the calendar.

sentences.zh: 凡日月星辰之變，風雲氣色之異，率其屬而占候之。

translations.literal: All changes of sun, moon, and stars and anomalies of wind, clouds, and color—leading subordinates he observed and prognosticated.
translations.idiomatic: He led staff in watching solar, lunar, and stellar changes and anomalies of wind, cloud, and sky color.

sentences.zh: 其屬有司曆二人，掌造曆。

translations.literal: Subordinates included two calendar officers in charge of making the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Two calendar officers made the almanac.

sentences.zh: 保章正一人，掌教。

translations.literal: One Chart-Registrar Chief chief in charge of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: One Keeper of the Bureau Seal supervised training.

sentences.zh: 曆生四十一人。

translations.literal: Forty-one calendar students.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-one calendar students.

sentences.zh: 監候五人，掌候天文。

translations.literal: Five observer-inspectors in charge of observing heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Five observer-inspectors watched the sky.

sentences.zh: 觀生九十人，掌晝夜司候天文氣色。

translations.literal: Ninety observation students in charge of day and night observation of celestial color.
translations.idiomatic: Ninety observation students tracked heaven day and night.

sentences.zh: 靈台郎二人，掌教習天文氣色。

translations.literal: Two Spirit Platform officers in charge of teaching celestial color.
translations.idiomatic: Two Spirit Platform officers taught sky observation.

sentences.zh: 天文生六十人。

translations.literal: Sixty astronomy students.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty astronomy students.

sentences.zh: 挈壺正二人。

translations.literal: Two clepsydra chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Two clepsydra chiefs.

sentences.zh: 掌知漏刻。

translations.literal: In charge of knowing the water clock and graduations.
translations.idiomatic: They managed the water clock and its graduations.

sentences.zh: 司辰七十人，漏刻典事二十二人，漏刻博士九人，漏刻生三百六十人，典鐘一百一十二人，典鼓八十八人，楷書手二人，亭長、掌固各四人。

translations.literal: Seventy timekeepers, twenty-two clepsydra clerks, nine clepsydra doctors, three hundred sixty clepsydra students, one hundred twelve bell custodians, eighty-eight drum custodians, two regular-script copyists, four hall chiefs and watchmen each.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included seventy timekeepers, twenty-two clepsydra clerks, nine doctors, three hundred sixty students, one hundred twelve bell keepers, eighty-eight drum keepers, two copyists, and four hall chiefs and watchmen each.

sentences.zh: 自乾元元年別置司天臺。

translations.literal: From Qianyuan first year the Directorate of Astronomy was separately established.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyuan 1 split off the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 改置官吏，不同太史局舊數，今據司天職掌書之也。

translations.literal: Reestablished officials differed from old Grand Astrologer Bureau numbers; now recorded according to the directorate's duties.
translations.idiomatic: New staffing diverged from the old bureau; the following follows directorate responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 凡玄象器物、天文圖書，苟非其任，不得預焉。

translations.literal: All celestial instruments and astronomical books—if not one's duty one may not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial instruments and astronomical texts were off limits except to assigned personnel.

sentences.zh: 每季錄所見災祥，送門下中書省，入起居注。

translations.literal: Each season recorded observed omens and sent them to the Chancellery and Secretariat for entry in the Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: Each quarter they logged portents to the Chancellery and Secretariat for the Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 歲終總錄，封送史館。

translations.literal: At year's end they compiled the total record and sealed it to the History Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Year-end summaries were sealed and sent to the History Bureau.

sentences.zh: 每年預造來年曆，頒於天下。

translations.literal: Each year they prepared the next year's calendar in advance and distributed it throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: They issued the coming year's calendar empire-wide every year.

sentences.zh: 五官正五員，正五品。

translations.literal: Five Bureau Chiefs of the Five Offices, fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Five chiefs of the five seasonal offices, fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年置五官，有春、夏、秋、冬、中五官之名。

translations.literal: Qianyuan first year established the Five Offices with names Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter, and Central Five Office Chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyuan 1 created Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter, and Central office chiefs.

sentences.zh: 丞二員，正七品。

translations.literal: Two aides, seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two aides, seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 主簿二員，正七品。

translations.literal: Two registrars, seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two registrars, seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 定額直五人，五官靈台郎五員，正七品。

translations.literal: Five fixed quota clerks, five Spirit Platform officers of the Five Offices, seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Five quota clerks and five Spirit Platform officers of the Five Offices, seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 舊靈台郎，正八品下，掌觀天文之變而占候之。

translations.literal: Former Spirit Platform officers, lower eighth rank, observed changes of heaven and prognosticated.
translations.idiomatic: Former Spirit Platform officers, lower eighth rank, watched celestial change and divined meaning.

sentences.zh: 凡二十八宿，分為十二次，事具《天文志》也。

translations.literal: All twenty-eight lodges divided into twelve stations—the details are in the Astronomical Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-eight lodges fell into twelve celestial stations, detailed in the Astronomical Treatise.

sentences.zh: 五官保章正五員，正七品。

translations.literal: Five Keepers of the Seal of the Five Offices, seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Five Chart-Registrar Chiefs for the Five Offices, seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 五官司曆五員，正八品。

translations.literal: Five Calendar Officers of the Five Offices, eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Five calendar officers of the Five Offices, eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 舊司曆二人，從九品上，掌國之曆法，造曆以頒四方。

translations.literal: Formerly two calendar officers, upper ninth rank, in charge of the realm's calendar method, making the calendar to distribute to the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly two calendar officers, upper ninth rank, maintained state calendrics and issued almanacs to the regions.

sentences.zh: 其曆有《戊寅曆》、《麟德曆》、《神龍曆》、《大衍曆》。

translations.literal: Its calendars included Wuyin Calendar, Linde Calendar, Shenlong Calendar, and Dayan Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Calendars in use included Wuyin, Linde, Shenlong, and Dayan.

sentences.zh: 天下之測量之處，分至表准，其詳可載，故參考星度，稽驗晷影，各有典章。

translations.literal: Places of measurement throughout the empire, solstice and equinox gauge standards—the details can be recorded; therefore consulting star degrees and verifying gnomon shadows each had statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Empire-wide observatories with solstice and equinox standards had codified methods for checking star positions and sundial shadows.

sentences.zh: 五官監候五員，正八品。

translations.literal: Five Observer-Inspectors of the Five Offices, eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Five observer-inspectors of the Five Offices, eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 五官挈壺正五員，正九品。

translations.literal: Five Clepsydra Chiefs of the Five Offices, ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Five clepsydra chiefs of the Five Offices, ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 五官司辰十五員。

translations.literal: Fifteen Timekeepers of the Five Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen timekeepers of the Five Offices.

sentences.zh: 正九品。

translations.literal: Ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 舊挈壺正二員，從八品下。

translations.literal: Formerly two clepsydra chiefs, lower eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly two clepsydra chiefs, lower eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 司辰十七人，正九品下。

translations.literal: Seventeen timekeepers, lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen timekeepers, lower ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 皆掌知漏刻。

translations.literal: All in charge of knowing the water clock graduations.
translations.idiomatic: All managed clepsydra graduations.

sentences.zh: 孔壺為漏，浮箭為刻，以告中星昏明之候也。

translations.literal: Bronze vessel as leak, floating arrow as graduation, to announce the markers of midnight stars and dawn and dusk.
translations.idiomatic: A bronze jar leaked water; floating arrows marked graduations to signal midnight stars and the moments of dawn and dusk.

sentences.zh: 五官禮生十五人，五官楷書手五人，令史五人，漏刻博士二十人，漏刻之法，孔壺為漏，浮箭為刻。

translations.literal: Fifteen ritual attendants of the Five Offices, five regular-script copyists of the Five Offices, five clerks, twenty clepsydra doctors—the method of clepsydra graduations: bronze vessel as leak, floating arrow as graduation.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen ritual attendants, five copyists, five clerks, and twenty clepsydra doctors of the Five Offices—all using jar-and-arrow timing.

sentences.zh: 其箭四十有八，晝夜共百刻。

translations.literal: Its arrows forty-eight in number; day and night together one hundred graduations.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-eight arrows marked one hundred day-and-night graduations.

sentences.zh: 冬夏之間，有長短。

translations.literal: Between winter and summer there were long and short periods.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night lengths shifted between winter and summer.

sentences.zh: 冬至之日，晝漏四十刻，夜漏六十刻。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice day-graduations forty, night sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice: forty day-graduations, sixty at night.

sentences.zh: 夏至，晝漏六十刻夜漏四十刻。

translations.literal: Summer solstice: day sixty, night forty.
translations.idiomatic: Summer solstice: sixty by day, forty by night.

sentences.zh: 春分秋分之時，晝夜各五十刻。

translations.literal: At spring and autumn equinox day and night each fifty graduations.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and autumn equinoxes split day and night evenly at fifty graduations each.

sentences.zh: 秋分之後，減晝益夜，凡九日加一刻。

translations.literal: After the autumn equinox reduce day and increase night; every nine days add one graduation.
translations.idiomatic: After autumn equinox days shortened and nights lengthened—one graduation added every nine days.

sentences.zh: 春分已後，減夜益晝，九日減一刻。

translations.literal: After spring equinox reduce night and increase day; every nine days reduce one graduation.
translations.idiomatic: After spring equinox nights shortened and days lengthened—one graduation removed every nine days.

sentences.zh: 二至前後，加減遲，用日多。

translations.literal: Before and after the two solstices increase and decrease slowly, using more days.
translations.idiomatic: Near the solstices adjustment slowed and required more days.

sentences.zh: 二分之間，加減速，用日少。

translations.literal: Between the two equinoxes increase and decrease quickly, using fewer days.
translations.idiomatic: Between equinoxes adjustment was faster over fewer days.

sentences.zh: 候夜以為更點之節。

translations.literal: Night-watching served as the measure for night watches and bell strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Night observation set the rhythm for watches and bell strokes.

sentences.zh: 每夜分為五更，每更分為五點。

translations.literal: Each night divided into five watches; each watch divided into five strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Each night had five watches; each watch five strokes.

sentences.zh: 更以擊鼓為節，點以擊鐘為節也。

translations.literal: Watches took drumbeats as measure; strokes took bellbeats as measure.
translations.idiomatic: Drums marked watches; bells marked strokes.

sentences.zh: 典鐘、典鼓三百五十人，天文觀生九十人，天文生五十人，曆生五十五人，漏生四十人，視品十人。

translations.literal: Bell and drum custodians three hundred fifty persons, astronomy observation students ninety, astronomy students fifty, calendar students fifty-five, clepsydra students forty, tenth-rank viewers ten.
translations.idiomatic: Staff totaled three hundred fifty bell and drum keepers, ninety observation students, fifty astronomy students, fifty-five calendar students, forty clepsydra students, and ten tenth-rank viewers.

sentences.zh: 已上官吏，皆乾元元年隨監司新置也。

translations.literal: The above officials were all newly established with the directorate in Qianyuan first year.
translations.idiomatic: All listed posts were created with the Qianyuan 1 reorganization of the directorate.
